items.ma-2310: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us – ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said: And I myself heard it from Ibn Abī Shaybah –, he said: Ibn Mubārak narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the man of Aslam: “Perhaps you kissed, or touched, or looked.”
items.ma-2311: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us – and I myself heard it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad =, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to set out on a journey, he would say: “O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor over the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the burden of the journey, and from the gloom of the return. O Allah, fold up the earth for us, and make the journey easy for us.” And when he wished to return, he would say: “Returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Rabb.” And when he entered upon his family, he would say: “Repentance, repentance, to our Rabb a return; it leaves no sin upon us.”
items.ma-2312: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There will surely be peoples from my ummah who recite the Qurʾān, [yet] they pass through Islam as the arrow passes through the game.”
items.ma-2313: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not go out to meet [them], and do not tie up [the udders], and let not some of you inflate [prices] for others.”
items.ma-2314:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – ʿAbd Allāh said: And I heard it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad –, he said: ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ affirmed Umayyah as truthful in something of his poetry, and he said:
A man and a bull beneath his right foot … and the eagle for the other, and a lion lying in wait.
The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has spoken truly.” And he said:
And the sun rises at the end of every night … red, its color turning rose-like by morning.
It refuses, and it does not rise for us at its leisure … except tormented, and unless it is lashed.
The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has spoken truly.”
items.ma-2315: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad –, ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no wuḍūʾ upon one who sleeps while prostrating, until he lies on his side; for when he lies on his side, his joints relax.”
items.ma-2316: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man took a woman, or took her captive, and she struggled with him over the hilt of his sword, so he killed her. The Prophet ﷺ passed by her and was informed of her affair, so he forbade the killing of women.
items.ma-2317: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [a force] to Muʾtah, and appointed Zayd [over it]: if Zayd were killed, then Jaʿfar; and if Jaʿfar were killed, then Ibn Rawāḥah. Ibn Rawāḥah stayed behind, and attended the Jumuʿah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who saw him and said: “What kept you behind?” He said: I am attending the Jumuʿah with you. He said: “A morning journey or an evening journey is better than the world and what is in it.”
items.ma-2318: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is not of us who has intercourse with a pregnant woman.”
items.ma-2319: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: On the day of the Trench a man of the polytheists was struck down, and they asked the Prophet ﷺ that they might cover him [in burial]. He said: “No, and there is no honor for you.” They said: Then we will give you a payment for that. He said: “And that is more vile, and more vile.”
items.ma-2320: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in a single garment, wrapped in it, guarding with its excess against the heat of the ground and its cold.
items.ma-2321: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Abū Jahl passed by and said: Did I not forbid you? The Prophet ﷺ rebuked him, and Abū Jahl said to him: Why do you rebuke me, O Muḥammad? By Allah, you know that there is no man in it with a larger assembly than mine. He said: Then Jibrīl ﵇ said: {Then let him call his assembly} [al-ʿAlaq: 17]. He said: Then Ibn ʿAbbās said: By Allah, had he called his assembly, the Zabāniyah of punishment would have seized him.
items.ma-2322: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to give the khuṭbah on the day of Jumuʿah standing, then sit, then stand and give the khuṭbah.
items.ma-2323: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad –, Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is not one of you but that his companion from among the Shayāṭīn has been assigned to him.” They said: And you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Yes, but Allah helped me against him, so he submitted.”
items.ma-2324:
ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Jarīr narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, he said: On the night the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was taken on the night journey, he entered Paradise and heard from one side of it a faint sound. He said: “O Jibrīl, what is this?” He said: This is Bilāl the muʾadhdhin. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said, when he came to the people: “Bilāl has succeeded; I saw for him such and such.” He said: Then Mūsā ﷺ met him and welcomed him, and said: Welcome to the unlettered Prophet. He said: “And he was a tawny man, tall, his hair straight, level with his ears or above them.” He said: “Who is this, O Jibrīl?” He said: This is Mūsā ﵇. He said: Then he went on, and ʿĪsā met him and welcomed him, and he said: “Who is this, O Jibrīl?” He said: This is ʿĪsā. He said: Then he went on, and a venerable, awe-inspiring old man met him, and welcomed him and greeted him with salām – and all of them would greet him with salām –; he said: “Who is this, O Jibrīl?” He said: This is your father Ibrāhīm. He said: Then he looked into the Fire, and there was a people eating carrion. He said: “Who are these, O Jibrīl?” He said: These are those who eat the flesh of people. And he saw a man, red, blue, curly-haired, dishevelled, when you see him. He said: “Who is this, O Jibrīl?” He said: This is the hamstringer of the she-camel.
He said: When the Prophet ﷺ entered al-Masjid al-Aqṣā, he stood to pray, then turned, and behold, all the Prophets were praying with him. When he finished, two cups were brought, one on the right and the other on the left; in one of them was milk and in the other honey. He took the milk and drank from it, and the one who had the cup with him said: You have attained the fiṭrah.
items.ma-2325: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I stood with the Prophet ﷺ in the prayer at his left, so he made me stand at his right.
items.ma-2326: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sumayʿ al-Zayyāt, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of that.
items.ma-2327: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I am your forerunner at the Ḥawḍ; whoever comes to it has succeeded. And peoples will be brought, and they will be taken to the left side, and I will say: O my Rabb. Then it will be said: They did not cease, after you, turning back on their heels.”
items.ma-2328: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take good omens and not take bad omens, and a good name pleased him.
items.ma-2329: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad –, Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, raising it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “He is not of us who does not respect the elder, and show mercy to the young, and enjoin the good, and forbid the wrong.”
items.ma-2330: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from, with the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Five, all of them wrongdoers, that one in iḥrām may kill, and that are killed in the Ḥaram: the mouse, the scorpion, the snake, the biting dog, and the crow.”
items.ma-2332: ʿUthmān narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish a sunnah in anything but that I knew it, except for three: I do not know whether he used to recite in the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr or not; and I do not know how he used to recite: {and I have reached, of old age, ʿutiyyā} or {ʿusiyyā}. Ḥuṣayn said: And I forgot the third. ʿAbd Allāh said: I myself heard all of it from ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad.
items.ma-2333: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us – and I myself heard it from him –, Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ to make al-Ṣafā gold for them, and to remove the mountains from them so that they could sow. So it was said to him: If you wish, give them respite; and if you wish, we shall give them what they asked, but if they disbelieve they will be destroyed, as I destroyed those before them. He said: “No, rather I give them respite.” So Allah ﷿ revealed this verse: {And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier ones denied them; and We gave Thamūd the she-camel, clearly visible} [al-Isrāʾ: 59].
items.ma-2334: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The name of Juwayriyah was Barrah, and the Prophet ﷺ seemingly disliked that, so he named her Juwayriyah, disliking that it be said: He went out from Barrah. He said: And he went out after he had prayed, then came to her, and she said: I have not ceased, after you, O Messenger of Allah, to be constant [in remembrance]. He said: So he said to her: “I said after you words which, if they were weighed, would outweigh what you said: Glory be to Allah by the number of what He created; Glory be to Allah, Riḍāʾa Nafsih; Glory be to Allah, the weight of His ʿArsh; Glory be to Allah, the ink of His words.”
items.ma-2335: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fast on seeing it, and break the fast on seeing it; and if a cloud comes between you and it, complete the number; and the month is twenty-nine,” meaning that it can be deficient.
items.ma-2336: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother has died and she owed the fast of a month; shall I make it up on her behalf? He said: “If your mother had owed a debt, would you have paid it on her behalf?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then the debt of Allah is more deserving to be paid.” Sulaymān said: Al-Ḥakam and Salamah ibn Kuhayl said, while we were all sitting when Muslim narrated this ḥadīth, both said: We heard Mujāhid mention this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-2337: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Wuhayb informed me, Ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped and gave the cupper his wage, and took nasal medicine.
items.ma-2338: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Wuhayb informed us, Ibn Ṭāwūs informed us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about slaughtering, throwing [the pebbles], shaving, putting forward and putting back, and he said: “There is no harm.”
items.ma-2339: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Khaffāf narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr informed us, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: A roasted shoulder was brought to him, and he ate morsels from it, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ because of that.
items.ma-2340: Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, that he heard his father narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Health and free time are two blessings from the blessings of Allah, in which many of the people are cheated.”
items.ma-2341: ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – narrated to us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, that he narrated to him; that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat from a shoulder or a foreleg, then stand and pray, and he did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2342: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them this supplication, as he taught them a sūrah of the Qurʾān: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Jahannam, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of the Masīḥ al-Dajjāl, and I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of life and death.”
items.ma-2343: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it, except that he said: “from the fitnah of the Masīḥ al-Dajjāl.”
items.ma-2344: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: Hishām informed us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm al-Ḥalīm; there is no deity except Allah, You are Rabb of the Mighty ʿArsh; there is no deity except You, Rabb of the heavens and Rabb of the earth, and Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh.”
items.ma-2345: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it, meaning the like of the supplication of distress.
items.ma-2346: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Zāʾidah ibn Abī al-Ruqād, from Ziyād al-Numayrī, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: When Rajab began, the Prophet ﷺ would say: “O Allah, bless us in Rajab and Shaʿbān, and bless us in Ramaḍān.” And he used to say: “The night of Jumuʿah is bright, and its day is radiant.”
items.ma-2347: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī: The cousin of your Prophet – meaning Ibn ʿAbbās – narrated to us, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “On the night I was taken by night, I saw Mūsā ibn ʿImrān ﵇, a tawny man, tall, curly-haired, as though he were of the men of Shanūʾah; and I saw ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﵇, of medium build, in redness and whiteness, with straight hair.”
items.ma-2348:
ʿAbīdah ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: “Make it an ʿumrah; for if I had faced in my affair what I turned my back on, I would have commanded you with it; and let him who has no hady with him leave iḥrām.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a hady with him.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ʿumrah has entered into the Ḥajj until the Day of Resurrection,” and he interlaced between his fingers.
items.ma-2349: ʿAbīdah ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a journey, and he halted for the night, and slept, and did not wake except at sunrise. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Bilāl, and he called the adhān, and he prayed two rakʿahs. He said: Then Ibn ʿAbbās said: The world and what is in it would not please me in exchange for it – meaning the concession.
items.ma-2350: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās ﵄, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from al-Madīnah intending Makkah, and he fasted until he reached ʿUsfān. He said: Then he called for a vessel and placed it on his hand, until the people looked at it, then he broke his fast. He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: Whoever wishes fasts, and whoever wishes breaks the fast.
items.ma-2351: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Manṣūr … and he mentioned it with its isnād and its meaning.
items.ma-2352: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, Qābūs narrated to me, from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came to them hurrying – he said: until he alarmed us by his haste. When he reached us, he said: “I came hurrying to inform you of Laylat al-Qadr, but I was made to forget it between me and you; so seek it in the last ten of Ramaḍān.”
items.ma-2353: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the conquest of Makkah: “Indeed this land is ḥarām; Allah made it ḥarām on the day He created the heavens and the earth. So it is ḥarām – Allah made it ḥarām until the Day of Resurrection. Killing in it was not made lawful for anyone but me, and it is not lawful for anyone after me until the Hour is established; and it was not made lawful for me except for an hour of the day. So it is ḥarām – Allah ﷿ made it ḥarām until the Hour is established. Its thorns are not to be cut down, its fresh grass is not to be uprooted, its game is not to be scared away, and its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who will announce it.” He said: Al-ʿAbbās – and he was of the people of the land and knew what they could not do without – said: Except the idhkhir, O Messenger of Allah, for they cannot do without it; indeed it is for the graves and the houses. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Except the idhkhir.”
items.ma-2354: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, he said: Wāqid Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Khayyāṭ narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Ghee, dried curd and a lizard were given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ate the ghee and the dried curd, then said of the lizard: “This is something I have never eaten; so whoever wishes to eat it, let him eat it.” He said: So it was eaten at his table.
items.ma-2355: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī narrated to us, Hishām – meaning Ibn Ḥassān – narrated to us, ʿIkrimah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped on his head while in iḥrām, because of a headache he had, or something he had, at a water called Laḥy Jamal.
items.ma-2356: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Hishām ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The mukātab is paid blood-money in proportion to what he has paid off, the blood-money of a free man, and in proportion to what remains of his bondage, the blood-money of a slave.”
items.ma-2357:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the people gathered to wash the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was no one in the house except his family: his uncle al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, Quthama ibn al-ʿAbbās, Usāmah ibn Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, and Ṣāliḥ his mawlā; when they had gathered for the washing, Aws ibn Khawliyy al-Anṣārī, then of Banū ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, who was a participant of Badr, called from behind the door to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said to him: O ʿAlī, I adjure you by Allah, [remember] our share in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: ʿAlī said to him: Enter. So he entered and was present at the washing of the Messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ, and he did not take part in any of his washing. He said: Then [ʿAlī] propped him against his chest, with his shirt on him, and al-ʿAbbās, al-Faḍl and Quthama were turning him over with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and Usāmah ibn Zayd and Ṣāliḥ, their mawlā, were pouring the water; and ʿAlī went on washing him, and nothing of what is seen of the dead was seen of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was saying: My father and my mother [be your ransom], how good you are, living and dead!
Until, when they had finished washing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – and he was washed with water and lote-leaf – they dried him, then was done to him what is done to the dead, then he was wrapped in three garments: two white garments and a cloak of ḥibarah.
Then al-ʿAbbās called two men and said: Let one of you go to Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ – Abū ʿUbaydah used to dig a ḍarīḥ for the people of Makkah – and let the other go to Abū Ṭalḥah ibn Sahl al-Anṣārī – Abū Ṭalḥah used to dig a laḥd for the people of al-Madīnah. He said: Then al-ʿAbbās said to them when he sent them off: O Allah, choose [what is best] for Your Messenger. He said: So they went, and the companion of Abū ʿUbaydah did not find Abū ʿUbaydah, and the companion of Abū Ṭalḥah found Abū Ṭalḥah and brought him, and he dug a laḥd for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2358: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Khuṣayf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jazarī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: I said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, how astonishing is the disagreement of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the ihlāl of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he made it obligatory! He said: I am the most knowledgeable of the people about that. It was only one Ḥajj from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and from that they disagreed: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out intending Ḥajj, and when he had prayed his two rakʿahs in his mosque at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he made it obligatory in his sitting place, and he made ihlāl for the Ḥajj when he had finished his two rakʿahs. Some people heard that from him and memorised it from him. Then he mounted, and when his she-camel rose with him, he made ihlāl, and some people caught that from him – for the people used to come in separate groups – so they heard him making ihlāl when his she-camel rose with him, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only made ihlāl when his she-camel rose with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on, and when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ he made ihlāl, and some people caught that from him, and they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only made ihlāl when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ. By Allah, he made it obligatory in his place of prayer, and he made ihlāl when his she-camel rose with him, and he made ihlāl when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ. So whoever takes the statement of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, let him make ihlāl in his place of prayer when he has finished his two rakʿahs.
items.ma-2359: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: A man narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid ibn Jabr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered as hady in the Farewell Ḥajj a hundred camels; he slaughtered thirty of them with his own hand, then commanded ʿAlī, and he slaughtered what remained of them, and he said: “Distribute their meat, their covers and their hides among the people, and do not give any of it to a butcher; and take for us from each camel a portion of meat, then put them in one pot, so that we may eat of their meat and sip of their broth.” So he did so.
items.ma-2360: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Kurayb, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I said to him: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, what of your saying: No man performs Ḥajj who has not driven the hady with him, then performs ṭawāf of the House, except that he is released through an ʿumrah; and no pilgrim who has driven the hady with him performs ṭawāf with it, except that an ʿumrah and a Ḥajj are combined for him; and the people do not say this. He said: Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and those with him of his Companions mentioned only the Ḥajj; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded whoever did not have the hady with him to perform ṭawāf of the House and be released through an ʿumrah. Then a man among them began to say: O Messenger of Allah, it is only the Ḥajj. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say: “It is not the Ḥajj, but it is an ʿumrah.”
items.ma-2361: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not have ʿĀʾishah perform ʿumrah on the night of al-Ḥaṣbah except to cut off a matter of the people of polytheism; for they used to say: When the sore has healed, and the trace has faded, and Ṣafar has entered, then ʿumrah has become lawful for whoever performs ʿumrah.
items.ma-2362: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to me, from Mujāhid ibn Jabr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had offered as hady the camel of Abū Jahl, which he had seized on the day of Badr, with a silver ring in its head, in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, among his hady. And he said in another place: to enrage the polytheists by that.
items.ma-2363: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Bushayr ibn Yasār, the mawlā of Banū Ḥārithah, narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the year of the Conquest in Ramaḍān, and he fasted Ramaḍān, and the Muslims fasted with him, until, when he was at al-Kadīd, he called for water in a bowl while he was on his mount, and drank, while the people were looking, informing them that he had broken his fast; so the Muslims broke their fast.
items.ma-2364: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The People of the Book used to let their hair hang loose, and the polytheists used to part their heads. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked to conform with the People of the Book in some of what he had not been commanded about; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ let his forelock hang loose, then afterwards he parted [it].
items.ma-2365: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās ibn Rabīʿah, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over her own affair, and the orphan girl is consulted about herself, and her permission is her silence.”
items.ma-2366: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned his daughter Zaynab to Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ; her acceptance of Islam was six years before his acceptance of Islam, [and she returned] on the first marriage, and he did not introduce a [new] testimony or marriage-gift.
items.ma-2367: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: And Ṭalḥah ibn Nāfiʿ mentioned, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man married a woman of the Anṣār from Bal-ʿAjlān, and went in to her and spent the night with her; when morning came, he said: I did not find her a virgin. He said: So her matter was raised to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the girl and asked her, and she said: Indeed, I was a virgin. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the two of them, and they performed liʿān, and he gave her the mahr.
items.ma-2368: Yaʿqūb and Saʿd said: Our father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: And Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Yazīd ibn Rukānah narrated to me, from Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Shaybānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the stoning of the Jewish man and the Jewish woman at the door of his mosque. When the Jewish man felt the touch of the stones, he stood over his companion, bending over her, shielding her from the touch of the stones, until both were killed; and that was part of what Allah ﷿ did for His Messenger in confirming the zinā of the two of them.
items.ma-2369: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, he said: And Ibn Shihāb narrated that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a dead sheep and said: “Why did you not benefit from its hide?” They said: O Messenger of Allah, it is carrion. He said: “Only the eating of it has been made ḥarām.”
items.ma-2371: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, he said: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd informed me; that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-2372: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated it to us, from Maʿmar … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-2373: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās about the vision of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he mentioned. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was mentioned to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “While I was sleeping, I was shown that two bracelets of gold were placed in my hands, and I was alarmed by them and disliked them; then I was permitted, and I blew upon them, and they flew away. So I interpreted it as two liars who would come forth.” ʿUbayd Allāh said: One of them is al-ʿAnsī, whom Fayrūz killed in Yemen, and the other is Musaylimah.
items.ma-2374: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, he said: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came out from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his illness in which he died, and the people said: O Abū Ḥasan, how is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this morning? He said: By the praise of Allah, he has risen recovered. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him by the hand and said: Do you not see? By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will be taken in this illness of his; I know the faces of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib at death. So go with us to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and let us ask him in whom this matter lies. If it is in us, we will know that, and if it is in others, we will speak to him, and he will make a bequest concerning us. ʿAlī said: By Allah, if we ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for it and he refuses it to us, the people will never give it to us; so by Allah, I will never ask him.
items.ma-2375:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of Ibn Shihāb's brother narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī narrated to him, that they heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām reciting … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
Muḥammad said: And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd narrated to me, that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl made me recite upon one ḥarf, so I went back to him, and I kept asking him for more and he kept adding for me, until it ended at seven aḥruf.”
items.ma-2376: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of Ibn Shihāb's brother narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās said: I came, having nearly reached puberty, riding a she-donkey, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing, leading the people in prayer at Minā, until I came before part of the first row; then I dismounted from her and she grazed, and I joined the row with the people behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2378: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān narrated to us, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ṭawāf on his camel, and whenever he came to the corner, he pointed to it and said takbīr.
items.ma-2379: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while I was circumcised.
items.ma-2380:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Nuwayfiʿ narrated to me, from Kurayb, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr sent Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He came to him and made his camel kneel at the door of the mosque, then hobbled it, then entered the mosque, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting among his Companions. Ḍimām was a strong man, hairy, with two braids. He came forward until he stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among his Companions and said: Which of you is the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.” He said: Muḥammad? He said: “Yes.” He said: Son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I am going to ask you and be harsh in the questioning, so do not feel anything in yourself. He said: “I do not feel anything in myself; so ask about whatever appears to you.”
He said: I adjure you by Allah, your deity, and the deity of those who were before you, and the deity of those who will be after you: did Allah send you to us as a messenger? He said: “O Allah, yes.”
He said: Then I adjure you by Allah, your deity, and the deity of those who were before you, and the deity of those who will be after you: did Allah command you to command us to worship Him alone, associating nothing with Him, and to cast off these rivals that our fathers used to worship alongside Him? He said: “O Allah, yes.”
He said: Then I adjure you by Allah, your deity, and the deity of those who were before you, and the deity of those who will be after you: did Allah command you that we pray these five prayers? He said: “O Allah, yes.”
He said: Then he began to mention the obligations of Islam, obligation by obligation: the zakāh, the fasting, the Ḥajj, and all the laws of Islam, adjuring him at each obligation as he had adjured him at the one before it, until, when he had finished, he said: Then I testify that there is no deity except Allah, and I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and I will perform these obligations and avoid what you have forbidden me, then I will neither add nor subtract. He said: Then he turned and went back to his camel, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when he turned away: “If the one with the two locks speaks truly, he will enter Paradise.” He said: He came to his camel and undid its hobble, then went out until he came to his people, and they gathered around him. The first thing he spoke was to say: Wretched are al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. They said: Hush, O Ḍimām! Beware of leprosy and elephantiasis; beware of madness. He said: Woe to you! By Allah, those two neither harm nor benefit. Allah ﷿ has sent a messenger and sent down upon him a Book by which He has rescued you from what you were in; and I testify that there is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. I have come to you from him with what he commanded you and forbade you. He said: By Allah, that day had not ended, and in his settlement there was not a man or a woman except a Muslim.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās says: We have not heard of a delegate of a people who was more excellent than Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah.
items.ma-2381: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Nuwayfiʿ, the mawlā of Āl al-Zubayr, narrated to me … and he mentioned it, abridged.
items.ma-2382: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, the mawlā of ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The prayer of fear was nothing but like the prayer of these guards of yours today behind your imams, except that it was in turns. A group stood, all of them with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a group prostrated with him; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and those who had been standing prostrated for themselves; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, and they all stood with him; then he bowed and they all bowed with him; then he prostrated, and those who had been standing with him the first time prostrated, and the others, who had prostrated with him the first time, stood; and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those who had prostrated with him sat at the end of their prayer, those who had been standing prostrated for themselves, then they sat, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought them together with the salām.
items.ma-2383: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Ṭāwūs al-Yamānī, he said: I said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: They claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Perform ghusl on the day of Jumuʿah, and wash your heads, even if you are not in a state of janābah, and touch some perfume.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: As for perfume, I do not know; and as for washing, yes.
items.ma-2384: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Salamah ibn Kuhayl al-Ḥaḍramī and Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Nuwayfiʿ, the mawlā of Āl al-Zubayr, both of them narrated to me from Kurayb, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying at night in a Ḥaḍramī cloak of his, wrapped in it, with nothing on him other than it.
items.ma-2385: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a rainy day, guarding against the mud, when he prostrated, with a cloak that he had on, placing it between his hands and the ground when he prostrated.
items.ma-2386: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maʿbad ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, from some of his family, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in his two rakʿahs before Fajr, in the first rakʿah, the Opening of the Qurʾān and the two verses from the end of al-Baqarah, and in the other rakʿah, the Opening of the Qurʾān and the verse from Āl ʿImrān: {Say: O People of the Book, come to a word that is equal between us and you} [Āl ʿImrān: 64], until he completed the verse.
items.ma-2387: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Rukānah ibn ʿAbd Yazīd, the brother of Banū al-Muṭṭalib, divorced his wife three [times] in one sitting, and grieved over her with intense grief. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him: “How did you divorce her?” He said: I divorced her three. He said: “In one sitting?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then that is only one; so take her back, if you wish.” He said: So he took her back. And Ibn ʿAbbās used to hold that divorce is only at each [state of] purity.
items.ma-2388: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, from Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When your brothers were struck at Uḥud, Allah ﷿ placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that come to the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take shelter in lanterns of gold in the shade of the ʿArsh. When they found the goodness of their drink and their food and the beauty of their resting place, they said: Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not renounce jihād and not shrink back from war. So Allah ﷿ said: I will convey it to them from you.” Then Allah ﷿ revealed these verses to His Messenger: {And do not think of those who were killed} [Āl ʿImrān: 169].
items.ma-2389: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.
items.ma-2390: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Al-Ḥārith ibn Fuḍayl al-Anṣārī narrated to me, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd al-Anṣārī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The shuhadāʾ are at Bāriq, a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome; their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening.”
items.ma-2391: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Thawr ibn Zayd narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked with them to Baqīʿ al-Gharqad, then sent them off and said: “Go forth in the name of Allah,” and said: “O Allah, help them” – meaning the group whom he had sent off to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.
items.ma-2392: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Then Muḥammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on his journey and appointed as successor over al-Madīnah Abū Ruhm Kulthūm ibn Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUtbah ibn Khalaf al-Ghifārī, and went out when ten [nights] of Ramaḍān had passed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted and the people fasted with him, until, when he was at al-Kadīd – a water between ʿUsfān and Amaj – he broke his fast; then he went on until he encamped at Marr al-Ẓahrān with ten thousand of the Muslims.
items.ma-2393: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, he said: Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and Mujāhid Abū al-Ḥajjāj, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith on his journey while he was ḥarām [in iḥrām].
items.ma-2394: Ḥusayn – meaning Ibn Muḥammad – narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: A man was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose mount had broken his neck while he was in iḥrām, and he said: “Shroud him, and do not cover his head, and do not apply perfume to him; for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection while he is making the talbiyah – or while he is making ihlāl.”
items.ma-2395: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, with its isnād, except that he said: “and do not cover his face.”
items.ma-2396: Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Manṣūr narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the conquest of Makkah: “There is no hijrah – he says: after the conquest – but jihād and intention; and if you are called to go forth, then go forth.”
items.ma-2397: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr Abū Khaythamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand on my shoulder – or on my upper shoulder, Saʿīd was unsure – then said: “O Allah, give him understanding in the religion, and teach him the interpretation.”
items.ma-2398: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Thābit Abū Zayd narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This Stone has a tongue and two lips; on the Day of Resurrection it will bear witness for whoever touched it in truth.”
items.ma-2399: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah fifteen years: eight years or seven seeing light and hearing a voice, and eight or seven being given revelation; and he stayed in al-Madīnah ten.
items.ma-2400: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas ibn Mālik: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the khuṭbah toward the trunk of a palm tree; when he took the minbar, he moved to the minbar, and the trunk yearned until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to it and embraced it, and it grew quiet. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Had I not embraced it, it would have yearned until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-2401: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, and from Thābit, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of its meaning.
items.ma-2402: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that two angels came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what a sleeper sees; one of them sat at his feet and the other at his head, and the one at his feet said to the one at his head: Strike a parable for this one and for his ummah. He said: Indeed his parable and the parable of his ummah is like a party of travelers who reached the edge of a desert, and they did not have with them enough provisions to cross the desert, nor to return. While they were like that, a man came to them in a robe of ḥibarah and said: What do you think: if I bring you to meadows rich in herbage and brimming pools, will you follow me? They said: Yes. He said: So he went off with them and brought them to meadows rich in herbage and brimming pools, and they ate, and drank, and grew fat. Then he said to them: Did I not meet you in that condition, and you made a pledge to me that if I brought you to meadows rich in herbage and brimming pools, you would follow me? They said: Yes indeed. He said: Then before you are meadows richer in herbage than these, and pools more brimming than these, so follow me. He said: A group said: He has spoken truly, by Allah; we will follow him. And a group said: We are content with this; we will remain upon it.
items.ma-2403: Yaḥyā ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, he said: Water used to collect in the eyelids of the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿAlī used to sip it.
items.ma-2404: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, he said: When Ibn ʿAbbās made the talbiyah, he would say: Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, here I am; indeed all praise and favor are Yours, and the dominion; You have no partner. He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: Keep to it, for it is the talbiyah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2405: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, who narrates tafsīr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from behind him, and I saw the whiteness of his armpits, while he was mujakhkhin, having spread his arms apart.
items.ma-2406: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ ate the shoulder of a sheep, then prayed and did not repeat the wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2407: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated to me that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the shade of one of his rooms, and with him a group of Muslims, the shade having almost receded from them. He said: Then he said: “A person will come to you who looks at you with the eyes of a Shayṭān; so when he comes to you, do not speak to him.” He said: A blue man came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and spoke to him. He said: Why do you revile me – you, and so-and-so, and so-and-so? – a group whom he called by their names. He said: So the man went and called them, and they swore by Allah and made excuses to him. He said: Then Allah ﷿ revealed: {They swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think …} the verse [al-Mujādilah: 18].
items.ma-2408: Muʾammal narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the shade of a room, the shade having almost receded from him … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-2409: Ḥasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Qābūs, that his father narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Two men came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, their need being one; one of them spoke, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ found a change from his mouth, and said to him: “Do you not use the siwāk?” He said: I do, but I have not eaten food for three days. So he commanded a man concerning him, and he took him in, and he fulfilled his need.
items.ma-2410: Ḥasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān, that his father narrated to him, he said: We said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What do you make of the saying of Allah ﷿: {Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body} [al-Aḥzāb: 4] – what did He mean by that? He said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood one day to pray. He said: And a passing thought came to him, and the hypocrites who were praying with him said: Do you not see that he has two hearts – a heart with you, and a heart with them? So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body}.
items.ma-2411: Ḥasan – meaning Ibn Mūsā – narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when a matter distressed him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say: “There is no deity except Allah, al-Ḥalīm, al-ʿAẓīm; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Mighty ʿArsh; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and Rabb of the earth and Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh,” then he would supplicate.
items.ma-2412: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to one of his daughters while she was in the throes [of death], and he took her and placed her in his lap until she was taken; his eyes shed tears, and Umm Ayman wept. It was said to her: Do you weep in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? She said: Should I not weep when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeps? He said: “I did not weep; this is mercy. The believer's soul comes out from between his sides while he praises Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-2413: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, and ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, in meaning, both said: Thābit narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I stood to pray with the Prophet ﷺ and I stood on his left. So he made a [motion] with his hand from behind, until he took hold of my upper arm – or my hand – until he stood me at his right.
items.ma-2414: Yaḥyā ibn Ghaylān narrated to us, Rishdīn narrated to us, Ḥasan ibn Thawbān narrated to me, from ʿĀmir ibn Yaḥyā al-Maʿāfirī, Ḥanash narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: This verse was revealed – {Your women are a tilth for you} [al-Baqarah: 223] – about some people of the Anṣār who came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Come to her in every condition, so long as it is in the farj.”
items.ma-2415: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Qazaʿah – meaning Ibn Suwayd – narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I do not ask you for any payment for what I have brought you of the clear proofs and the guidance, except that you love Allah, and that you draw near to Him by obedience to Him.”
items.ma-2416: Abū Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, he said: Ibn Bilāl informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he performed wuḍūʾ: he washed his face, then took a handful of water and rinsed his mouth with it and blew water out of his nose; then he took a handful and did thus with it – meaning he joined it to his other hand – and washed his face with it; then he took a handful of water and washed his right hand with it; then he took a handful of water and washed his left hand with it; then he wiped his head; then he took a handful of water, then sprinkled it on his right foot until he had washed it; then he took another handful and washed his left foot with it; then he said: Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2417: Abū Salamah narrated to us, Ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of this from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2418: Abū Salamah narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman came to the Prophet ﷺ with a son of hers and said: This son of mine has madness that seizes him at our lunch and our dinner, and he spoils it for us. So the Prophet ﷺ wiped his chest and supplicated, and he retched a retch – meaning he coughed – and something like a black puppy came out of his belly.
items.ma-2419: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from ʿAmr – meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmr –, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, and a man asked him about ghusl on the day of Jumuʿah, whether it is obligatory. He said: No; whoever wishes performs ghusl. And I will narrate to you about the beginning of ghusl: The people were needy, and used to wear wool, and used to water the palm trees on their backs, and the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ was narrow with a low ceiling; so the people went out in the afternoon in wool and sweated. And the minbar of the Prophet ﷺ was short, only three steps; so the people sweated in the wool, and their odors rose – the odors of wool – and they were harmed by one another, until their odors reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on the minbar, and he said: “O people, when you come to the Jumuʿah, perform ghusl, and let each of you touch the finest perfume he has, if he has it.”
items.ma-2420: Abū Saʿīd narrated to me, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has intercourse with an animal, kill him, and kill the animal.”
items.ma-2421: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning putting forward and putting back in the throwing, the slaughtering and the shaving: “There is no harm.”
items.ma-2422: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, give Ibn ʿAbbās wisdom, and teach him the interpretation.”
items.ma-2423: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Rabīʿah ibn Hishām ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kinānah narrated to us, he said: I heard my grandfather Hishām ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrating from his father, he said: Al-Walīd sent to ask Ibn ʿAbbās: How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ act in the seeking of rain? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in humble attire, humbly submissive, and came to the place of prayer and prayed two rakʿahs, as he prays at al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā.
items.ma-2424: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, some poetry is judgment, and some eloquence is magic.”
items.ma-2425: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no contagion, no bad omen, no ṣafar, and no hāmah” – Simāk mentioned that the ṣafar is an animal that is in the belly of a person – and a man said: O Messenger of Allah, there is a mangy camel among a hundred, and it makes them mangy. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Then who infected the first?”
items.ma-2426: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Abū Saʿīd said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: from Simāk –, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on the small mat.
items.ma-2427: Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out from ʿArafah and commanded them to be calm, and made Usāmah ibn Zayd ride behind him, and said: “O people, hold to calm and dignity, for righteousness is not in the hurrying of camels and horses.” And I did not see a she-camel lifting her foreleg, running, until he reached Jamʿ. Then he made al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās ride behind him from Jamʿ to Minā, while he was saying: “O people, hold to calm and dignity, for righteousness is not in the hurrying of camels and horses.” And I did not see a she-camel lifting her foreleg, running, until he reached Minā.
items.ma-2428: Muʾammal narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered as hady a hundred camels, among them a red camel of Abū Jahl, in whose nose was a silver ring.
items.ma-2429: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever speaks about the Qurʾān without knowledge, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-2430: Muʾammal narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman whose husband was away came to a man to buy something from him, and he said: Enter the inner room until I give you. So she entered, and he kissed her and squeezed her, and she said: Woe to you, I am one whose husband is away. So he left her, and regretted what had been from him, and he came to ʿUmar and informed him of what he had done, and he said: Woe to you, perhaps she is one whose husband is away! He said: She is one whose husband is away. He said: Then go to Abū Bakr and ask him. So he came to Abū Bakr and informed him, and Abū Bakr said: Woe to you, perhaps she is one whose husband is away! He said: She is one whose husband is away. He said: Then go to the Prophet ﷺ and inform him. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Perhaps she is one whose husband is away!” He said: She is one whose husband is away. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent, and the Qurʾān was revealed: {And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night} up to His saying: {for those who remember}. He said: The man said: O Messenger of Allah, is it for me specifically, or for the people in general? He said: ʿUmar said: No, and no delight of the eye for you; rather it is for the people in general. He said: The Prophet ﷺ laughed and said: “ʿUmar has spoken truly.”
items.ma-2431: Muʾammal narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah said: Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said, about the saying of the jinn: {And that when the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they almost became about him a dense crowd} [al-Jinn: 19], he said: When they saw him leading his Companions in prayer, and they were praying his prayer, bowing with his bowing, and prostrating with his prostration, they marveled at the obedience of his Companions to him. So when they returned to their people, they said: When the servant of Allah – meaning the Prophet ﷺ – stood calling upon Him, they almost became about him a dense crowd.
items.ma-2432: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out in his illness in which he died, with his head bound in a cloth, and sat on the minbar, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: “There is no one who has been more generous to me with his person and his wealth than Abū Bakr ibn Abī Quḥāfah; and if I were to take a khalīl from among the people, I would have taken Abū Bakr as a khalīl; but the khullah of Islam is more excellent. Close for me every small door in this mosque, except the door of Abū Bakr.”
items.ma-2433: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when Māʿiz ibn Mālik came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Perhaps you kissed, or pressed, or looked?” He said: No. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Did you have intercourse with her?” – he did not use euphemism – He said: Yes. He said: Then, at that, he commanded his stoning.
items.ma-2434: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying: “I seek refuge for you both in Kalimāt Allāh al-tāmmah, from every Shayṭān and every venomous creature, and from every harmful eye.” Then he would say: “Thus my father Ibrāhīm ﵇ used to seek refuge for Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq ﵉.”
items.ma-2435: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: I said to him: We go on campaign, and are brought hides and waterskins. He said: I do not know what to say to you, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whatever hide is tanned has become pure.”
items.ma-2436: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven [limbs], and not to gather up hair or clothing.
items.ma-2437: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2438: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he has received it in full.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: And I reckon everything to be in the position of food.
items.ma-2439: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Eat from the sides of the bowl, and do not eat from its middle, for the blessing descends in its middle.”
items.ma-2440: Surayj narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from Qays ibn Saʿd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās – I think he raised it – he said: When he raised his head from the rukūʿ, he would say: “Samiʿa Allāhu li-man ḥamidah. O Allah, our Rabb, to You is the praise, filling the heaven and filling the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything thereafter.”
items.ma-2441: Surayj narrated to us, ʿAbbād – meaning Ibn al-ʿAwwām – narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Qāsim Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ proposed to Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and she placed her affair with al-ʿAbbās, so he gave her in marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2442: Surayj narrated to us, ʿAbbād narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Muslims killed a man of the polytheists on the day of the Trench, and they sent a messenger to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [offering] to pay blood-money for his corpse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is vile, vile in his blood-money, vile in his corpse.” So he left them to have him.
items.ma-2443: Surayj narrated to us, ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Prophet ﷺ wrote a document between the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār: “that they pay their blood-money according to their [customary] liabilities, and ransom their captive in a fair manner, and [make] reconciliation among the Muslims.”
items.ma-2444: Surayj narrated to me, ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
items.ma-2445: Surayj narrated to us, Ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from his father, from the blind one, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took his sword Dhū al-Faqār as an extra share on the day of Badr, and it is the one concerning which he saw the vision on the day of Uḥud. He said: “I saw in my sword Dhū al-Faqār a notch, and I interpreted it: a breach that would occur among you. And I saw that I was riding with a ram behind me, and I interpreted it: the ram of the battalion. And I saw that I was in a strong coat of mail, and I interpreted it: al-Madīnah. And I saw cattle being slaughtered; and cattle, by Allah, is good; cattle, by Allah, is good.” And what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said came to pass.
items.ma-2446: Surayj narrated to us, Ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night was to the extent that whoever was in the room could hear it, while he was in the house.
items.ma-2447: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Report is not like seeing with one's own eyes. Allah ﷿ informed Mūsā of what his people had done with the calf, and he did not throw down the tablets; but when he saw what they had done, he threw down the tablets and they broke.”
items.ma-2448:
Surayj narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed us, he said: I was with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: Which of you saw the star that shot down last night? I said: I. Then I said: I was not in prayer, but I was stung. He said: And what did you do? I said: I sought ruqyah. He said: And what made you do that? I said: A ḥadīth that al-Shaʿbī narrated to us, from Buraydah al-Aslamī, that he said: There is no ruqyah except for the [evil] eye or a venomous sting. Saʿīd – meaning Ibn Jubayr – said: He has done well who stops at what he heard.
Then he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The nations were shown to me, and I saw a prophet with a small group, and a prophet with one man and two men, and a prophet with no one with him, when a great mass was raised before me, and I said: This is my ummah. But it was said: This is Mūsā and his people; but look at the horizon. And behold, a great mass. Then it was said to me: Look at this other side. And behold, a great mass. And it was said: This is your ummah, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.” Then the Prophet ﷺ rose and entered, and the people plunged into discussion of that, and said: Who are these who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment? Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ. And some of them said: Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and never associated anything with Allah; and they mentioned other things. Then the Prophet ﷺ came out to them and said: “What is this that you were plunging into?” So they informed him of what they had said, and he said: “They are those who do not cauterize, do not seek ruqyah, and do not take bad omens, and upon their Rabb they rely.” Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan al-Asadī stood and said: Am I among them, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “You are among them.” Then another stood and said: Am I among them, O Messenger of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “ʿUkkāshah has preceded you to it.”
items.ma-2449: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shujāʿ narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us … the like of it.
items.ma-2450: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never fasted a complete month other than Ramaḍān; and he would fast, when he fasted, until the sayer would say: By Allah, he will not break his fast; and he would break his fast, when he broke his fast, until the sayer would say: By Allah, he will not fast.
items.ma-2451: Surayj narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʾammal narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ crossed the valleys and came with a hady, and he had no alternative but to perform ṭawāf of the House and to run between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah before standing at ʿArafah. As for you, O people of Makkah, delay your ṭawāf until you return.
items.ma-2452: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When wine was made ḥarām, they said: O Messenger of Allah, [what of] our companions who died while they were drinking it? So Allah ﷿ revealed: {There is no blame upon those who believed and did righteous deeds for what they ate} [al-Māʾidah: 93].
items.ma-2453: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, al-Ḥasan – meaning Ibn Ṣāliḥ – narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: It was narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who persistently drinks wine, if he dies, will meet Allah like a worshipper of an idol.”
items.ma-2454: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the blessing of horses is in their chestnut [ones].”
items.ma-2455: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr – meaning Ibn Ḥāzim – narrated to us, from Kulthūm ibn Jabr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Allah took the covenant from the back of Ādam at Naʿmān – meaning ʿArafah – and brought out from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before him like ants; then He Kallamahum qibalan, saying: {Am I not your Rabb? They said: Yes, we bear witness – lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed we were unaware of this. Or lest you say: It was only our forefathers who associated [others] before, and we were offspring after them; will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?} [al-Aʿrāf: 172–173].”
items.ma-2456: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in every Fajr prayer on the day of Jumuʿah: {Alif Lām Mīm. The revelation} and {Has there come upon man a period of time}.
items.ma-2457: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
items.ma-2458: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ; concerning the man who comes to his wife while she is menstruating, he said: “Let him give in charity half a dīnār.”
items.ma-2459: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent us ahead early – or sent Umm Salamah ahead early, and I was with them – from al-Muzdalifah to Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, and commanded us not to throw at it when the sun rises.
items.ma-2460: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning al-ʿAṭṭār – narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he said: ʿAṭāʾ narrated to me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with the baggage and the weak ones of his family on the night of al-Muzdalifah, and we prayed the Ṣubḥ at Minā, and threw the jamrah.
items.ma-2461: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAlqamah al-Qurashī, he said: We entered the house of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and found ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās in it, and we mentioned wuḍūʾ from what fire has touched. ʿAbd Allāh said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat of what fire had touched, then pray and not perform wuḍūʾ. One of us said to him: You saw him, O Ibn ʿAbbās? He said: Then he pointed with his hand to his eyes and said: My two eyes saw.
items.ma-2462: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man of Banū Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ while he was driving sheep of his, and he greeted them with salām, and they said: He only greeted you with salām in order to seek refuge from you. So they went for him and killed him and took his sheep, and brought them to the Prophet ﷺ. Then Allah ﷿ revealed: {O you who believe, when you strike out in the way of Allah, then be discerning, and do not say to one who offers you [the greeting of] peace: You are not a believer} up to the end of the verse [al-Nisāʾ: 94].
items.ma-2463: Ḥusayn and Abū Nuʿaym said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, about His saying ﷿: {You are the best ummah brought out for mankind: you enjoin the good and forbid the wrong} [Āl ʿImrān: 110], he said: They are those who emigrated with Muḥammad ﷺ to al-Madīnah. Abū Nuʿaym said: with the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2464: Ḥusayn and Abū Nuʿaym said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, he said: He who heard Ibn ʿAbbās say narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not stop between ʿArafāt and Jamʿ except to pour out water.
items.ma-2465: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, he said: I heard Jābir ibn Zayd say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed eight together, and seven together.
items.ma-2466: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ offered as hady, among his budn, a camel that had belonged to Abū Jahl, with a silver ring in its nose.
items.ma-2467: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ tore meat from a bone, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2468: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When Hilāl ibn Umayyah accused his wife [of zinā], it was said to him: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will flog you eighty lashes. He said: Allah is more just than that He would strike me eighty strikes, when He knows that I saw until I was certain, and heard until I was certain; no, by Allah, he will never strike me. He said: Then the verse of mutual cursing was revealed.
items.ma-2469: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a virgin girl came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that her father had married her [off] while she disliked it, so the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice.
items.ma-2470: Ḥusayn and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said: ʿUbayd Allāh – meaning Ibn ʿAmr – narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Ibn Jubayr – Aḥmad said: from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr – from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There will be a people at the end of time who dye with this blackness – Ḥusayn said: like the crops of pigeons – they will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.”
items.ma-2471: Ḥusayn narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bahrām narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: A band of the Jews attended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Abū al-Qāsim, tell us about some matters that we ask you about, which none knows except a prophet. Among what they asked him was: Which food did Isrāʾīl forbid himself before the Torah was sent down? He said: “Then I adjure you by Allah who sent down the Torah upon Mūsā: do you know that Isrāʾīl – Yaʿqūb ﵇ – fell gravely ill and his illness was prolonged, so he vowed a vow to Allah that if Allah cured him of his illness, he would forbid himself the drink dearest to him and the food dearest to him; and the food dearest to him was the meat of camels, and the drink dearest to him was their milk?” They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-2472: Al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Zamʿah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahrām, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed on a rug.
items.ma-2473: Al-Faḍl narrated to us, he said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, some poetry is judgment, and some speech is magic.”
items.ma-2474: Al-Faḍl narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās passed by some people who had set up a dove, at which they were throwing; and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that [a thing with] a soul be taken as a target.
items.ma-2475: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ took a daughter of his who was dying, and embraced her, and placed her between his breasts, and she died between his breasts. Umm Ayman cried out, and it was said: Do you weep in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? She said: Do I not see you weeping, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “I am not weeping; it is only mercy. The believer is in every good in every condition; his soul comes out from between his sides while he praises Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-2476: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Badhīmah, Qays ibn Ḥabtar narrated to me, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the white jar, the green jar, and the red jar. He said: The first to ask the Prophet ﷺ was the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, and they said: We take from the dregs, so which vessels? He said: “Do not drink in the gourd, the pitch-coated vessel, the hollowed trunk, and the ḥantam, and drink in waterskins.” Then he said: “Indeed Allah has forbidden for me – or has forbidden – khamr, maysir, and the kūbah, and every intoxicant is ḥarām.” Sufyān said: I said to ʿAlī ibn Badhīmah: What is the kūbah? He said: The drum.
items.ma-2477: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from a man, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The [evil] eye is true; it brings down the lofty [one].”
items.ma-2478: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd al-ʿAdanī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Duwayd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Thawbān, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
items.ma-2479: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of your kohls is antimony at the time of sleep; it makes the hair grow and clears the sight; and the best of your garments is white, so wear them, and shroud your dead in them.”
