items.ma-2480: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, ʿAdī ibn Thābit narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that anything in which there is a soul be taken as a target.
items.ma-2481: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mawhab narrated to us, he said: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: “The ayyim has more authority over her own affair than her walī, and the virgin is consulted about herself, and her silence is her consent.”
items.ma-2482: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The jinn used to listen to the revelation, listening for a word and adding ten to it; so what they heard was true, and what they added was false. And the stars were not hurled at before that. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, none of them would come to his seat but a shooting star would be hurled at him, burning what it struck; so they complained of that to Iblīs, and he said: This is only from some matter that has occurred. So he dispersed his troops, and behold, they found the Prophet ﷺ praying between the two mountains of Nakhlah; they came to him and informed him, and he said: This is the occurrence that has occurred on the earth.
items.ma-2483: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd al-ʿIjlī narrated to us – and he had a dignified appearance, we saw him at Ḥasan's –, from Bukayr ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Abū al-Qāsim, we ask you about five things; if you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet, and we will follow you. So he took from them what Isrāʾīl took from his sons, when they said: Allah is Wakīl over what we say. He said: “Bring [them].” They said: Tell us the sign of the Prophet. He said: “His eyes sleep, and his heart does not sleep.” They said: Tell us how a woman produces a female and how she produces a male. He said: “The two waters meet; when the man's water rises above the woman's water, she produces a male, and when the woman's water rises above the man's water, she produces a female.” They said: Tell us what Isrāʾīl forbade himself. He said: “He was suffering from sciatica, and found nothing that suited him except the milk of such and such – my father said: Some of them said: meaning camels – so he forbade their meat.” They said: You have spoken truly. They said: Tell us what this thunder is. He said: “An angel of the angels of Allah ﷿, assigned to the clouds; in his hand – or at his hand – is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds, driving them where Allah commands.” They said: And what is this sound we hear? He said: “His sound.” They said: You have spoken truly. Only one remains, and it is the one for which we will pledge allegiance to you if you inform us of it; for there is no prophet but that he has an angel who brings him the report; so tell us, who is your companion? He said: “Jibrīl ﵇.” They said: Jibrīl is the one who descends with war, fighting and punishment – our enemy! Had you said Mīkāʾīl, who descends with mercy, vegetation and rain, it would have been [well]. So Allah ﷿ revealed: {Whoever is an enemy to Jibrīl} up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 97].
items.ma-2484: Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid, from ʿIlbāʾ ibn Aḥmar, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and the time of the slaughter arrived, so we slaughtered the cow for seven, and the camel for ten.
items.ma-2485: Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā and al-Ṭālaqānī said: Al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ, when he prayed, would turn right and left, not twisting his neck behind his back. Al-Ṭālaqānī said: Thawr narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ … the like of it.
items.ma-2486: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from a man of the companions of ʿIkrimah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to glance in his prayer without twisting his neck.
items.ma-2487: Ḥasan ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān, from Abū Rajāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sees from his ruler something he dislikes, let him be patient; for whoever departs from the community by a span and dies, his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-2488: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī narrated to us, he said: Abū al-Mutawakkil narrated to us that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated: that he spent the night with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ one night, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ rose in the night, went out and looked at the sky, then recited this verse which is in Āl ʿImrān: {Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day} until he reached: {Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire} [Āl ʿImrān: 190–191]; then he returned to the house, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed, then lay on his side; then he returned again and looked at the sky, then recited this verse; then he returned, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed, then lay on his side; then he returned again and looked at the sky, then recited this verse; then he returned, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed.
items.ma-2489:
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Hāshim, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād – or from Abū Hāshim, from Ḥajjāj, Manṣūr was unsure – from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Samiʿa Allāhu li-man ḥamidah,” he would say: “O Allah, our Rabb, to You is the praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything thereafter.”
He said: And Manṣūr said: ʿAwn narrated to me, from his brother ʿUbayd Allāh, with this.
items.ma-2490: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was solicited concerning the daughter of Ḥamzah, that he marry her, and he said: “She is the daughter of my brother by nursing, and what becomes ḥarām through nursing is what becomes ḥarām through lineage.”
items.ma-2491: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿAlī said to the Prophet ﷺ concerning the daughter of Ḥamzah, and mentioned her beauty, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “She is the daughter of my brother by nursing.” Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “Do you not know that Allah ﷿ has made ḥarām through nursing what He has made ḥarām through lineage?”
items.ma-2492: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he saw no harm in a man marrying while he is in iḥrām, and would say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith at a water called Sarif while he was in iḥrām; and when the Prophet of Allah had completed his Ḥajj, he came back, until, when he was at that water, he consummated the marriage with her.
items.ma-2493: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man whose thigh was uncovered, and said: “Cover your thigh, for the thigh of a man is part of his ʿawrah.”
items.ma-2494: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He said: Which of the two recitations was the last: the recitation of ʿAbd Allāh, or the recitation of Zayd? He said: We said: The recitation of Zayd. He said: No; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present the Qurʾān to Jibrīl once every year, and in the year in which he was taken, he presented it to him twice, and the last of the recitations was the recitation of ʿAbd Allāh.
items.ma-2495: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, about His saying: {Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated}, he said: They were defeated and they were victorious. He said: The polytheists loved that Fāris would prevail over the Romans, because they were people of idols; and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Fāris, because they were people of a Book. They mentioned it to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “They will surely prevail.” He said: Abū Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: Set a term between us and you; if we prevail, we shall have such and such, and if you prevail, you shall have such and such. So he set a term of five years, and they did not prevail. Abū Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Did you not make it to below” – he said: I think he said: “the ten?” – Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The biḍʿ is what is less than ten – Then the Romans prevailed afterwards. He said: That is His saying: {Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated} up to His saying: {And on that day the believers will rejoice} [al-Rūm: 4]. He said: They rejoice {in the victory of Allah}.
items.ma-2496:
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated to me, that Dhakwān, the doorkeeper of ʿĀʾishah, narrated to him: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came asking permission to enter upon ʿĀʾishah; so I came, and at her head was her brother's son, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and I said: This is Ibn ʿAbbās asking permission. Her brother's son ʿAbd Allāh leaned over her and said: This is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās asking permission – and she was dying – and she said: Leave me from Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: O mother, Ibn ʿAbbās is one of your righteous sons; [let him in] to greet you with salām and bid you farewell. She said: Permit him if you wish.
He said: So I brought him in, and when he sat, he said: Receive glad tidings. She said: Again! He said: There is nothing between you and meeting Muḥammad ﷺ and the beloved ones except that the soul leave the body. You were the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah would love only what is good. Your necklace fell on the night of al-Abwāʾ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed until he reached morning in the camp, and the people reached morning without water; so Allah ﷿ revealed: that you perform tayammum with clean earth. So that was by reason of you, and of what Allah ﷿ sent down for this ummah of concession; and Allah sent down your exoneration from above seven heavens, brought by the Trustworthy Spirit; so that there is no mosque of the mosques of Allah in which Allah is mentioned except that it is recited in it during the hours of the night and the hours of the day. She said: Leave me from you, O Ibn ʿAbbās: by Him in whose Yad is my soul, I wish that I had been something discarded and forgotten.
items.ma-2497: Sufyān narrated to us, from Layth, from a man, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to her: You were only named Mother of the Believers so that you might be fortunate, and it was your name before you were born.
items.ma-2498: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Hishām, from Qays ibn Saʿd, ʿAṭāʾ narrated to me that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from the rukūʿ, he would say: “O Allah, our Rabb, to You is the praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything thereafter.”
items.ma-2499: Muʿāwiyah – he is Ibn ʿAmr – narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd, the ḥantam, the pitch-coated vessel and the hollowed trunk, and that unripe dates and ripening dates be mixed.
items.ma-2500: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Conquest was when thirteen [nights] of Ramaḍān had passed.
items.ma-2501: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Mujāhid, he said: We were with Ibn ʿAbbās, and they mentioned the Dajjāl, and they said: Written between his eyes is: k f r. He said: What are you saying? He said: They say: Written between his eyes is: k f r. Then Ibn ʿAbbās said: I did not hear him say that, but he said: “As for Ibrāhīm ﵇, look at your companion; and as for Mūsā ﵇, he is a tawny, curly-haired man on a red camel, haltered with a palm-fiber halter; it is as if I am looking at him when he descends into the valley making the talbiyah.”
items.ma-2502:
Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Mujāhid, he said: They mentioned him – meaning the Dajjāl – he said: Written between his eyes is: k f r. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I did not hear him say that, but he said: “As for Ibrāhīm ﵊, look at your companion – Yazīd said: meaning himself, ﷺ – and as for Mūsā, he is a tawny, curly-haired, tall man on a red camel, haltered with a palm-fiber halter; it is as if I am looking at him, when he has descended from the valley making the talbiyah.”
My father said: Hushaym said: The khulbah is palm fiber.
items.ma-2503: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, that Ibn ʿAbbās – Ibn ʿAwn said: I think he raised it – said: He commanded a caller, and he called out on a rainy day: Pray in your dwellings.
items.ma-2504: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Ibrāhīm – meaning Ibn Nāfiʿ – narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a sheep died in one of the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﵊ said: “Did you not benefit from its skin?”
items.ma-2505: Ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Ibrāhīm – meaning Ibn Nāfiʿ – narrated to us, from Wahb ibn Mīnās al-ʿAdanī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Prophet ﷺ wished to prostrate after the rakʿah, he would say: “O Allah, our Rabb, to You is the praise, filling the heavens and filling the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything thereafter.”
items.ma-2506: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Abī ʿImrān, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was born on Monday, was given prophethood on Monday, went out emigrating from Makkah to al-Madīnah on Monday, came to al-Madīnah on Monday, and died ﷺ on Monday, and raised the Black Stone on Monday.
items.ma-2507: ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ standing at ʿArafāt, having made al-Faḍl ride behind him; a bedouin came and stood nearby, with a slave-girl behind him, and al-Faḍl began looking at her; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed it, and began turning his face away. He said: Then he said: “O people, righteousness is not in the hurrying of horses or camels; so hold to calm.” He said: Then he set out, and I did not see it lifting its foreleg, running, until he reached Jamʿ. He said: When he stopped at Jamʿ, he made Usāmah ride behind him, then said: “O people, righteousness is not in the hurrying of horses and camels; so hold to calm.” He said: Then he set out, and I did not see it lifting its foreleg, running, until it reached Minā. Then he came to us in the dark, [to us,] the weak ones of Banū Hāshim, on donkeys of theirs, and began striking our thighs and saying: “O my sons, set out, and do not throw the jamrah until the sun rises.”
items.ma-2508: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Bukayr narrated to him, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the House, he found in it an image of Ibrāhīm and an image of Maryam, and said: “As for them, they have heard that the angels do not enter a house in which there is an image; this is Ibrāhīm, depicted – so what is the matter with him that he seeks division [by lot]?!”
items.ma-2509: Hārūn narrated to us – Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And I heard it from Hārūn – he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Abū Ṣakhr informed me, from Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Namir, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that a son of his died at Qudayd – or at ʿUsfān – and he said: O Kurayb, see how many people have gathered for him. He said: So I went out, and behold, people had gathered for him, and I informed him. He says: Are they forty? He said: Yes. He said: Bring him out, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There is no Muslim who dies and forty men who associate nothing with Allah stand over his funeral, except that Allah grants them intercession for him.”
items.ma-2510: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Muḥammad—meaning al-Khaṭṭābī—narrated to me, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man went out, and two men followed him, and a man was following them, saying: Go back. He said: So they went back. He said: Then he said to him: These two are two shayṭāns, and I did not cease [dealing] with them until I turned them back; so when you come to the Prophet ﷺ, convey to him the greeting of peace, and inform him that we are engaged in collecting our ṣadaqāt, and had they been fit for him, we would have sent them to him. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at that time prohibited seclusion.
items.ma-2511: Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, from al-Masʿūdī, he said: We did not meet anyone more steadfast in the saying of the Shīʿah than ʿAdī ibn Thābit.
items.ma-2512: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Muḥammad—meaning al-Khaṭṭābī—narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh—meaning Ibn ʿAmr—narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The price of a dog is foul.” He said: “So when he comes to you asking for the price of a dog, fill his two palms with dust.”
items.ma-2513: Yazīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān, he said: A man of Balhujaym said: O Abū ʿAbbās, what is this legal opinion that has spread among the people: that whoever performs ṭawāf of the House has become released [from iḥrām]? He said: The sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, even if it is against your will.
items.ma-2514:
Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, Ibn ʿAbbās said: A group of the Jews came before the Prophet of Allah ﷺ one day, and they said: O Abū al-Qāsim, tell us about certain matters that we will ask you about, which none knows except a prophet. He said: “Ask me whatever you wish, but give me the covenant of Allah, and what Yaʿqūb ﵇ took from his sons: that if I tell you something and you recognise it, you will follow me in Islam.” They said: That is yours. He said: “Then ask me whatever you wish.” They said: Inform us about four matters that we will ask you about: Inform us which food Isrāʾīl made forbidden for himself before the Torah was sent down? And inform us how the water of the woman and the water of the man are: how does the male come from it? And inform us how this unlettered Prophet is in sleep? And who is his walī among the angels? He said: “Then upon you is the covenant of Allah and His pledge that if I inform you, you will follow me?” He said: So they gave him whatever covenant and pledge he wished.
He said: “Then I adjure you by Him Who sent down the Torah upon Mūsā ﷺ: do you know that Isrāʾīl, Yaʿqūb ﵇, fell gravely ill, and his illness grew long, so he made a vow to Allah that if Allah, Exalted is He, cured him of his illness, he would forbid for himself the drink most beloved to him and the food most beloved to him; and the food most beloved to him was the meat of camels, and the drink most beloved to him was their milk?” They said: O Allah, yes. He said: “O Allah, bear witness against them. Then I adjure you by Allah, there is no deity except Him, Who sent down the Torah upon Mūsā: do you know that the water of the man is white and thick, and the water of the woman is yellow and thin, and whichever of them prevails, the child and the resemblance belong to it, by the permission of Allah? If the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, it is a male, by the permission of Allah; and if the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, it is a female, by the permission of Allah?” They said: O Allah, yes. He said: “O Allah, bear witness against them. Then I adjure you by Him Who sent down the Torah upon Mūsā: do you know that this unlettered Prophet’s eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?” They said: O Allah, yes. He said: “O Allah, bear witness.” They said: And now you, tell us: who is your walī among the angels? For at that point we will either join you or part from you. He said: “Indeed my walī is Jibrīl ﵇, and Allah never sent a prophet except that he was his walī.” They said: At that point we part from you; had your walī been other than him among the angels, we would have followed you and believed you. He said: “Then what prevents you from believing him?” They said: He is our enemy. He said: At that, Allah ﷿ said: {Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibrīl—indeed, he has sent it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah} up to His saying ﷿: {the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know}. And at that: {they returned with anger upon anger}, the verse. [al-Baqarah: 90]
items.ma-2515: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bahrām narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with something like it.
items.ma-2516: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from a man, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās while he was eating a pomegranate at ʿArafah, and he narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast at ʿArafah: Umm al-Faḍl sent him milk, and he drank.
items.ma-2517: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ broke his fast at ʿArafah. He said: Umm al-Faḍl sent him milk, and he drank it.
items.ma-2518:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abū al-Tayyāḥ informed us, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, he said: Sinān ibn Salamah and I performed Ḥajj, and with Sinān was a sacrificial camel, and it became exhausted and could go no further, and he was at a loss about its matter. So I said: If I reach Makkah I will certainly inquire into this. He said: When we reached Makkah, I said: Come with us to Ibn ʿAbbās. So we entered upon him, and a young girl was with him; I had two needs, and my companion had one need. He said: Shall I not clear [the place] for you? I said: No. Then I said: I had a sacrificial camel with me and it became exhausted upon us, and I said: If I reach Makkah I will certainly inquire into this. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent the sacrificial camels with so-and-so, and commanded him concerning them with his command. When he had turned his back, he returned and said: O Messenger of Allah, what shall I do with those of them that become exhausted and can go no further? He said: “Slaughter it, and dye its sandal in its blood, and strike it upon its side; and do not eat from it, neither you nor anyone of the people of your company.”
He said: So I said to him: I am in these military expeditions, and I take spoils, and I free [a slave] on behalf of my mother; will it suffice for her that I free? Ibn ʿAbbās said: A woman commanded Sinān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Juhanī to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about her mother, who had died and had not performed Ḥajj: will it suffice for her that she performs Ḥajj on her behalf? The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do you see, if her mother had owed a debt and she paid it on her behalf, would that have sufficed for her mother?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then let her perform Ḥajj on behalf of her mother.” And he asked him about sea water, and he said: “The water of the sea is purifying.”
items.ma-2519: ʿAffān narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what he narrated from his Rabb; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed your Rabb ﵎ is Raḥīm. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him; and if he does it, ten are written for him, up to seven hundred, up to many multiples. And whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him; and if he does it, one is written for him, or Allah erases it. And none is destroyed with Allah, Exalted is He, except one who is [already] destroyed.”
items.ma-2520: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Seek it in the last ten of Ramaḍān: in the ninth remaining, or the seventh remaining, or the fifth remaining.”
items.ma-2521: ʿAffān narrated to us, Salīm ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate in “Ṣād”.
items.ma-2522: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: We raid the people of the West, and most of their waterskins—and perhaps Ḥammād said: the majority of their waterskins—are carrion. He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Its tanning is its purification.”
items.ma-2523: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah fifteen years: seven years seeing the light and hearing the voice, and eight years being given revelation; and he stayed in Madīnah ten years.
items.ma-2524: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ gnawed [meat] from a shoulder, then prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2525: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿAmmār, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me—ʿAffān did not ascribe him [further] than ʿAbd Allāh—he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever sees me in a dream has seen me, for Shayṭān does not appear in my likeness.” And ʿAffān once said: “does not appear as me.”
items.ma-2526: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, he said: I heard Jābir ibn Zayd informing that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ giving a sermon at ʿArafāt: “Whoever does not find sandals, let him wear leather socks, and whoever does not find a waist-wrapper, let him wear trousers.”
items.ma-2527: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, he said: I heard Ṭāwūs narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones, and not to hold back hair or garment.” And he said on another occasion: Your Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones, and not to hold back hair or garment.
items.ma-2528: Bahz narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed me, he said: I heard Abū Ḥassān narrating from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed Ẓuhr at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then his sacrificial camel was brought, and he marked the right side of its hump, then wiped the blood off it, then garlanded it with two sandals; then his mount was brought, and when he sat upon it and it stood up with him at al-Baydāʾ, he pronounced the ihlāl for Ḥajj.
items.ma-2529: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrating that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-2530: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The hindquarter of a donkey—or he said: the leg of a donkey—was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in iḥrām, and he returned it.
items.ma-2531: Bahz narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith informed us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him, would say: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, al-Ḥalīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and Rabb of the earth, Rabb of the great Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the noble Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and Rabb of the earth, Rabb of the noble Throne.”
items.ma-2532:
Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAdī ibn Thābit informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take anything in which there is a soul as a target.”
Shuʿbah said: I said to him: From the Prophet ﷺ? He said: From the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2533: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAdī ibn Thābit informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on [the day of] Fiṭr and did not pray before it or after it; then he came to the women, and with him was Bilāl, and he began saying: “Give ṣadaqah.” And the woman began throwing her earring and her necklace.
items.ma-2534: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam informed me, he said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr led us in prayer at Jamʿ: the Maghrib prayer, three [rakʿahs] with one iqāmah. He said: Then he gave the salām, then prayed ʿIshāʾ, two rakʿahs. Then he mentioned that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar did that, and he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that.
items.ma-2535: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the leg of a donkey as a gift while he was in iḥrām, and he returned it while it was dripping blood.
items.ma-2536: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while he was fasting.
items.ma-2537: Bahz narrated to us, Abān ibn Yazīd al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from the cousin of your Prophet—meaning Ibn ʿAbbās—that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these supplications at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, al-Ḥalīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the great Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and the earth, Rabb of the noble Throne.”
items.ma-2538: Bahz narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, I said: We raid this West, and most of their waterskins are the hides of carrion? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Its tanning is its purification.”
items.ma-2539: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū Ḥassān, that a man said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: This which you say has spread among the people—Hammām said: meaning, everyone who performs ṭawāf of the House has become released [from iḥrām]. He said: The sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, even if it is against your will. Hammām said: meaning, one who has no sacrificial offering with him.
items.ma-2540: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥājib ibn ʿUmar Abū Khushaynah, the brother of ʿĪsā al-Naḥwī, narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam ibn al-Aʿraj narrated to us, he said: I sat with Ibn ʿAbbās while he was resting his head on his cloak by the well of Zamzam. So I sat with him, and he was a good companion. I asked him about ʿĀshūrāʾ. He said: About which aspect of it do you ask? I said: About its fast. He said: When you see the new moon of al-Muḥarram, count; and when you reach the morning of its ninth, fast that day. I said: Was it thus that Muḥammad ﷺ used to fast it? He said: Yes.
items.ma-2541: ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed us, that Ṭāwūs said: One who is more knowledgeable about it than they—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās—narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “That a man grant his brother his land is better for him than that he take upon it a known rent.”
items.ma-2542: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the husband of Barīrah was a black slave called Mughīth. He said: I used to see him following her in the streets of Madīnah, squeezing his eyes over her. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ gave four judgments concerning her: Her masters had stipulated the walāʾ, so the Prophet ﷺ judged: “The walāʾ is for the one who frees.” And he gave her the choice, and she chose herself, so he commanded her to observe the ʿiddah. He said: And ṣadaqah was given to her, and she gave some of it as a gift to ʿĀʾishah ﵂, and she mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “It is ṣadaqah for her, and a gift to us.”
items.ma-2543: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd and ʿIkrimah, both said: ʿUmar said: Who knows when Laylat al-Qadr is? They both said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is in the ten, in seven passing or seven remaining.”
items.ma-2544: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed al-Ṣafā one day and said: “Yā ṣabāḥāh, yā ṣabāḥāh!” He said: So Quraysh gathered to him and said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: “Do you see: if I informed you that the enemy is coming upon you at morning or at evening, would you not believe me?” They said: Yes. He said: “Indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.” He said: Abū Lahab said: Was it for this that you gathered us? Perish to you. He said: So Allah ﷿ sent down: {May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and he has perished} up to the end of the sūrah.
items.ma-2545: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from Wahb ibn Kaysān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eating a bone with meat from a sheep, then he prayed, and did not rinse his mouth and did not touch water.
items.ma-2546:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū Naḍrah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās gave us a sermon on the minbar of al-Baṣrah, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There was no prophet except that he had a supplication which he hastened to have answered in the world; and indeed I have kept my supplication hidden as intercession for my ummah. And I am the master of the children of Ādam on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting; and I am the first from whom the earth is split open, and there is no boasting; and in my hand is the banner of praise, and there is no boasting; Ādam and whoever is below him are beneath my banner, and there is no boasting.
And the Day of Resurrection will grow long for the people, and some of them will say to others: Go with us to Ādam, the father of mankind, that he may intercede with our Rabb ﷿ that He may judge between us. So they will come to Ādam ﷺ and say: O Ādam, you are the one whom Allah created with His Yad, and made to dwell in His Paradise, and for whom He made His angels prostrate; intercede for us with our Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I was brought out of Paradise because of my error, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to Nūḥ, the head of the prophets. So they will come to Nūḥ and say: O Nūḥ, intercede for us with our Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I made a supplication that drowned the people of the earth, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of Allah. So they will come to Ibrāhīm and say: O Ibrāhīm, intercede for us with our Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I lied three lies in Islam—by Allah, he only intended by them [to defend] the religion of Allah: his saying {Indeed, I am sick} [al-Ṣāffāt: 89], and his saying {Rather, this—the largest of them—did it, so ask them, if they can speak} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63], and his saying to his wife when he came upon the king: She is my sister—and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to Mūsā, whom Allah chose with His message and His speech. So they will come to him and say: O Mūsā, you are the one whom Allah chose with His message, and to whom He Kallama; so intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I killed a soul without [it being for] a soul, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to ʿĪsā, the Rūḥ of Allah and His Word. So they will come to ʿĪsā and say: Intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I was taken as a god besides Allah, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but do you see: if there were goods in a vessel that was sealed, could what is inside it be reached until the seal is broken? They will say: No. He will say: Indeed Muḥammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets, and he is present today, and he has been forgiven what preceded of his sin and what came later.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “So they will come to me and say: O Muḥammad, intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. So I will say: I am for it, until Allah ﷿ gives permission to whom He wills and is pleased with. Then when Allah ﵎ wills to cleave between His creation, a caller will call out: Where is Aḥmad and his ummah? So we are the last, the first; we are the last of the nations and the first to be reckoned with. The nations will be made to part for us from our path, and we will proceed with bright foreheads and limbs from the trace of purification. The nations will say: This ummah was almost all of them prophets. Then I will come to the gate of Paradise, and take hold of the ring of the gate, and knock on the gate. It will be said: Who are you? I will say: I am Muḥammad. So it will be opened for me, and I will come to my Rabb ﷿ upon His Kursī—or His sarīr, Ḥammād was uncertain—and I will fall down prostrating to Him, and I will praise Him with praises with which none before me has praised Him, and none after me will praise Him. Then it will be said: O Muḥammad, raise your head, and ask, you will be given; and speak, you will be heard; and intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will raise my head and say: O my Rabb, my ummah, my ummah! He will say: Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of such and such—Ḥammād did not remember it. Then I will return and prostrate, and say what I said, and it will be said: Raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; and ask, you will be given; and intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: O my Rabb, my ummah, my ummah! He will say: Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of such and such, less than the first. Then I will return and prostrate and say the like of that, and it will be said to me: Raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; and ask, you will be given; and intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will say: O my Rabb, my ummah, my ummah! He will say: Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of such and such, less than that.”
items.ma-2547: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, and he said: Simāk informed us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I was come to while I was asleep in Ramaḍān, and it was said to me: Tonight is Laylat al-Qadr. He said: So I rose, while I was drowsy, and held on to one of the ropes of the tent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and behold, he was praying. He said: Then I looked at that night, and behold, it was the night of twenty-three.
items.ma-2548: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Abū al-Minhāl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, and they were practising salaf, so he said: “Whoever makes salaf, let him not make salaf except in a known measure and a known weight.”
items.ma-2549: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ came out of the privy and food was brought to him, and it was said to him: Will you not perform wuḍūʾ? He said: “I was only commanded to perform wuḍūʾ when I stand for the prayer.”
items.ma-2550:
ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, Ḥanẓalah al-Sadūsī narrated to us, he said: I said to ʿIkrimah: I recite in the Maghrib prayer {Say: I seek refuge in the Rabb of the daybreak} and {Say: I seek refuge in the Rabb of mankind}, and some people find fault with me for that? He said: What is wrong with that? Recite them, for they are from the Qurʾān.
Then he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and prayed two rakʿahs, in which he recited only Umm al-Kitāb.
items.ma-2551: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah: that ʿAlī ﵁ was brought a group of these zanādiqah, with books with them; so he ordered a fire, and it was kindled, then he burned them and their books. ʿIkrimah said: That reached Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Had it been I, I would not have burned them, because of the prohibition of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I would have killed them, because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not punish with the punishment of Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-2552: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah: that ʿAlī seized some people who had apostatised from Islam and burned them with fire. That reached Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Had it been I, I would not have burned them. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not punish anyone with the punishment of Allah ﷿,” and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.” Then what Ibn ʿAbbās said reached ʿAlī, and he said: Woe to the son of the mother of Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-2553: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād—he is Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, ʿAmmār informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, in what the sleeper sees, at midday, and he was standing, dishevelled and dusty, in his hand a bottle in which was blood. So I said: May my father and my mother be [given] for you, O Messenger of Allah, what is this? He said: “This is the blood of al-Ḥusayn and his companions; I have not ceased gathering it since today.” So we counted that day, and they found that he was killed on that day.
items.ma-2554:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Sulaymān al-Shaybānī, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over a funeral after she had been buried.
And Wakīʿ said: Sufyān narrated to us, the like of it.
items.ma-2555: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If one of them, when he comes to his wife, said: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Shayṭān away from me, and keep Shayṭān away from what You provide for me, and a child were born between them, Shayṭān would never harm him.”
items.ma-2556: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Teach, and make things easy, and do not make things difficult; and when you become angry, be silent; and when you become angry, be silent; and when you become angry, be silent.”
items.ma-2557: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ combined Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in Madīnah, without travel and without fear. He said: I said: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, and why did he do that? He said: He wished not to put any of his ummah in difficulty.
items.ma-2558: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ went to the open ground and relieved himself, then food was brought near to him, and they said: Shall we bring you water for wuḍūʾ? He said: “For what shall I perform wuḍūʾ?! Shall I pray, that I should perform wuḍūʾ—or: I have prayed, that I should perform wuḍūʾ?!”
items.ma-2559: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I slept at the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and the Prophet ﷺ rose in the night and went to the need, then came and washed his face and his hands, then slept. Then he rose in the night and came to the waterskin, and loosed its tie, and performed wuḍūʾ, a wuḍūʾ between the two wuḍūʾs, not excessive, though he made it thorough; then he stood to pray. And I stretched myself, disliking that he should see me—I had been abqīhi, meaning watching him. Then I rose and did as he had done, and I stood at his left; so he took hold of what was beside my ear until he turned me around, and I was at his right, while he prayed. His prayer was completed to thirteen rakʿahs, among them the two rakʿahs of Fajr. Then he lay down and slept until he breathed heavily. Then Bilāl came and informed him of the prayer, so he rose and prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-2560: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām, and had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2561: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Ajlaḥ, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man said: O Messenger of Allah, what Allah wills and you will. He said: “You have made me an equal to Allah! Rather, what Allah alone wills.”
items.ma-2562: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, ʿUthmān al-Jazarī informed me that he heard Miqsam, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ entered the House, and supplicated in its corners, then came out and prayed two rakʿahs.
items.ma-2563: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz—meaning Ibn Rufayʿ—said: One who heard Ibn ʿAbbās say informed me: The Prophet ﷺ did not dismount between ʿArafāt and Jamʿ except to pour out water.
items.ma-2564: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the talbiyah until he threw [pebbles at] Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-2565: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah at Sarif while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2566: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ bathed from janābah, and the Prophet ﷺ came to perform wuḍūʾ from what was left of it; she said: I bathed from it. He said: “Indeed water is not made impure by anything.”
items.ma-2567:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and I watched the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [to see] how he prayed. He rose and urinated, then washed his face and his two palms, then slept; then he rose and went to the waterskin and loosed its tie, then poured into the basin—or the bowl—and inclined his hand over it, then performed wuḍūʾ, a good wuḍūʾ between the two wuḍūʾs; then he stood to pray. So I came and stood at his left, and he took me and made me stand at his right. So the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was completed at thirteen rakʿahs. He said: Then he slept until he breathed heavily—and we would recognise him when he slept by his breathing—then he went out to the prayer and prayed, and began to say in his prayer, or in his prostrations: “O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and light on my right, and light on my left, and light before me, and light behind me, and light above me, and light beneath me, and make me a light.” Shuʿbah said: or he said: “Make for me a light.”
He said: And ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he slept lying down.
items.ma-2568: Rawḥ narrated to us, Saʿīd and Hishām ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-Ḥalīm, al-ʿAẓīm. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the great Throne. There is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and Rabb of the earth, and Rabb of the noble Throne.”
items.ma-2569: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Zayd, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn Ḥarmalah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: My maternal aunt Umm Ḥufayd gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ clarified butter, milk, and lizards. As for the lizards, the Prophet ﷺ spat upon them. Khālid ibn al-Walīd said to him: Did you find it repulsive, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Yes—or: Indeed.” And the Prophet ﷺ took the milk and drank from it, then said to Ibn ʿAbbās, who was on his right: “The drink is yours, but do you permit that I give your uncle to drink?” Ibn ʿAbbās said: I said: No, by Allah, I would not prefer anyone over your leftover. He said: So I took it and drank, then gave it back. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “I know of no drink that suffices in place of food other than milk. So whoever of you drinks it, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and give us more of it; and whoever eats a food, let him say: O Allah, bless us in it and feed us better than it.”
items.ma-2570: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the open ground for his need, then returned, and a bone with meat on it was brought to him, and he did not perform wuḍūʾ, but ate from it. And ʿAmr added to me in this ḥadīth, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith, he said: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, you have not performed wuḍūʾ! He said: “I did not intend the prayer, that I should perform wuḍūʾ.”
items.ma-2571:
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I found these ḥadīths in my father’s book in his own handwriting: Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Warrāq narrated to us, he said: Rishdīn ibn Kurayb narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he drank, would breathe twice in the drink.
And my father wrote after this ḥadīth: I do not think that ʿAbd Allāh heard this ḥadīth.
items.ma-2572: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: I found in my father’s book in his handwriting, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-ʿAbdī al-ʿAṣarī narrated to me, he said: Jabalah ibn ʿAṭiyyah narrated to us, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I was a guest of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who is my maternal aunt, and it was a night when she was not praying. So she took a cloak and folded it, and cast a cushion upon it, then threw another cloak over it, then entered into it, and spread a mat for me beside her, and I rested my head with her on her pillow. Then the Prophet ﷺ came, having prayed the last ʿIshāʾ, and took a piece of cloth and wrapped it as a waist-wrapper, and cast off his garment, and entered her blanket with her, and spent the night, until when it was the end of the night, he rose to a hanging waterskin and moved it. I intended to rise and pour for him, but I disliked that he should see that I had been awake. He said: Then he performed wuḍūʾ, then came to the bed, and took his two garments and cast off the piece of cloth, then came to the mosque and stood in it praying. And I rose to the waterskin and performed wuḍūʾ, then came to the mosque and stood at his left; so he reached for me and made me stand at his right. He prayed and I prayed with him thirteen rakʿahs; then he sat, and I sat by his side, and he placed his elbow against my side, and inclined his cheek to my cheek, until I heard the breathing of a sleeper. While I was like that, Bilāl came and said: The prayer, O Messenger of Allah. So he walked to the mosque and I followed him, and he stood praying the two rakʿahs of Fajr, and Bilāl began the iqāmah.
items.ma-2573: Ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, and he mentioned something. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to use the siwāk often. He said: Until we thought—or: we saw—that [something] would be sent down upon him.
items.ma-2574:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed and then gave a sermon, and [so did] Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, on ʿĪd, without adhān and without iqāmah.
My father said: ʿAbd Allāh heard it.
items.ma-2575: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: I found this ḥadīth in my father’s book: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Safar, from Saʿīd ibn Shufayy, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that they began asking him about the prayer on a journey. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ, when he went out from his family, would not add to two rakʿahs until he returned.
items.ma-2576: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: I found this ḥadīth in my father’s book in his handwriting: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Jaʿfar al-Aḥmar narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Two qiblahs are not fitting in one city, nor is there jizyah upon the Muslims.”
items.ma-2577:
Jarīr narrated to us, he also raised it [to the Prophet ﷺ].
He said: “Two qiblahs are not fitting in one land, and there is no jizyah upon a Muslim.”
items.ma-2578: al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from Rishdīn, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to breathe in the vessel twice.
items.ma-2579: al-Ḥakam narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ made the talbiyah after the prayer.
items.ma-2580: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I saw my Rabb ﵎.” And I heard this ḥadīth from my father; he dictated it to me in another place.
items.ma-2581: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2582: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he prayed seven [rakʿahs] together and eight [rakʿahs] together.
items.ma-2583: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon at ʿArafāt, and he said: “Whoever does not find a waist-wrapper, let him wear trousers, and whoever does not find sandals, let him wear leather socks.”
items.ma-2584: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven, and not to hold back hair or garment.”
items.ma-2585: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of food until he takes full possession of it, or it is taken in full. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: I reckon all sales to be in its position.
items.ma-2586: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Do not take anything in which there is a soul as a target.”
items.ma-2587: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh and Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, that both heard ʿAṭāʾ narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2588: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven, and not to hold back hair, nor garment.”
items.ma-2589: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while in iḥrām and fasting.
items.ma-2590: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven, and not to hold back hair or garment.”
items.ma-2591: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah and Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man was thrown from his mount while he was in iḥrām, and died. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that they wash him with water and lote-leaf, and shroud him in his two garments, and not cover his head, for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection making the talbiyah. And Ayyūb said: with matted hair.
items.ma-2592: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he saw no harm in a man marrying while he is in iḥrām, and he would say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith at a water called Sarif while he was in iḥrām; then when the Prophet of Allah ﷺ completed his Ḥajj, he came back, until when he was at that water, he consummated the marriage with her.
items.ma-2593: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿAṭāʾ, that he bore witness upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn ʿAbbās bore witness upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he prayed on the day of ʿĪd, then gave a sermon, then came to the women and commanded them to give ṣadaqah, and they began throwing.
items.ma-2594: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to me, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while fasting.
items.ma-2595: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said concerning the one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating: “Let him give ṣadaqah of a dīnār, or half a dīnār.”
items.ma-2596: Hushaym narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones, and not to hold back hair or garment.”
items.ma-2597: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “If one of you—or: if one of them—when he came to his wife, said: O Allah, keep Shayṭān away from me, and keep Shayṭān away from what You provide me; then a child were to be between them, except that Shayṭān would not be given power over him—or: Shayṭān would not harm him.”
items.ma-2598:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid, from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and forbade us a matter that was beneficial to us, but the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better for us than what he forbade us. He said: “Whoever has land, let him cultivate it, or let him leave it, or let him lend it.”
He said: So I mentioned that to Ṭāwūs, and he held that Ibn ʿAbbās was among the most knowledgeable of them; he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “For whoever has land, that he lend it to his brother is better for him.” Shuʿbah said: ʿAbd al-Malik used to combine these: Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid, and the one from whom he narrated was Mujāhid. Shuʿbah said: As if he is the owner of the ḥadīth.
items.ma-2599: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, he said: I heard Ṭāwūs say: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about this verse: {Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it except affection in kinship} [al-Shūrā: 23]. He said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The kin of the family of Muḥammad. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: You have been hasty! There was no clan of Quraysh with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not have kinship, so he said: Except that you maintain what is between me and you of kinship.
items.ma-2600: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Bishr narrating that he heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ while in iḥrām, and fell from his she-camel, and she killed him instantly. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded concerning him that he be washed with water and lote-leaf, and be shrouded in two garments, and he said: “Do not touch him with perfume, outside his head—Shuʿbah said: Then later he narrated it to me, and said: outside his head, or his face—for he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with matted hair.”
items.ma-2601:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when I was ten years old, and I was circumcised, and I had read the muḥkam of the Qurʾān.
He said: So I said to Abū Bishr: What is the muḥkam? He said: The mufaṣṣal.
items.ma-2602: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, so I stood at his left, and he took me and placed me at his right.
items.ma-2603: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to me, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed women who visit graves, and those who take mosques and lamps over them.
items.ma-2604: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Ṣāliḥ, the mawlā of al-Tawʾamah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ about something of the matter of the prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Run [water] between the fingers of your hands and your feet—meaning completing the wuḍūʾ.” And among what he said to him: “When you bow, place your palms on your knees until you are at ease—and al-Hāshimī once said: until you both are at ease—and when you prostrate, let your forehead rest firmly on the ground, until you feel the bulk of the ground.”
items.ma-2605: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us. And ʿAttāb said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to let his hair hang loose, while the polytheists used to part their hair, and the People of the Book used to let their hair hang loose; and he used to love to conform with the People of the Book in what he had not been commanded anything about; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ parted his hair.
items.ma-2606: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from ʿIkrimah: that a man asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the nabīdh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: He used to drink by day what was made at night, and drink by night what was made by day.
items.ma-2607: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the hollowed vessel, the gourd, and the pitch-coated vessel, and said: “Do not drink except from one that has a tie.” So they made [vessels of] camel hides, then made necks for them from sheepskins. That reached him, and he said: “Do not drink except from that whose upper part is from it.”
items.ma-2608: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh informed us. And ʿAttāb said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿĀṣim informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him, he said: I gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [water] to drink from Zamzam, and he drank while standing.
items.ma-2609: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād informed us, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: Allah ﵎ did not grant victory in any place as He granted victory on the day of Uḥud. He said: So we denied that. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Between me and whoever denied that is the Book of Allah ﵎. Indeed Allah ﷿ says concerning the day of Uḥud: {And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission}—Ibn ʿAbbās says: and al-ḥass is killing—{until, when you lost courage}—up to His saying—{and He has already pardoned you; and Allah is full of bounty to the believers} [Āl ʿImrān: 152]. He only meant by this the archers. That was because the Prophet ﷺ stationed them in a place, then said: “Protect our backs; if you see us being killed, do not come to our aid, and if you see that we have taken spoils, do not share with us.” Then when the Prophet ﷺ had taken spoils, and they had made the camp of the polytheists lawful, the archers all bent down and entered the camp, plundering; and the ranks of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had met together, and they were like this—and he interlaced the fingers of his hands—and had become mixed up. So when the archers left that gap in which they had been, the horses entered from that place upon the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and they struck one another and became confused, and many of the Muslims were killed. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions had had the first part of the day, until seven or nine of the bearers of the polytheists’ banner were killed. Then the Muslims turned in flight toward the mountain, and did not reach what the people call the cave; they were only beneath the mihrās. And Shayṭān cried out: Muḥammad has been killed. There was no doubt that it was true, and we remained so, not doubting that he had been killed, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appeared between the two Saʿds; we recognised him by his swaying when he walked. He said: So we rejoiced, as though what had befallen us had not befallen us. He said: Then he climbed toward us, and he was saying: “The Ghaḍab of Allah has intensified upon a people who made the face of His Messenger bleed.” He said: And he said another time: “O Allah, it is not for them to be above us,” until he reached us. He stayed a while, and behold, Abū Sufyān was shouting at the bottom of the mountain: Be exalted, Hubal—twice, meaning his gods—where is Ibn Abī Kabshah? Where is Ibn Abī Quḥāfah? Where is Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb? ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I not answer him? He said: “Yes.” So when he said: Be exalted, Hubal, ʿUmar said: Allah is higher and more majestic. He said: Abū Sufyān said: O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, indeed its eye has been delighted, so turn back from it—or: so come away from it. Then he said: Where is Ibn Abī Kabshah? Where is Ibn Abī Quḥāfah? Where is Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb? ʿUmar said: This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this is Abū Bakr, and here I am, ʿUmar. He said: Abū Sufyān said: A day for the day of Badr; the days are in turns, and war is by buckets. He said: ʿUmar said: Not alike: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire. He said: You claim that; then we have indeed been disappointed and have lost. Then Abū Sufyān said: Indeed you will find mutilation among your slain, and that was not by the opinion of our nobles. He said: Then the zeal of the Jāhiliyyah overtook him. He said: So he said: Indeed, that did happen. And he did not dislike it.
items.ma-2610: Nūḥ ibn Maymūn narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh—meaning al-ʿUmarī—informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah, from his brother Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman brought out a boy of hers and said: O Messenger of Allah, does this one have Ḥajj? He said: “Yes, and for you is a reward.”
items.ma-2611: Nūḥ ibn Maymūn narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿĀʾishah, both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded from Minā by night.
items.ma-2612: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated it to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ṭawāf of the Day of Sacrifice until night.
items.ma-2613: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that two men disputed before the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked the claimant for proof, but he had no proof; so he made the defendant swear, and he swore by Allah, there is no deity except Him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You have sworn, but Allah has forgiven you because of your sincerity in your saying: There is no deity except Allah.”
items.ma-2614: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah, from Ḥanash, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out and pour out water, then wipe himself with dust. So I would say: O Messenger of Allah, water is near you. He would say: “And what lets me know? Perhaps I will not reach it.”
items.ma-2615: ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us, he said: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not fast on Friday alone.”
items.ma-2616: ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was most generous in Ramaḍān, when Jibrīl met him; and Jibrīl used to meet him every night of Ramaḍān and study the Qurʾān with him. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous with good than the wind that is sent forth.
items.ma-2617: ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Aslamī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and confessed to zinā, and he said: “Perhaps you kissed, or pressed, or looked.”
items.ma-2618: ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Abū Hurayrah and Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Do not eat the sharīṭah, for it is the slaughtering of Shayṭān.”
items.ma-2619:
ʿAttāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he forbade every one with a fang among the beasts of prey, and every one with a talon among the birds.
He said: al-Ḥakam raised it [to the Prophet ﷺ]. Shuʿbah said: And I dislike to narrate it as raised. He said: And Ghaylān and al-Ḥajjāj narrated to me from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, not raising it.
items.ma-2620: ʿAttāb narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ passed by Abū Qatādah while he was beside a man whom he had killed, and said: “Leave him and his salab.”
items.ma-2621: ʿAttāb narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah informed us, from Yazīd al-Naḥwī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the teeth and the fingers equal in blood-money.
items.ma-2622: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, Mūsā ibn Aʿyan narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The likeness of the one who gives ṣadaqah and then returns to his ṣadaqah is only like the one who vomits, then eats his vomit.”
items.ma-2623: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Ḥarrānī narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik al-Nukrī narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The kaffārah of sin is regret.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If you did not sin, Allah ﷿ would bring a people who sin, so that He might forgive them.”
items.ma-2624: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan—meaning Ibn Shaqīq—narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah informed us, he said: Yazīd al-Naḥwī narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The teeth are equal, and the fingers are equal.”
items.ma-2625: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Muḥammad both said: ʿUbayd Allāh—meaning Ibn ʿAmr—narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Indeed Allah has made unlawful for you khamr, maysir, and kūbah,” and he said: “Every intoxicant is ḥarām.”
items.ma-2626: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the price of khamr, the mahr of a prostitute, and the price of a dog, and he said: “When its owner comes asking for its price, fill his two palms with dust.”
items.ma-2627: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Ibn Hubayrah, that Maymūn al-Makkī informed him: that he saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr lead them in prayer, gesturing with his two palms when he stood, and when he bowed, and when he prostrated, and when he rose for standing; he would stand, then gesture with his hands. He said: So I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I saw Ibn al-Zubayr praying a prayer such as I have not seen anyone pray; and I described to him this gesture. He said: If you love to look at the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, then follow the prayer of Ibn al-Zubayr.
items.ma-2628: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān narrated to us, Dāwūd—meaning al-ʿAṭṭār—narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man said: How much suffices me for wuḍūʾ? He said: A mudd. He said: How much suffices me for ghusl? He said: A ṣāʿ. The man said: It does not suffice me. He said: May you have no mother! It sufficed one who is better than you: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2629: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ghasīl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out with his head covered by his garment, and said: “O people, the people increase and the Anṣār decrease; so whoever of you takes charge of a matter in which he benefits anyone, let him accept from their doer of good and overlook their wrongdoer.”
items.ma-2630: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Ḥakam informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah al-Laythī gave the Messenger of Allah ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, while he was in iḥrām at Qudayd, the hindquarter of a donkey, and he returned it while it was dripping blood.
items.ma-2631: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah said: from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ returned it.
items.ma-2632: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed me, he said: I heard Mūsā ibn Salamah say: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās; I said: I am in Makkah, so how do I pray? He said: Two rakʿahs, the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-2633: Bahz and ʿAffān both said: Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah—ʿAffān said: Qatādah narrated to us—from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was proposed the daughter of Ḥamzah [for marriage], and he said: “Indeed she is the daughter of my brother by suckling, and what is prohibited by suckling is what is prohibited by the womb.” ʿAffān said: “And indeed she is not lawful for me.”
items.ma-2634: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Kaysān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I saw my Rabb ﵎.”
items.ma-2635: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah narrated to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cast [pebbles at] the jimār when the sun had passed its zenith.
items.ma-2636: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Thābit informed us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the lightest of the people of the Fire in punishment is Abū Ṭālib, and he is wearing two sandals of fire from which his brain boils.”
items.ma-2637: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed us, from Mūsā ibn Salamah: that he asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the prayer at al-Baṭḥāʾ, when one has not caught the prayer with the imām. He said: Two rakʿahs, the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-2638: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered, then shaved.
items.ma-2639: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions arrived, and the fever of Yathrib had weakened them. He said: The polytheists said: There is coming to you a people whom the fever has weakened. He said: So Allah made the Prophet ﷺ aware of that, and he commanded his Companions to do raml, and the polytheists sat on the side of al-Ḥijr, looking at them. So they did raml, and walked between the two corners. He said: The polytheists said: These are the ones whom you claim the fever has weakened?! These are stronger than such and such. They mentioned their saying. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Nothing prevented him from commanding them to do raml in all the circuits except sparing them. And I heard Ḥammād narrate it from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, or from ʿAbd Allāh, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās; and I heard Ḥammād mention it from Ibn Jubayr, with no doubt about it from him.
