items.ma-2640: ʿAffān narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from ʿAmmār, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās: How many [years] had come upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day he died? He said: I did not think that someone like you, among his people, would have that hidden from him! He said: I said: I asked, and was told differing things, so I wished to know your saying on it. He said: Do you count? I said: Yes. He said: Hold: forty he was sent for, and fifteen he stayed in Makkah, in security and in fear, and ten as an emigrant in Madīnah.
items.ma-2641: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from a man, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions arrived on the morning of the fourth, pronouncing the ihlāl for Ḥajj, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them to make it ʿumrah, except whoever had the sacrificial offering with him. He said: So shirts were put on, and the censers gave off their scent, and women were married.
items.ma-2642: ʿAffān narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Kathīr Abū Dāwūd al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, he said: I heard Ibn Shihāb narrating from Abū Sinān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us a sermon and said: “O people, Ḥajj has been prescribed for you.” He said: So al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis stood and said: Every year, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Had I said it, it would have become obligatory, and had it become obligatory you would not have acted upon it, and you would not be able to act upon it. Ḥajj is once; whoever adds, it is voluntary.”
items.ma-2643: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah will surely resurrect the stone on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, bearing witness by it upon whoever touched it in truth.”
items.ma-2644: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madīnah and saw the Jews fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said: “What is this day on which you fast?” They said: This is a righteous day; this is a day on which Allah delivered the Children of Isrāʾīl from their enemy. He said: So Mūsā fasted it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am more entitled to Mūsā than you.” He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted it and commanded its fasting.
items.ma-2645: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us—from my memory—from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade ḥabal al-ḥabalah.
items.ma-2646:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who returns to his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
Qatādah said: And I do not know vomit [to be] anything except ḥarām.
items.ma-2647: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, he said: We used to say, while we were boys: The one who returns to his gift is like the dog; it vomits, then returns to its vomit. And we did not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given a likeness regarding that, until Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who returns to his gift is like the dog that vomits, then returns to its vomit.”
items.ma-2648: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked during the Farewell Ḥajj, and a man said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered. He said: So he gestured with his hand and said: “No harm.” And a man said: O Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered before I threw [the pebbles]. He said: So he gestured with his hand and said: “No harm.” He said: So on that day he was not asked about anything of putting forward and putting back, except that he gestured with his hand and said: “No harm.”
items.ma-2649: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Abū Jamrah informed us, he said: I used to ward off the people from Ibn ʿAbbās, then I was kept away for some days. He said: What kept you away? I said: The fever. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the fever is from the flaring of Jahannam, so cool it with the water of Zamzam.”
items.ma-2650: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd, the jar, and the pitch-coated vessel.
items.ma-2651: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah informed us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I was a boy running with the boys. He said: I turned around, and behold, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was behind me, approaching. I said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ has come only for me. He said: So I ran until I hid behind the door of a house. He said: I did not perceive anything until he reached me. He said: He took me by the nape of my neck and pushed me a push, and said: “Go and call Muʿāwiyah for me”—and he was his scribe. He said: So I ran, and said: Answer the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, for he has a need.
items.ma-2652: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from Madīnah to Makkah and fasted until he reached ʿUsfān; then he called for water and raised it to his hand to show the people, and broke his fast until he reached Makkah, and that was in Ramaḍān. And Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted and broke his fast; so whoever wishes, let him fast, and whoever wishes, let him break his fast.
items.ma-2653: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr informed me, he said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās—he did not hear it from him—: that a kid wanted to pass in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and he began to ward it off.
items.ma-2654: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is none of the children of Ādam but has erred, or intended an error, except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā; and it is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā.”
items.ma-2655: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us with Usāmah riding behind him, and we gave him to drink of this nabīdh—meaning the nabīdh of the siqāyah—and he drank from it and said: “You have done well; do thus.”
items.ma-2656: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I prayed behind an old man in Makkah, and he said the takbīr twenty-two times in the Ẓuhr prayer. So I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I prayed behind a foolish old man, and he said the takbīr twenty-two times in the Ẓuhr prayer. He said: May your mother be bereaved of you! That is the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-2657: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb ibn Khālid narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Attach the farāʾiḍ to their people; what remains is for the nearest male man.”
items.ma-2658: And with this isnād—thus my father said—that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones: the forehead—then he pointed with his hand to his nose—and the two hands, and the two knees, and the ends of the two feet; and that we not hold back the garments, nor the hair.”
items.ma-2659: And with this isnād—he said: thus my father said—that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped, and gave the cupper his wage, and put [medicine] in his nose.
items.ma-2660: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The mukātab: blood-money is paid for what of him has been freed at the reckoning of a free man, and for what of him remains enslaved at the reckoning of a slave.”
items.ma-2661: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, from Muḥammad—meaning Ibn Isḥāq—from Ḥusayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: In Madīnah there were two men who dug graves: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ would dig for the people of Makkah, and Abū Ṭalḥah would dig for the Anṣār and make the laḥd for them. He said: So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, al-ʿAbbās sent two men to them, and said: O Allah, choose for Your Prophet. So they found Abū Ṭalḥah, and did not find Abū ʿUbaydah, so he dug for him and made the laḥd.
items.ma-2662: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Abū Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw the whiteness of his armpits while he was prostrating.
items.ma-2663: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Upon every Muslim is a Ḥajj, and had I said: every year, it would have been so.”
items.ma-2664: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid—meaning Ibn Ziyād—narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar until he died, and ʿUthmān until he died; and the first to forbid it was Muʿāwiyah. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So I was amazed at him, when he has narrated to me that he trimmed [hair] for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a broad arrowhead.
items.ma-2665: Yūnus and Ḥujayn both narrated to me, they said: Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us the tashahhud as he taught us the Qurʾān, and he would say: “The blessed greetings, the good prayers are for Allah. Peace be upon you—Ḥujayn said: Peace upon you—O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
items.ma-2666: Yūnus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2667: Yūnus narrated to us, al-Barāʾ—meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghanawī—narrated to us, from Abū Naḍrah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was on the minbar of the people of al-Baṣrah, and I heard him say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge after his prayer from four things, saying: “I seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire, and I seek refuge in Allah from the fitnahs, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, and I seek refuge in Allah from the fitnah of the one-eyed liar.”
items.ma-2668: Yūnus narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt narrated to us, from ʿIlbāʾ, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew four lines on the ground. He said: “Do you know what this is?” They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of the women of the people of Paradise: Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, the wife of Firʿawn, and Maryam daughter of ʿImrān.”
items.ma-2669: Yūnus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that he narrated to him: that he rode behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “O boy, I am going to teach you words: Preserve Allah, He will preserve you; preserve Allah, you will find Him in front of you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help through Allah. And know that the ummah, if they gathered to benefit you, would not benefit you except with something that Allah has written for you; and if they gathered to harm you, they would not harm you except with something that Allah has written against you. The pens have been lifted, and the pages have dried.”
items.ma-2670: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped, and gave the cupper his wage, and put [medicine] in his nose.
items.ma-2671: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade drinking from the mouth of the waterskin, and the mujaththamah, and the milk of the jallālah.
items.ma-2672:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿAṭāʾ informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you eats food, let him not wipe his hand until he licks it or has it licked.”
Abū al-Zubayr said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say that: I heard it from the Prophet ﷺ: “And let him not lift the dish until he licks it or has it licked, for the last of the food has the blessing in it.”
items.ma-2673: Ḥasan—meaning Ibn Mūsā—narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I prayed the eclipse prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I did not hear from him in it a letter of the Qurʾān.
items.ma-2674: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ the prayer of the eclipse, and I did not hear from him in it a single letter.
items.ma-2675: Ḥasan narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah al-Waḍḍāḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be wary of narrating from me except what you know; for whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-2676: Ḥasan narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was attended [by death], he said: “Bring me a shoulder-blade, I will write for you in it a writing, so that no two men of you differ after me.” He said: So the people came forward in their clamor, and the woman said: Woe to you, the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!
items.ma-2677: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah narrated to us, from Ḥanash ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed in the urine of camels and their milk is a cure for those whose bellies are corrupted.”
items.ma-2678: Surayj narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from Barakah ibn al-ʿUryān al-Mujāshiʿī, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah curse the Jews: fats were made forbidden for them, so they sold them and ate their prices; and indeed, when Allah ﷿ makes the eating of something forbidden, He makes its price forbidden.”
items.ma-2679: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: I was with my father at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was a man conversing privately with him, and he seemed like one turning away from my father. So we went out from him, and my father said to me: O my son, did you not see your cousin as one turning away from me? I said: O father, he had a man with him conversing privately with him. He said: So we returned to the Prophet ﷺ, and my father said: O Messenger of Allah, I said to ʿAbd Allāh such and such, and he informed me that you had a man with you conversing privately with you; was anyone with you? So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “And did you see him, O ʿAbd Allāh?” He said: I said: Yes. He said: “Indeed that was Jibrīl, and he is the one who occupied me from you.”
items.ma-2680: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah fifteen years: eight years or seven seeing the light and hearing the voice, and eight or seven being given revelation; and he stayed in Madīnah ten.
items.ma-2681: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Duwayd, Ismāʿīl ibn Thawbān narrated to me, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The eye is true; the eye is true; the eye brings down the ḥāliq.”
items.ma-2682: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Yūnus narrating from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of companions are four, and the best of detachments are four hundred, and the best of armies are four thousand; and twelve thousand will not be overcome because of fewness.”
items.ma-2683: Yūnus narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd narrated to us, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, what do you say of a man who killed a believer? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: {His recompense is Jahannam, abiding therein} to the end of the verse [al-Nisāʾ: 93]. He said: He said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, what do you say if he repents and believes and does righteous deeds? He said: May his mother be bereaved of him! And how could repentance be for him?! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The slain one will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his head with his right—or he said: with his left—and seizing his companion with his other hand, his jugular veins pouring blood, in front of the Throne of al-Raḥmān, and he will say: O my Rabb, ask this one why he killed me.”
items.ma-2684: Yūnus narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, Sulaymān al-Shaybānī narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm narrated to us, he said: A man invited us, and brought a table on which were thirteen lizards. He said: And that was at night, so some ate and some left. When morning came we went early to Ibn ʿAbbās, and I asked him; and those who sat with him said a great deal about that, until one of them said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I do not eat it, and I do not forbid it.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Evil is what you have said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was only sent as one who makes lawful and one who makes unlawful. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with Maymūnah, and with him were al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, Khālid ibn al-Walīd and a woman; and a table was brought on which were bread and the meat of a lizard. He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to take [from it], Maymūnah said to him: O Messenger of Allah, it is the meat of a lizard. So he withheld his hand and said: “It is meat that I have not eaten, but you eat.” He said: So al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, Khālid ibn al-Walīd and the woman ate. He said: And Maymūnah said: I will not eat from food from which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not eat.
items.ma-2685: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed us, from Qays ibn Saʿd, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz: that Najdah wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the share of the near of kin: for whom is it? And about the orphan: when does his orphanhood end? And about the woman and the slave who attend the spoils? And about the killing of the children of the polytheists? Ibn ʿAbbās said: Were it not that I would be turning him back from something he is falling into, I would not have answered him. And he wrote to him: You wrote to me asking about the share of the near of kin: for whom is it? We used to see it as for the kin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but our people refused that to us. And about the orphan: when does his orphanhood end? When he has reached puberty and good has been perceived in him. And about the woman and the slave who attend the spoils: they have nothing, but they are given a gift and are given [something]. And about the killing of the children of the polytheists: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill them, so do not kill them, unless you know of them what al-Khaḍir knew of the boy when he killed him.
items.ma-2686: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions arrived in Makkah, and the fever of Yathrib had weakened them. The polytheists said: A people have come to you whom the fever of Yathrib has weakened, and they have met evil from it. So the polytheists sat at the side that adjoins al-Ḥijr, and Allah made His Prophet aware of what they said. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them to do raml in the three circuits, so that the polytheists would see their strength. He said: So they did raml for three circuits, and he commanded them to walk between the two corners, where the polytheists did not see them. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: Nothing prevented the Prophet ﷺ from commanding them to do raml in all the circuits except sparing them. Then the polytheists said: These are those whom you claimed the fever had weakened? These are tougher than such and such.
items.ma-2687: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a Bedouin gave the Prophet ﷺ a gift, and he gave him something in return for it. He said: “Are you satisfied?” He said: No. He said: So he added to it. He said: “Are you satisfied?” He said: No. He said: So he added to it. He said: “Are you satisfied?” He said: Yes. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I had resolved not to accept a gift except from a Qurashī, or an Anṣārī, or a Thaqafī.”
items.ma-2688: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions performed ʿumrah from al-Jiʿrānah, and did raml at the House for three [circuits] and walked four.
items.ma-2689: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is none of the people but has erred, or intended an error, except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā.”
items.ma-2690: Ḥasan and ʿAffān narrated to us, in meaning, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The lightest of the people of the Fire in punishment is Abū Ṭālib: on his two feet are two sandals of fire from which his brain boils.”
items.ma-2691: Shādhān narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When khamr was made unlawful, some people said: O Messenger of Allah, our companions who died while they were drinking it? So there was revealed: {There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten} [al-Māʾidah: 93]. He said: And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: O Messenger of Allah, our companions who died while they were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis? So there was revealed: {And Allah would never let your faith be lost} [al-Baqarah: 143].
items.ma-2692:
Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū Naḍrah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās gave us a sermon on this minbar, the minbar of al-Baṣrah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There was no prophet except that he had a supplication which he hastened to have answered in the world, and I have kept my supplication hidden as intercession for my ummah. And I am the master of the children of Ādam on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no boasting; and I am the first from whom the earth is split open, and there is no boasting; and in my hand is the banner of praise, and there is no boasting; Ādam and whoever is below him are beneath my banner.”
He said: “And the Day of Resurrection will grow long for the people, until some of them will say to others: Go with us to Ādam, the father of mankind, that he may intercede for us with his Rabb ﷿, so that He may judge between us. So they will come to Ādam ﵇ and say: O Ādam, you are the one whom Allah created with His Yad, and made to dwell in His Paradise, and for whom He made His angels prostrate; so intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I was brought out of Paradise because of my error, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to Nūḥ, the head of the prophets. So they will come to Nūḥ and say: O Nūḥ, intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I made a supplication that drowned the people of the earth, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of Allah ﵇. He said: So they will come to Ibrāhīm and say: O Ibrāhīm, intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I lied three lies in Islam, and nothing concerns me today except myself—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: He only intended by them [to defend] the religion of Allah: his saying {Indeed, I am sick}, and his saying {Rather, this—the largest of them—did it}, and his saying to his wife: She is my sister—but go to Mūsā, whom Allah chose with His message and His speech. So they will come to Mūsā and say: O Mūsā, you are the one whom Allah chose with His message, and to whom He Kallama; so intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I killed a soul without [it being for] a soul, and nothing concerns me today except myself; but go to ʿĪsā, the Rūḥ of Allah and His Word. So they will come to ʿĪsā and say: O ʿĪsā, you are the Rūḥ of Allah and His Word, so intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. He will say: I am not [the one] for that; I was taken as a god besides Allah, and nothing concerns me today except myself. Then he will say: Do you see: if there were goods in a vessel that had been sealed, could what is in the vessel be reached until the seal is broken? They will say: No. He will say: Indeed Muḥammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets, is present today, and he has been forgiven what preceded of his sin and what came later.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “So they will come to me and say: O Muḥammad, intercede for us with your Rabb, that He may judge between us. So I will say: Yes, I am for it, until Allah gives permission to whom He wills and is pleased with. Then when Allah ﷿ wills to cleave between His creation, a caller will call out: Where is Aḥmad and his ummah? So we are the last, the first; we are the last of the nations and the first to be reckoned with. The nations will be made to part for us from our path, and we will proceed with bright foreheads and limbs from the trace of purification, and the nations will say: This ummah was almost all of them prophets.” He said: “Then I will come to the gate of Paradise, and take hold of the ring of the gate of Paradise, and knock on the gate. It will be said: Who are you? I will say: Muḥammad. So it will be opened for me, and I will see my Rabb ﷿, and He is upon His Kursī—or His sarīr—and I will fall down prostrating to Him, and I will praise Him with praises with which none before me has praised Him, and none after me will praise Him. Then it will be said: Raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; and ask, you will be given; and intercede, your intercession will be accepted.” He said: “So I will raise my head and say: O my Rabb, my ummah, my ummah! It will be said to me: Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of such and such. So I will bring them out. Then I will return and fall down prostrating, and I will praise Him with praises with which none before me has praised Him, and none after me will praise Him. Then it will be said to me: Raise your head, and speak, you will be heard; and ask, you will be given; and intercede, your intercession will be accepted. So I will raise my head and say: O my Rabb, my ummah, my ummah! It will be said: Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of such and such. So I will bring them out.” He said: And in the third time he said the like of this also.
items.ma-2693: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, with something similar: that he said in the first: “Whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of barley of īmān,” and in the second: “a grain of wheat,” and in the third: “a speck.”
items.ma-2694: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl ﵇ said to me: Indeed the prayer has been made beloved to you, so take of it what you wish.”
items.ma-2696: Ḥasan narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, he said: And Abū Salamah informed me, from ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in Makkah ten years, the Qurʾān being sent down upon him, and in Madīnah ten.
items.ma-2697: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿUthmān—meaning Ibn al-Mughīrah—from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I saw ʿĪsā son of Maryam, and Mūsā, and Ibrāhīm. As for ʿĪsā, he is ruddy, curly-haired, broad-chested; and as for Mūsā, he is dark-skinned, large-bodied.” They said to him: And Ibrāhīm? He said: “Look at your companion”—meaning himself.
items.ma-2698: Ḥasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, he said: Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān narrated to us, that his father narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet of Allah ﷺ—Zuhayr said: there is no doubt about it—he said: “Indeed good guidance, good bearing, and moderation are one part of twenty-five parts of prophethood.”
items.ma-2699: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated it to us, Zuhayr and Jaʿfar—meaning al-Aḥmar—narrated to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The good bearing …” and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-2700: Aswad narrated to us, Abū Kudaynah Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed five prayers at Minā.
items.ma-2701: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū al-Muḥayyāh Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿlā al-Taymī narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Ẓuhr on the Day of Tarwiyah at Minā, and prayed the morning prayer on the Day of ʿArafah there.
items.ma-2702: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān, he said: I heard Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever sees from his ruler something he dislikes, let him be patient; for no one separates from the community by a span and dies, except that he dies a death of Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-2703: Ḥasan narrated to us, Yaʿqūb—meaning al-Qummī—narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined. He said: “And what has ruined you?” He said: I turned my saddle last night. He said: So he did not reply to him with anything. He said: Then Allah revealed to His Messenger this verse: {Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish} [al-Baqarah: 223]: “Come from the front, and from the back, and beware of the rear and the menstruation.”
items.ma-2704: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to one of his daughters, who was giving up her soul, and he fell upon her, and did not raise his head until she was taken. He said: Then he raised his head and said: “Praise be to Allah. The believer is in good: his soul is drawn out from between his two sides while he praises Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-2705: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a group of the Anṣār who had set up a dove to shoot at, and he said: “Do not take anything in which there is a soul as a target.”
items.ma-2706: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me ride behind him, with Qutham in front of him.
items.ma-2707:
Surayj and Yūnus narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād—meaning Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did raml at the House, and that that is a sunnah. He said: They spoke truly and they spoke falsely. I said: And how did they speak truly and falsely? He said: They spoke truly: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did raml at the House; and they spoke falsely: it is not a sunnah. Quraysh said at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah: Leave Muḥammad and his Companions until they die the death of the nagaf. Then when they made peace with him that they would come in the following year [and] stay in Makkah three days, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and the polytheists were on the side of Quʿayqiʿān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: “Do raml at the House three [circuits],” and it is not a sunnah.
I said: And your people claim that he performed ṭawāf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a camel, and that that is a sunnah. He said: They spoke truly and they spoke falsely. I said: And how did they speak truly and falsely? He said: They spoke truly: he did perform ṭawāf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a camel; and they spoke falsely: it is not a sunnah. The people were not being driven away from the Messenger of Allah, nor turned away from him, so he performed ṭawāf on a camel so that they might hear his speech, and their hands would not reach him.
I said: And your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ran between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and that that is a sunnah? He said: They spoke truly. Indeed Ibrāhīm, when he was commanded with the rites, Shayṭān presented himself to him at the place of running and raced him, and Ibrāhīm outran him. Then Jibrīl went with him to Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, and a shayṭān presented himself to him—Yūnus said: al-Shayṭān—and he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then he presented himself to him at the middle Jamrah, and he threw seven pebbles at him. He said: He had laid him down on his forehead—Yūnus said: and there he laid him down on his forehead—and Ismāʿīl had on a white shirt, and he said: O my father, I have no garment in which you could shroud me other than this one, so take it off so that you may shroud me in it. So he tried to take it off, and he was called from behind him: {That O Ibrāhīm, you have already fulfilled the vision} [al-Ṣāffāt: 105]. Ibrāhīm turned around, and behold, there was a white ram, horned, large-eyed. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Indeed we used to follow that kind of ram. He said: Then Jibrīl went with him to the farthest Jamrah, and Shayṭān presented himself to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he went away. Then Jibrīl went with him to Minā; he said: This is Minā—Yūnus said: this is where the people make their camels kneel—then he brought him to Jamʿ and said: This is al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. Then he went with him to ʿArafah, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: Do you know why it was called ʿArafah? I said: No. He said: Jibrīl said to Ibrāhīm: You have known—Yūnus said: Have you known?—He said: Yes. Ibn ʿAbbās said: From that it was called ʿArafah. Then he said: Do you know how the talbiyah was? I said: And how was it? He said: When Ibrāhīm was commanded to call out to the people for Ḥajj, the mountains lowered their heads for him, and the villages were raised for him, and he called out to the people for Ḥajj.
items.ma-2708: Muʾammal narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū al-Ṭufayl … and he mentioned it, except that he said: their hands do not reach him; and he said: And there Ibrāhīm laid Ismāʿīl down on his forehead.
items.ma-2709: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them this supplication as he taught them a sūrah of the Qurʾān, saying: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Jahannam, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl, and I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of life and death.”
items.ma-2710: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he stood for the prayer from the middle of the night, would say: “O Allah, to You is the praise; You are Nūr al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ. And to You is the praise; You are Qayyām al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ. And to You is the praise; You are Rabb of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. You are al-Ḥaqq, and Your saying is true, and Your promise is true, and meeting You is true, and Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, and in You I have believed, and upon You I have relied, and to You I have turned, and by You I have disputed, and to You I have referred judgment. So forgive me what I have put forward and what I have delayed, and what I have concealed and what I have declared. You are the One [beside whom] there is no deity except You.”
items.ma-2711:
Isḥāq – meaning Ibn ʿĪsā – narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Zayd – meaning Ibn Aslam –, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The sun was eclipsed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and the people with him. He stood for a long standing – he said: about the length of Sūrat al-Baqarah – then he bowed a long bowing, then he raised [his head] and stood a long standing, which was shorter than the first standing, then he bowed a long bowing, which was shorter than the first bowing, then he prostrated, then he stood, and stood a long standing, which was shorter than the first standing, then he bowed a long bowing, which was shorter than the first bowing – My father said: And in what I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: Then he stood a long standing, which was shorter than the first standing, then he bowed a long bowing, which was shorter than the first bowing, then he prostrated, then he finished; then he returned to the narration of Isḥāq: – Then he finished, and the sun had cleared, and he said: “Indeed the sun and the moon are two signs from the signs of Allah; they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life; so when you see that, remember Allah.”
They said: O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something where you stood, then we saw you draw back? He said: “Indeed I saw Paradise, and I reached for a cluster from it, and had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains. And I saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight like today, and I saw that most of its people were women.” They said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Because of their kufr.” It was said: Do they disbelieve in Allah? He said: “They disbelieve in the husband, and they disbelieve in kindness. If you were kind to one of them for a lifetime, then she saw something from you, she would say: I have never seen any good from you.”
items.ma-2712: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me that Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed him that Marwān said: Go, O Rāfiʿ – to his doorkeeper – to Ibn ʿAbbās and say: If every man among us who rejoiced in what he was given and loved to be praised for what he did not do is to be punished, then we will all be punished! Ibn ʿAbbās said: What have you to do with this? This was revealed only about the People of the Book. Then Ibn ʿAbbās recited: {And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book: You will surely make it clear to the people} – this verse – and Ibn ʿAbbās recited: {Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they have not done} [Āl ʿImrān: 187 - 188]. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and told him of something else, and they went out having shown him that they had informed him of what he had asked them about, and they sought his praise for that, and they rejoiced in what they had brought of their concealing from him what he had asked them about.
items.ma-2713: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The first to deny was Ādam” – he said it three times – “Indeed Allah, when He created him, wiped his back and brought out his offspring and presented them to him, and he saw among them a man who shone. He said: O Rabb, who is this? He said: Your son Dāwūd. He said: How long is his lifespan? He said: Sixty. He said: O Rabb, increase his lifespan. He said: No, unless you add to it from your own lifespan. So he added to it forty years from his lifespan, and Allah wrote a document against him, and made the angels witness against him. Then when He wished to take his soul, he said: Forty of my term remain. It was said to him: You gave it to your son Dāwūd. He said: So he denied.” He said: “So Allah ﷿ brought out the document and established the proof against him, and He completed it for Dāwūd ﵇ to a hundred years, and He completed for Ādam ﵇ his lifespan to a thousand years.”
items.ma-2714: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Abū Bakr – meaning al-Nahshalī – narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray eight rakʿahs at night, and pray witr with three, and pray the two rakʿahs. Then when he grew old, he came to nine: six and three.
items.ma-2715: ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, he said: Ibn Hubayrah narrated to me, he said: One who heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying informed me: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Beware of the three curse-causing [acts].” It was said: What are the curse-causing [acts], O Messenger of Allah? He said: “That one of you sit in a shade in which people take shade, or on a road, or in a pool of standing water.”
items.ma-2716: Abū Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, he said: Layth informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2717: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of Ibn Shihāb's brother narrated to us, from his uncle, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah narrated to me that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl made me recite upon one ḥarf, so I went back to him, and I did not cease asking him for more and he increasing me, until it reached seven aḥruf.”
items.ma-2718:
Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, ʿUqayl ibn Khālid narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of companions are four, and the best of detachments are four hundred, and the best of armies are four thousand.”
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A people will never be overcome on account of fewness, once they reach the number of twelve thousand.”
items.ma-2719: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man went out from Khaybar, and two men followed him, and another followed behind the two, saying: Go back, go back, until he turned them back. Then he caught up with the first one and said: These two are two shayṭāns, and I did not cease with them until I turned them back. So when you come to the Messenger of Allah, convey to him the greeting of peace, and inform him that we are here collecting our ṣadaqāt, and if they were fit for him, we would have sent them to him. He said: So when the man reached al-Madīnah, he informed the Prophet ﷺ, and at that [time] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade seclusion.
items.ma-2720: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray witr with three: with {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, and {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-2721: Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, from Muḥammad, of the family of ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, she said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to prolong looking at lepers.
items.ma-2723: Isḥāq narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to go out on a journey, he would say: “O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor over the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the burden on the journey and the gloom of the return. O Allah, fold up the earth for us, and make the journey easy for us.”
items.ma-2724: ʿAffān and Abū Saʿīd – the meaning [being the same] – both said: Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl ibn Khabbāb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ turned toward Uḥud and said: “By the One in whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad, it would not please me that Uḥud be turned into gold for the family of Muḥammad that I spend in the path of Allah, and I die on the day I die leaving two dīnārs of it, except two dīnārs that I set aside for a debt, if there be one.” Then he died, and he left no dīnār and no dirham, and no slave and no slave-girl, and he left his coat of mail pawned with a Jew for thirty ṣāʿs of barley.
items.ma-2725: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad and Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī both said: Sharīk narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj – both said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr with three: with {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, and {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-2726: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr with three … then he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-2727: Abū al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Ḥabībah informed me, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Kill the doer and the one it is done to, in the deed of the people of Lūṭ; and the animal, and the one who has intercourse with the animal; and whoever has intercourse with a woman who is a maḥram, kill him.”
items.ma-2728: Abū al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Ḥabībah informed me, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out his armies, he would say: “Go out in the name of Allah, fighting in the path of Allah whoever disbelieved in Allah. Do not act treacherously, and do not commit ghulūl, and do not mutilate, and do not kill children, nor the people of the hermitages.”
items.ma-2729: Abū al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Ḥabībah informed me, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us, for fever and pains: “In the name of Allah, al-Kabīr. I seek refuge in Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, from the evil of a gushing vein, and from the evil of the heat of the Fire.”
items.ma-2730: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a bowl of tharīd, and he said: “Eat from around it, and do not eat from its middle, for the blessing descends in its middle.”
items.ma-2731: Rawḥ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked on the Day of Sacrifice about a man who shaved before he threw [the pebbles], or slaughtered by naḥr, or slaughtered by dhabḥ, and the like of this in putting forward and putting back. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no harm, there is no harm.”
items.ma-2732: Abū Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lūṭ, kill the doer and the one it is done to.”
items.ma-2733: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he said, about the one who comes to an animal: Kill the doer and the one it is done to.
items.ma-2734: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man of the Anṣār spoke ill of a father of al-ʿAbbās who had been in the Jāhiliyyah, so al-ʿAbbās slapped him. He came to his people, and they said: By Allah, we will slap him as he slapped him. So they put on weapons, and that reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he ascended the minbar and said: “O people, which of the people of the earth is most honoured with Allah?” They said: You. He said: “Indeed al-ʿAbbās is from me, and I am from him, so do not revile our dead, lest you harm our living.” Then the people came and said: O Messenger of Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from your anger.
items.ma-2735: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Sulaymān, from Mujāhid: that the people were circumambulating the House, and Ibn ʿAbbās was sitting with a hooked staff with him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “{O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. And if a drop of the zaqqūm were dropped, it would embitter the livelihood of the people of the earth; so what of those who have no food except the zaqqūm?!”
items.ma-2736: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no one of the people except that he has erred, or intended a sin, [it] not being Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā.”
items.ma-2737: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah informed us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never fasted a complete month other than Ramaḍān; and when he fasted, he would fast until the one who says would say: By Allah, he will not break the fast; and he would break the fast when he broke it until the one who says would say: By Allah, he will not fast.
items.ma-2738: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to trim his moustache, and your father Ibrāhīm before him used to trim his moustache.
items.ma-2739: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Hishām – meaning al-Dastuwāʾī – narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not boast of your fathers who died in the Jāhiliyyah; for by the One in whose Yad is my soul, what the dung beetle rolls with its two nostrils is better than your fathers who died in the Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-2740: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr al-Nahshalī narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray witr with three.
items.ma-2741: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Sharīk informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man said: O Messenger of Allah, Ḥajj every year? He said: “Rather one Ḥajj upon every person; and if I had said: Yes, every year, it would have been every year.”
items.ma-2742: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Yazīd narrated to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been given five that no prophet before me was given, and I do not say them boastfully: I was sent to all the people, the red and the black; and I was made victorious by terror [for the distance of] a month's journey; and the spoils were made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; and the earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification; and I was given the intercession, so I deferred it for my ummah, and it is for whoever does not associate anything with Allah.”
items.ma-2743: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ looked at Uḥud and said: “By the One in whose Yad is the soul of Muḥammad, it would not please me that Uḥud be gold for the family of Muḥammad that I spend in the path of Allah, and I die on the day I die with two dīnārs of it with me, except that I set them aside for a debt.” He said: Then he died, and he left no dīnār and no dirham, and no slave and no slave-girl, and he left his coat of mail as a pledge with a Jew for thirty ṣāʿs of barley.
items.ma-2744: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, Abū Saʿīd and ʿAffān said: Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUmar entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on a mat that had left a mark on his side. He said: O Prophet of Allah, if only you would take a bed softer than this! He said: “What have I to do with the world? My likeness and the likeness of the world is only that of a rider who travelled on a summer day, then took shade under a tree for an hour of the day, then set out and left it.”
items.ma-2745: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ fought an enemy, and he did not finish with them until he delayed the ʿAṣr beyond its time. When he saw that, he said: “O Allah, whoever has kept us back from the middle prayer, fill their houses with fire, and fill their graves with fire,” or words like that.
items.ma-2746:
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān both said: Thābit narrated to us, Hilāl narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed qunūt for a month continuously, in the Ẓuhr, the ʿAṣr, the Maghrib, the ʿIshāʾ and the Ṣubḥ, at the end of every prayer, when he said: Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah, in the last rakʿah, calling down [a curse] upon them, upon a clan of Banū Sulaym, upon Riʿl, Dhakwān and ʿUṣayyah, and those behind him would say āmīn. He had sent to them, calling them to Islam, and they killed them.
ʿAffān said in his narration: He said: And ʿIkrimah said: This was the key of the qunūt.
items.ma-2747: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam and Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every one with a canine tooth among the beasts of prey, and every one with a talon among the birds.
items.ma-2748: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ḥusayn narrated to us, Ibn Buraydah narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, to You I have submitted, and in You I have believed, and upon You I have relied, and to You I have turned in repentance, and by You I have disputed. I seek refuge in Your ʿIzzah – there is no deity except You – that You lead me astray. You are al-Ḥayy who does not die, while the jinn and mankind die.”
items.ma-2749:
Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Ḍimād al-Azdī came to Makkah, and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with boys following him, and he said: O Muḥammad, I treat madness! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, praise is for Allah; we seek His help and we seek His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of ourselves. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray, and whomever He leads astray, there is none to guide him. And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone, no partner for Him, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.” He said: He said: Repeat these words to me. He said: Then he said: I have heard poetry, and divination by birds, and soothsaying, and I have not heard the like of these words; they have reached the deep of the sea. And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. So he accepted Islam, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him when he accepted Islam: “Upon you and upon your people?” He said: He said: Yes, upon me and upon my people.
He said: Then a detachment from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ passed by his people after that, and some of them took something from them – a water-container or other – and they said: This is from the people of Ḍimād; return it. He said: So they returned it.
items.ma-2750: Abū Jaʿfar al-Madāʾinī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbbād ibn al-ʿAwwām informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Umm al-Faḍl, the daughter of al-Ḥārith, came with Umm Ḥabībah bint ʿAbbās and placed her in the lap of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she urinated, so Umm al-Faḍl snatched her away, then struck her between her shoulders, then snatched her away again. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give me a cup of water.” Then he poured it over where she had urinated, then said: “Make the water follow the path of the urine.”
items.ma-2751: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ziyād informed me that Qazaʿah, a mawlā of ʿAbd al-Qays, informed him that he heard ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I prayed beside the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿĀʾishah was behind us praying with us, and I was beside the Prophet ﷺ praying with him.
items.ma-2752:
Aswad narrated to us, Ayyūb ibn ʿUtbah narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of uncertainty.
Ayyūb said: And Yaḥyā explained the sale of uncertainty; he said: “Among uncertainty is the diver's cast; and the sale of uncertainty is the runaway slave, and the sale of the straying camel, and the sale of uncertainty is what is in the wombs of livestock, and the sale of uncertainty is the dust of mines, and the sale of uncertainty is what is in the udders of livestock, except by measure.
items.ma-2753: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrating, holding [his arms] apart, until I saw the whiteness of his armpits.
items.ma-2754: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The talbiyah of the Prophet ﷺ was: “Labbayka, O Allah, labbayk. Labbayka, there is no partner for You, labbayk. Indeed the praise and the favour are Yours, and the dominion; there is no partner for You.”
items.ma-2755:
Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A cheese was brought to the Prophet ﷺ on an expedition, and he said: “Where was this made?” They said: In Fārs, and we think that carrion is put in it. He said: “Pierce it with the knife, and mention the name of Allah, and eat.”
Sharīk mentioned it another time, and added in it: So they began striking it with sticks.
items.ma-2756: Aswad narrated to us, al-Ḥasan – meaning Ibn Ṣāliḥ – narrated to us, from his father, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in an upper room of his, and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you; may ʿUmar enter?
items.ma-2757: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When you differ about the road, leave seven cubits, then build; and whoever his neighbour asks that he [be allowed to] prop upon his wall, let him leave him.”
items.ma-2758: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ conquered Makkah, he stayed in it seventeen [days], praying two rakʿahs.
items.ma-2759: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he raised it [to the Prophet ﷺ], he said: “Whoever's slave-woman bears from him, she is one set free in the wake of him” – or he said: “after him.”
items.ma-2760: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ praying in one garment, wrapped in it, protecting himself with its excess [parts] from the cold of the ground and its heat.
items.ma-2761: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke with clear speech, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed among eloquence there is sorcery, and indeed among poetry there is wisdom.”
items.ma-2762: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The chiefs of Quraysh gathered in al-Ḥijr, and made a pact by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other, and Nāʾilah and Isāf: If we see Muḥammad, we will rise to him as one man, and we will not part from him until we kill him. Then his daughter Fāṭimah ﵂ came weeping, until she entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: These chiefs of Quraysh have made a pact against you; if they see you, they will rise to you and kill you, and there is no man among them but he knows his share of your blood. He said: “O little daughter, show me [water for] wuḍūʾ.” So he performed wuḍūʾ, then entered the mosque upon them, and when they saw him they said: Here he is. And they lowered their eyes, and their chins fell onto their chests, and they were hamstrung in their seats, and none raised a gaze to him, and none of them rose to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced until he stood over their heads, and took a handful of dust, and said: “May the faces be disfigured.” Then he threw it at them, and not a single pebble of those pebbles struck a man among them except that he was killed as a disbeliever on the day of Badr.
items.ma-2763: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd that Qays ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to him that Ḥanash narrated to him that Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to him, he said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to me: “O boy, I will narrate to you a narration. Guard Allah, He will guard you; guard Allah, you will find Him in front of you. When you ask, ask Allah, and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried. If the ummah were to come to benefit you with something that Allah ﷿ has not written for you, it would not be able to; and if it wished to harm you with something that Allah has not written for you, it would not be able to.”
items.ma-2764:
Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq and Mūsā ibn Dāwūd both said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah – Yaḥyā said: from al-Aʿraj, and Mūsā did not say: from al-Aʿraj – from Ḥanash, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out and urinate, and rub himself with dust; so I would say: O Messenger of Allah, the water is near to you. He said: “I do not know; perhaps I will not reach it.”
Yaḥyā said on another occasion: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he went out, and urinated, and performed tayammum, and it was said to him: The water is near to us.
items.ma-2765: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Abū Kudaynah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed five prayers at Minā.
items.ma-2766: Aswad narrated to us, Huraym narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take good omens and did not take bad omens, and a good name pleased him.
items.ma-2767: Yaḥyā ibn Ghaylān narrated to us, Rishdīn narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith praying with his hair knotted behind him, so he stood behind him and began to undo it, and the other acquiesced to him. Then he turned to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: What do you want with my head? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The likeness of this is only like the likeness of one who prays while tied up.”
items.ma-2768: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Avoid drinking in the ḥantam, and the gourd, and the pitch-coated vessel; and drink in the waterskin.”
items.ma-2769: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Muslims loved that the Romans prevail over Fārs, because they were People of a Book; and the polytheists loved that Fārs prevail over the Romans, because they were people of idols. The Muslims mentioned that to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Indeed, they will be defeated.” Abū Bakr mentioned that to them, and they said: Set a term between us and you; if they prevail, you will have such and such, and if we prevail, we will have such and such. So he set a term between them of five years, and they did not prevail. Abū Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Why did you not make it – I think he said – less than ten?” He said: And Saʿīd said: The biḍʿ is what is less than ten. He said: Then the Romans prevailed after that, and that is His saying, Exalted: {Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been overcome in the nearest land, and they, after their being overcome, will overcome in a few years}. He said: So the Romans were overcome, then they overcame afterward. He said: {To Allah belongs the command before and after, and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah}. He said: The believers rejoice in the victory of Allah.
items.ma-2770: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Duwayd narrated to us, from Salm ibn Bashīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Two believers met at the door of Paradise, a rich believer and a poor believer, who had been in the world. The poor one was admitted into Paradise, and the rich one was held back for as long as Allah willed that he be held back, then he was admitted into Paradise, and the poor one met him and said: O my brother, what held you back? By Allah, you were held back until I feared for you. He said: O my brother, after you I was held in a dreadful, detestable place of detention, and I did not reach you until so much sweat flowed from me that if a thousand camels, every one of them an eater of ḥamḍ, had come to it, they would have departed from it satisfied.”
items.ma-2771:
Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Yazīd ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ḥabīb – meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmrah –, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd, the ḥantam, the naqīr, and the pitch-coated vessel, and that unripe dates be mixed with ripe dates.
He said: I said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, what do you think of a man who puts his nabīdh in a green jar as if it were a glass bottle, in the morning, and drinks it at night? He said: No, desist from what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you?!
items.ma-2772: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Yazīd – meaning Ibn ʿAṭāʾ – narrated to us, from Yazīd – meaning Ibn Abī Ziyād –, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ came, and he had been ailing, and circumambulated the House on a camel, with a hooked staff with him; whenever he passed by it he touched it with the staff. When he finished his circumambulation, he made [the camel] kneel and prayed two rakʿahs.
items.ma-2773: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “A man must not come into direct contact with a man, nor a woman with a woman.”
items.ma-2774: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the prohibition of khamr was revealed, they said: O Messenger of Allah, what of those who died while they were drinking khamr?! So there was revealed: {There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten} up to the end of the verse [al-Māʾidah: 93].
items.ma-2775: Khalaf narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the qiblah was changed, it was said: O Messenger of Allah, what of those who died while they were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis? So Allah sent down: {And Allah would not waste your īmān} [al-Baqarah: 143].
items.ma-2776: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mukhawwal, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr with three: with {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, and {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-2777: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Wuhayb ibn Khālid informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones: the forehead – and he indicated with his hand toward his nose – and the two hands, and the two knees, and the ends of the digits; and not to hold back the garments nor the hair.”
items.ma-2778: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, al-Barāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghanawī, of their own [people], narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Naḍrah narrating, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was upon this minbar saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge at the end of every prayer from four, saying: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the fitnahs, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of the one-eyed liar.”
items.ma-2779: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Whoever is killed in the face of the wrong done to him is a shahīd.”
items.ma-2780: Mūsā narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from Ibn Shihāb that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed him that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ sent his letter to Kisrā with a man, and commanded him to hand it to the chief of al-Baḥrayn, and the chief of al-Baḥrayn handed it to Kisrā. When he read it, he tore it up. He said: I think that Ibn al-Musayyab said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them that they be torn to pieces with every [kind of] tearing.
items.ma-2781: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I observed the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I saw him holding [his arms] apart, and I saw the whiteness of his armpits.
items.ma-2782:
Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us, Ismāʿīl – meaning Ibn Zakariyyā – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn ʿUthmān –, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alighted at Marr al-Ẓahrān on his ʿumrah, it reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Quraysh were saying: They do not rouse themselves from leanness. His Companions said: If we were to slaughter by naḥr some of our mounts, and eat of its meat and sip of its broth, would we be, tomorrow when we enter upon the people, with vigour in us? He said: “Do not do that, but gather for me from your provisions.” So they gathered for him, and spread out the leather mats, and they ate until they turned away, and each one of them scooped into his bag. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced until he entered the mosque, and Quraysh sat near al-Ḥijr. He performed iḍṭibāʿ with his cloak, then said: “Let the people not see any weakness in you.” Then he touched the Corner, then went on, until when he was hidden behind the Yamānī Corner, he walked to the Black Corner. Quraysh said: They are not content with walking; they are leaping like gazelles. So he did that for three circuits, and it became a sunnah.
Abū al-Ṭufayl said: And Ibn ʿAbbās informed me: that the Prophet ﷺ “did that in the Farewell Ḥajj.
items.ma-2783: Surayj narrated to us, Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Mālik al-Nukrī, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A beautiful woman used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Some of the people would go forward in the first row so that they would not see her, and some of them would hang back until he was in the rear row, and when he bowed, he would look from beneath his armpits. So Allah sent down concerning her: {And We have certainly known those of you who have gone forward, and We have certainly known those who lag behind} [al-Ḥijr: 24].
items.ma-2784: Surayj narrated to us, ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Hilāl, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman from the Jews gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a poisoned sheep as a gift, so he sent for her and said: “What made you do what you did?” She said: I wished – or I intended – that if you were a prophet, then Allah would make you aware of it, and if you were not a prophet, I would give the people rest from you! He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he felt anything of that, would have himself cupped. He said: So he travelled once, and when he entered iḥrām, he felt something of that, so he had himself cupped.
items.ma-2785: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Abū Uways narrated to us, Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Muzanī narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī the mines of al-Qabaliyyah: its highlands and its lowlands, and wherever is suitable for cultivation of Qudus, and he did not give him the right of a Muslim. And the Prophet ﷺ wrote for him: “In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, gave to Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī; he gave him the mines of al-Qabaliyyah: its highlands and its lowlands, and wherever is suitable for cultivation of Qudus, and he did not give him the right of a Muslim.”
items.ma-2786: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Abū Uways narrated to us, he said: Thawr ibn Zayd, a mawlā of Banū al-Dīl ibn Bakr ibn Kinānah, narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-2787: Surayj and Yūnus both said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions performed ʿumrah from Jiʿirrānah, and they performed ramal around the House for three [circuits], and walked four.
items.ma-2788: Surayj narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He gives ṣadaqah of a dīnār, and if he does not find a dīnār, then half a dīnār.”
items.ma-2789: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ismāʿīl – meaning Ibn Jaʿfar – narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad – meaning Ibn Abī Ḥarmalah – informed me, from Kurayb: that Umm al-Faḍl bint al-Ḥārith sent him to Muʿāwiyah in al-Shām. He said: So I came to al-Shām and fulfilled her need, and the crescent of Ramaḍān appeared to me while I was in al-Shām, and we saw the crescent on the night of Friday. Then I came to al-Madīnah at the end of the month, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās asked me, then mentioned the crescent, and said: When did you see the crescent? I said: We saw it on the night of Friday. He said: Did you see it? I said: Yes, and the people saw it and fasted, and Muʿāwiyah fasted. He said: But we saw it on the night of Saturday, so we will keep fasting until we complete thirty or see it. I said: Do you not suffice with the sighting of Muʿāwiyah and his fasting? He said: No, thus the Prophet ﷺ commanded us.
items.ma-2790: Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl informed us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind informed me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whomever Allah wishes good for, He gives him understanding in the religion.”
items.ma-2791: Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind, he said: Thawr narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to turn in his prayer to the right and to the left, and did not twist his neck.
items.ma-2792:
Surayj and Yūnus both said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions performed ʿumrah from Jiʿrānah, and they performed iḍṭibāʿ with their cloaks beneath their armpits.
Yūnus narrated to us: They put their cloaks – Yūnus said: and they threw them over their left shoulders.
items.ma-2793: Surayj and Yūnus both said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Quraysh said: Muḥammad and his Companions, the fever of Yathrib has weakened them. So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in the year in which he performed ʿumrah, he said to his Companions: “Perform ramal around the House for three [circuits], so that the polytheists see your strength.” When they performed ramal, Quraysh said: It has not weakened them.
items.ma-2794: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl went with Ibrāhīm to Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, and Shayṭān appeared before him, so he threw seven pebbles at him, and he sank into the ground. Then he came with him to the middle Jamrah, and Shayṭān appeared before him, so he threw seven pebbles at him, and he sank into the ground. Then he came with him to the farthest Jamrah, and Shayṭān appeared before him, so he threw seven pebbles at him, and he sank into the ground. Then when Ibrāhīm wished to slaughter his son Isḥāq, he said to his father: O my father, bind me so that I do not struggle, and some of my blood splashes upon you when you slaughter me. So he bound him, and when he took the knife and wished to slaughter him, a call was made from behind him: {That, O Ibrāhīm, you have already confirmed the vision} [al-Ṣāffāt: 105].”
