items.ma-2795: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Black Stone is from Paradise, and it was whiter than snow, until the sins of the people of shirk blackened it.”
items.ma-2796: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Stone will surely be raised on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which it sees, and a tongue with which it speaks, and it will bear witness on whoever touched it in truth.”
items.ma-2797: Muʾammal narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, and he mentioned it, except that he said: “The Corner will be raised.”
items.ma-2798: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “I was commanded to use the siwāk, until I thought that a Qurʾān, or revelation, would come down upon me concerning it.” The Prophet ﷺ is the one who said this.
items.ma-2799: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer on the day of Friday: {Alif Lām Mīm. The sending down} – al-Sajdah – and {Has there come upon man a period of time}.
items.ma-2800: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Shuʿbah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās: that Ibn ʿAbbās, when he performed ghusl from janābah, would pour with his right hand over the left and wash it seven [times], before putting it into the vessel. Once he forgot how many times he had poured over his hand, so he asked me: How many did I pour? I said: I do not know! He said: May you have no mother! And why do you not know? Then he performed wuḍūʾ, his wuḍūʾ for the prayer, then he would pour water over his head and his body. He said: Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to purify himself, meaning perform ghusl.
items.ma-2801: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When Allah ﷿ sent down: {And warn your closest kinsfolk} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 214], he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to al-Ṣafā and climbed up on it, then called: “Alas, the morning!” So the people gathered to him, between a man who came to him and a man who sent his messenger. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, O Banū Fihr, O sons, O sons, what do you think: if I informed you that cavalry at the foot of this mountain were intending to raid you, would you believe me?” They said: Yes. He said: “Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.” Abū Lahab said: May you perish for the rest of the day! Did you call us only for this? So Allah ﷿ sent down: {May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and he has perished}.
items.ma-2802: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informed me, claiming that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ distributed sheep among his Companions on the Day of Sacrifice, and said: “Slaughter them for your ʿumrah, for they suffice for you.” And a billy goat fell to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
items.ma-2803: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Kahmas ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Furāfiṣah – Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And I had seen him on a road, and he greeted me, while I was a boy – he raised it to Ibn ʿAbbās, or he traced it back to Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: And Hammām ibn Yaḥyā Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the companion of al-Baṣrī, narrated to us, he traced it back to Ibn ʿAbbās. And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah and Nāfiʿ ibn Yazīd, the two Egyptians, narrated to me, from Qays ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Ḥanash al-Ṣanʿānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās – and I do not retain the narration of some of them apart from others – that he said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “O boy – or O little boy – shall I not teach you words by which Allah will benefit you?” I said: Yes. He said: “Guard Allah, He will guard you; guard Allah, you will find Him in front of you. Make yourself known to Him in ease, He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah, and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has dried with what will be. If all of creation together wished to benefit you with something that Allah has not written for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they wished to harm you with something that Allah has not written for you, they would not be able to do it. And know that in patience over what you dislike there is much good, and that victory is with patience, and that relief is with distress, and that with hardship there is ease.”
items.ma-2804: al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came, I and a boy of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, on a donkey, while the Prophet ﷺ was in prayer. He said: So we let it loose in front of us to graze, and he did not break [his prayer]. He said: And two girls of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came, racing each other. The Prophet ﷺ separated between them, and he did not break [his prayer]; and a kid fell, and he did not break [his prayer].
items.ma-2805: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ bathed from janābah, and the Prophet ﷺ came to bathe from what remained of it, and she said: I bathed from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, water is not made impure by anything.”
items.ma-2806: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Water is not made impure by anything.”
items.ma-2807: My father said in his ḥadīth: Wakīʿ narrated it to us in “al-Muṣannaf”, from Sufyān, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, then afterward he made it from Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-2808: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “ʿUmrah in Ramaḍān equals a Ḥajj.”
items.ma-2809: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: And Ḥajjāj informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-2810: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Yaḥyā – meaning Ibn Abī Isḥāq –, from Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, I am a man who forms these pictures and makes these images, so give me a ruling concerning them. He said: Come near me. So he came near him. He said: Come near me. So he came near him, until he placed his hand on his head. He said: Shall I inform you of what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Every picture-maker is in the Fire; for every picture he made, a soul is made for him that punishes him in Jahannam.” So if you must do it, make trees and what has no soul.
items.ma-2811:
Muḥammad ibn Maymūn al-Zaʿfarānī narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar narrated to me, from his father, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, he said: Najdah wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about five matters. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The people claim that Ibn ʿAbbās corresponds with the Ḥarūriyyah, and were it not that I fear concealing my knowledge, I would not write to him. Najdah wrote to him: Now then, inform me: did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ go on expeditions with women with him? And did he allot them a share? And did he kill boys? And when does the orphanhood of the orphan end? And inform me about the khumus, for whom is it?
So Ibn ʿAbbās wrote to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used indeed to go on expeditions with women with him, and they would treat the sick; and he did not allot them a share, but he would give them a gift from the spoils. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill boys, and do not kill boys, unless you know what al-Khaḍir knew of the boy whom he killed, so that you kill the disbeliever and leave the believer. And you wrote asking me about the orphanhood of the orphan, when does it end? By my life, a man's beard grows while he is weak in taking for himself; so when he takes for himself from what is sound of what people take, then orphanhood has gone. And as for the khumus, we used to think that it was ours, but our people refused that to us.
items.ma-2812: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: Mālik, from Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, from Ṭāwūs, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he came to the prayer in the middle of the night, would say: “O Allah, to You is the praise; You are al-Nūr of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is the praise; You are al-Qayyām of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is the praise; You are Rabb of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; and to You is the praise; You are al-Ḥaqq, and Your word is true, and Your promise is true, and Your meeting is true, and Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, and in You I have believed, and upon You I have relied, and to You I have turned in repentance, and by You I have disputed, and to You I have referred judgment; so forgive me what I have put forward and what I have held back, and what I have concealed and what I have declared. You are my deity, there is no deity except You.”
items.ma-2813: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Zāʾidah. And ʿAbd al-Ṣamad: Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray on the small mat.
items.ma-2814: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed among poetry there is wisdom, and indeed among eloquence there is sorcery.”
items.ma-2815: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ delayed the ṭawāf on the Day of Sacrifice until night.
items.ma-2816: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from ʿAmr – meaning Ibn Abī ʿAmr –, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever alters the boundary markers of the land; and may Allah curse whoever leads the blind astray from the path; and may Allah curse whoever reviles his father; and may Allah curse whoever attaches himself to other than his mawālī; and may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ; and may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ; and may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ.”
items.ma-2817: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade blowing into food and drink.
items.ma-2818: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “No man who believes in Allah and His Messenger hates the Anṣār.” Or: “Except that Abghaḍahu Allāh wa-Rasūluh.”
items.ma-2819:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Rawḥ – the meaning [being the same] – both said: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When it was the night I was taken by night, and I woke in the morning in Makkah, I was distressed about my affair, and I knew that the people would belie me.” So he sat apart, sorrowful. He said: Then the enemy of Allah, Abū Jahl, passed by him, and came and sat by him, and said to him, like one mocking: Has anything happened? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Yes.” He said: What is it? He said: “I was taken by night last night.” He said: To where? He said: “To Bayt al-Maqdis.” He said: Then you woke in the morning among us?! He said: “Yes.” He said: He did not let him see that he was belying him, for fear that he would deny him the account if he called his people to him. He said: What do you think, if I call your people, will you tell them what you told me? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Yes.” So he said: Come, O company of Banū Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy. Until he said: Then the gatherings stirred toward him, and they came until they sat with the two of them. He said: Tell your people what you told me.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was taken by night last night.” They said: To where? He said: “To Bayt al-Maqdis.” They said: Then you woke in the morning among us?! He said: “Yes.” He said: Then among them were one who clapped, and one who put his hand on his head, wondering at the lie, he claimed!! They said: And are you able to describe the mosque to us? And among the people were those who had travelled to that town and seen the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “So I went to describe it, and I kept describing until some of the description became confused for me.” He said: “Then the mosque was brought while I was looking, until it was set down by the house of ʿIqāl – or ʿUqayl – and I described it while I was looking at it.” He said: “And with this there was a description that I did not retain.” He said: “And the people said: As for the description, by Allah, he has got it right.”
items.ma-2820: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When Firʿawn said: {I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom Banū Isrāʾīl believe} [Yūnus: 90], he said: Jibrīl said to me: O Muḥammad, if only you had seen me when I took some mud from the mud of the sea and thrust it into his mouth, for fear that mercy would reach him.”
items.ma-2821:
Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When it was the night in which I was taken by night, a pleasant fragrance came upon me, and I said: O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance? He said: This is the fragrance of the hairdresser of Firʿawn's daughter and her children. He said: I said: And what is her story? He said: While she was combing the hair of Firʿawn's daughter one day, the comb fell from her hand, and she said: In the name of Allah. Firʿawn's daughter said to her: My father? She said: No, but my Rabb and the Rabb of your father is Allah. She said: I will tell him that! She said: Yes. So she told him, and he called her and said: O so-and-so, do you have a master other than me? She said: Yes, my Rabb and your Rabb is Allah. So he ordered a cow of copper, and it was heated, then he ordered that she and her children be thrown into it. She said to him: I have a need of you. He said: And what is your need? She said: I would like you to gather my bones and the bones of my children in one cloth, and bury us. He said: That is yours from us by right. He said: Then he ordered that her children be thrown before her, one by one, until it came to a suckling child of hers, as if she hesitated because of him. He said: O mother, plunge in, for the punishment of the world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. So she plunged in.”
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Four little ones spoke: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﵇, and the companion of Jurayj, and the witness of Yūsuf, and the son of the hairdresser of Firʿawn's daughter.
items.ma-2822: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken by night, a pleasant fragrance passed by him … then he mentioned something like it.
items.ma-2823: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken by night, a pleasant fragrance passed by him … then he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: Who is your Rabb? She said: My Rabb and your Rabb is Man fī al-samāʾ. And he did not mention the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: Four spoke.
items.ma-2824: Hudbah ibn Khālid narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, something like it.
items.ma-2825: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Zayd narrated to us, al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī narrated to me, narrating it from Ibn ʿAbbās, narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whichever man dislikes something from his commander, let him be patient; for there is no one of the people who departs from the authority by a span and dies, except that he dies a death of Jāhiliyyah.”
items.ma-2826: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān informed us, Abū Rajāʾ narrated to us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Whoever sees from his commander something he dislikes …” then he mentioned something like it.
items.ma-2827: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Zayd narrated to us, al-Jaʿd Abū ʿUthmān narrated to us, he said: Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, narrating it from the Prophet ﷺ, narrating it from his Rabb ﷿, he said: “Indeed Allah wrote the good deeds and the evil deeds. So whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, Allah writes it with Him as a complete good deed; and if he does it, Allah writes it as ten, up to seven hundred, up to many multiples – or: up to what Allah wills to multiply. And whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, Allah writes it for him with Him as a complete good deed; and if he does it, Allah writes it as one evil deed.”
items.ma-2828: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a mawlā of the family of Ṭalḥah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my sister vowed to perform Ḥajj walking? He said: “Allah will do nothing with the hardship of your sister; let her go out riding, and let her offer kaffārah for her oath.”
items.ma-2829: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, he said: Qatādah informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulated the House seven [times], and hastened a hastening, and he hastened only [because] he wished to show the people his strength.
items.ma-2830: Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: He used to dislike unripe dates alone, and he would say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays from al-muzzāʾ, and I dread that it is the unripe dates.
items.ma-2831: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to al-Madīnah and saw the Jews fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and said to them: “What is this day on which you fast?” They said: This is a righteous day; this is a day on which Allah saved Banū Isrāʾīl from their enemy, so Mūsā ﵇ fasted it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am more deserving of Mūsā than you.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted it, and commanded fasting it.
items.ma-2832: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ayyūb narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked on the Day of Sacrifice; it was said: O Messenger of Allah, a man slaughtered before he threw [the pebbles], or shaved before he slaughtered. He said: “There is no harm.” He said: So he was not asked on that day about anything except that he would grasp with his two palms as though he were throwing with them, and say: “There is no harm, there is no harm.”
items.ma-2833: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Kaʿbah, and in it were six pillars, and he stood at each pillar and supplicated, and did not pray in it.
items.ma-2834: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān – the meaning [being the same] – both said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the sister of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir vowed to perform Ḥajj walking, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ is free of need of the vow of your sister; let her ride, and let her present a badanah.”
items.ma-2835: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān both said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulated seven [times], and circumambulated hastening, and he circumambulated only to show the polytheists his strength. And ʿAffān said: And for this the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to show the people his strength.
items.ma-2836:
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū Mijlaz, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the witr, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “One rakʿah from the end of the night.”
And I asked Ibn ʿUmar? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “One rakʿah from the end of the night.”
items.ma-2837: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn Shihāb al-ʿAnbarī narrated to us, he said: I heard my father say: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās, I and a companion of mine, and we met Abū Hurayrah at the door of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Who are you two? We informed him. He said: Go to people [who live] on dates and water; every valley flows only according to its measure. He said: We said: May your goodness be abundant; ask permission for us to see Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: So he asked permission for us, and we heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon on the day of Tabūk, and said: “There is not among the people the like of a man holding the rein of his horse, striving in the path of Allah, and avoiding the evils of people; and the like of a man in the desert with his sheep, who entertains his guest and fulfils his right.” He said: I said: Did he say it? He said: He said it. He said: I said: Did he say it? He said: He said it. He said: I said: Did he say it? He said: He said it. So I magnified Allah, and praised Allah, and gave thanks.
items.ma-2838: Rawḥ narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them this supplication as he taught them a sūrah of the Qurʾān, saying: “Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Jahannam, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl, and I seek refuge in You from the fitnah of life and death.”
items.ma-2839: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: A badanah is upon me, and I am well-off for it, but I do not find it so that I may buy it? So the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to buy seven sheep and slaughter them.
items.ma-2840: Rawḥ narrated to us, Abū Mālik ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mughīth, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever acquires a knowledge from the stars acquires a branch of sorcery; as much as he increases, it increases, and as much as he increases, it increases.”
items.ma-2841: Rawḥ narrated to us, al-Thawrī narrated to us, Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of al-Muzdalifah – the little boys of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib – on our donkeys, and he began patting our thighs with his hand and saying: “O my sons, do not throw the jamrah until the sun rises.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not think anyone throws the jamrah until the sun rises.
items.ma-2842: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl – thus Rawḥ said: ʿĀṣim, and the people say: Abū ʿĀṣim – he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Your people claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ṭawāf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a camel, and that that is a sunnah? He said: They spoke truth and they lied. I said: What did they speak truth about and what did they lie about? He said: He did perform ṭawāf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a camel, and that is not a sunnah. The people were not turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor pushed back, so he performed ṭawāf on a camel so that they would listen, and see his place, and their hands would not reach him.
items.ma-2843: Yazīd narrated to me, he said: Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded the one who comes to his wife while she is menstruating to give ṣadaqah of a dīnār, or of half a dīnār.
items.ma-2844: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to say: “There is no ṣarūrah in Islam.”
items.ma-2845: Abū Kāmil and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us – Ḥasan said: from ʿAmmār; Ḥammād said: and I think it was from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ḥasan did not doubt it – he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said. And ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, mursal, Ibn ʿAbbās not being in it: that the Prophet ﷺ said to Khadījah … then ʿAffān mentioned the ḥadīth, and Abū Kāmil and Ḥasan said in their narration: that the Prophet ﷺ said to Khadījah: “Indeed I see a light and hear a voice, and I fear that there is madness in me.” She said: Allah would not do that to you, O son of ʿAbd Allāh. Then she went to Waraqah ibn Nawfal and mentioned that to him, and he said: If he is truthful, then this is a nāmūs like the nāmūs of Mūsā; if he is sent while I am alive, I will support him, and aid him, and believe in him.
items.ma-2846: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah fifteen years: seven years seeing the brightness and the light and hearing the voice, and eight years being sent revelation; and he stayed in al-Madīnah ten.
items.ma-2847:
Abū Kāmil and ʿAffān – the meaning [being the same] – both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I was with my father at the Prophet ﷺ, and with him was a man conversing privately with him – ʿAffān said: and he was like one turning away from al-ʿAbbās – so we went out from him, and he said: Have you not seen your cousin, as if turning away from me? I said: A man was with him, conversing privately with him – ʿAffān said: So he said: Was there anyone with him? I said: Yes. – He said: So he returned to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, was anyone with you? For ʿAbd Allāh informed me that you had a man with you conversing privately with you. He said: “Did you see him, O ʿAbd Allāh?” He said: Yes. He said: “That was Jibrīl, and he is the one who occupied me from you.”
ʿAffān narrated to us: that there was with you a man conversing privately with you ….
items.ma-2848: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Hudbah ibn Khālid narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, something like it.
items.ma-2849:
Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from Ibn ʿAbbās – as Ḥammād reckons –: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Khadījah, and her father was inclined to marry her to him. So she made food and drink, and invited her father and some men of Quraysh, and they ate and drank until they became intoxicated. Khadījah said to her father: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh is proposing to me, so marry me to him. So he married her to him, and she smeared him with khalūq and clothed him in a ḥullah – and thus they used to do with fathers. When his intoxication was lifted from him, he looked, and behold, he was smeared with khalūq and was wearing a ḥullah. He said: What is my matter, what is this? She said: You married me to Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh. He said: I marry [her to] the orphan of Abū Ṭālib! No, by my life.
Khadījah said: Have you no shame! Do you want to make yourself look foolish before Quraysh, telling the people that you were drunk? She did not cease with him until he was content.
items.ma-2850: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us, from Ibn ʿAbbās – as he reckons –: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Khadījah bint Khuwaylid … then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-2851: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed me, he said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: A badanah is upon me, and I am well-off for it, but I do not find it so that I may buy it? So the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to buy seven sheep and slaughter them.
items.ma-2852: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah informed me, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he mentioned the Prophet ﷺ: that he mentioned al-Dajjāl, he said: “He is one-eyed, hijān, as if his head were an aṣalah; the most similar of your men to him is ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qaṭan. So if the doomed perish, then indeed your Rabb ﷿ is not one-eyed.”
items.ma-2853: Muḥammad ibn Bakr and ʿAbd al-Razzāq both said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abū al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Ṭāwūs saying: We said to Ibn ʿAbbās, about the iqʿāʾ upon the two feet? He said: It is the sunnah. He said: We said: We consider it a roughness toward the foot. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2854: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek out a day, seeking its excellence over any other, except this day – the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ – or the month of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-2855: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Ṭāwūs, he said: I saw Ibn ʿAbbās kneeling on the fronts of his feet, and I said: The people claim that this is from roughness. He said: It is the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-2856: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade only the solid garment of silk.
items.ma-2857: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Khuṣayf informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade only the solid garment.
items.ma-2858:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Jibrīl made me recite upon one ḥarf, so I went back to him, and I did not cease asking him for more and he increasing me, and it ended at seven aḥruf.”
Al-Zuhrī said: These aḥruf are only in the one matter, and it does not differ in what is lawful or what is unlawful.
items.ma-2859: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed among poetry there are wisdoms, and indeed among eloquence there is sorcery.”
items.ma-2860: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Divide the property among the people of the farāʾiḍ according to the Book of Allah ﵎; and whatever the farāʾiḍ leave, is for the nearest male.”
items.ma-2861: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in two white cloaks and a red cloak.
items.ma-2862: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: That one of you grant his brother his land is better for him than that he take for it such and such, for something specified. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: And it is al-ḥaql, which in the tongue of the Anṣār is al-muḥāqalah.
items.ma-2863: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar and ʿUthmān likewise, and the first to forbid it was Muʿāwiyah.
items.ma-2864: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, its meaning, with its isnād.
items.ma-2865: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no harm and no inflicting of harm; and a man may place a beam in the wall of his neighbour; and the frequented road is seven cubits.”
items.ma-2866:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAṭāʾ informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: If you are able that none of you go out on the day of Fiṭr until he has eaten, let him do so.
He said: So I have not ceased to eat before I go out, since I heard that from Ibn ʿAbbās; I eat a bite from the end of the ṣarīqah, or drink milk or water. I said: And how is this interpreted? He said: He heard it – I think from the Prophet ﷺ – he said: They would not go out until the forenoon had extended, and they would say: We eat so that we are not hurried from our prayer.
items.ma-2867: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī informed us, from Ismāʿīl – he is Abū Isrāʾīl al-Mulāʾī –, from Fuḍayl – meaning Ibn ʿAmr –, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Hasten to the Ḥajj – meaning the obligatory one – for none of you knows what may befall him.”
items.ma-2868: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions when they wished to enter Makkah on his ʿumrah, after al-Ḥudaybiyah: “Your people will see you tomorrow, so let them see you strong.” When they entered the mosque they touched the Corner, then performed ramal, with the Prophet ﷺ among them, until when they reached the Yamānī Corner, they walked to the Black Corner. So he did that three times, then walked the four.
items.ma-2869: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl informed us. And Abū Nuʿaym: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled, concerning the rikāz, [that there be] the khumus.
items.ma-2870: Aswad narrated it to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, he said: And ruled – and Abū Nuʿaym said in his narration: ruled – the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, concerning the rikāz, [that there be] the khumus.
items.ma-2871: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man does not come into direct contact with a man, nor a woman with a woman.”
items.ma-2872: ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: And Aswad did not raise it, and he narrated it to us from Ḥasan, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, mursal.
items.ma-2873: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ when he had finished with Badr: [Take] the caravan, there is nothing before it. He said: Then al-ʿAbbās called out to him while he was a captive in his bonds: It is not fitting. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Why?” He said: Because Allah promised you one of the two groups, and He has given you what He promised you.
items.ma-2874: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Māʿiz was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he confessed before him twice, and he said: “Take him away.” Then he said: “Bring him back.” And he confessed twice, until he confessed four times, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Take him away and stone him.”
items.ma-2875: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Divorce, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of Abū Bakr and for two years of the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb – the divorce of three – was one. ʿUmar said: The people have hastened in a matter in which they had deliberation; so if only we were to carry it through upon them. So he carried it through upon them.
items.ma-2876: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, he said: al-Faraj ibn Faḍālah narrated to us, from Abū Harim, from Ṣadaqah al-Dimashqī, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about fasting. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “Among the best of fasting is the fasting of my brother Dāwūd; he used to fast a day and break the fast a day.”
items.ma-2877: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ, and Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān; and the first to forbid it was Muʿāwiyah.
items.ma-2878: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from his brother, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ wished to perform wuḍūʾ from a waterskin, and it was said to him: It is carrion. He said: “Its tanning removes its filth, or its foulness, or its impurity.”
items.ma-2879: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, he said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand between my shoulders – or he said: on my shoulders – and said: “O Allah, give him understanding in the religion, and teach him the interpretation.”
items.ma-2880: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered by naḥr in the Ḥajj a hundred badanahs; he slaughtered sixty of them with his own hand, and commanded the rest, and they were slaughtered; and he took a piece from every badanah, and they were gathered in a pot, and he ate of it and sipped of its broth. And he slaughtered by naḥr on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah seventy, among them the camel of Abū Jahl; and when it was barred from the House, it yearned as it yearns for its young.
items.ma-2881: Abū al-Jawwāb narrated to us, ʿAmmār – meaning Ibn Ruzayq – narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drove a hundred badanahs … then he mentioned something like it.
items.ma-2882: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, from Ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the year of the Conquest when ten [nights] of Ramaḍān had passed, and when he alighted at Marr al-Ẓahrān ….
items.ma-2883: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Abū al-Naḍr both said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah in the year of the Conquest seventeen [days], praying two rakʿahs. Abū al-Naḍr said: shortening, praying two rakʿahs.
items.ma-2884: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn al-Kharrāz – of the trustworthy – narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us. And Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, he said: My father informed me, from Sharīk, from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, something like it.
items.ma-2885: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a mawlā of the family of Ṭalḥah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, raising it to him, that he said: “Let her ride, and let her expiate her oath.”
items.ma-2886: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Sayf ibn Sulaymān al-Makkī informed us, Qays ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled with the witness and the oath.
items.ma-2887: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Qāriẓ ibn Shaybah, from Abū Ghaṭafān, he said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās and found him performing wuḍūʾ; he rinsed his mouth, then sniffed water into his nose, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Twice – or two thorough [times] –, or three [times].”
items.ma-2888: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī narrated to us, he said: Ḥabīb ibn al-Shahīd narrated to me, Maymūn ibn Mihrān narrated to me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2889: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū ʿUlwān, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: Fifty prayers were made obligatory upon your Prophet ﷺ, so he asked his Rabb ﷿, and He made them five.
items.ma-2890: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿIṣm, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: Your Prophet ﷺ was commanded with fifty prayers, so he asked his Rabb, and He made them five prayers.
items.ma-2891: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿIṣm, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Allah ﷿ made the prayer obligatory upon His Prophet ﷺ as fifty prayers, so he asked his Rabb ﷿, and He made them five prayers.
items.ma-2892: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us the tashahhud as he used to teach us a sūrah of the Qurʾān.
items.ma-2893: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, he said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to use the siwāk, until I feared that it would be revealed to me concerning it.”
items.ma-2894: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and Khalaf ibn al-Walīd both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The righteous dream is one part of seventy parts of prophethood.”
items.ma-2895: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Kāmil ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Ibn ʿAbbās, or from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said between the two prostrations in the night prayer: “O Rabb, forgive me, and have mercy on me, and raise me, and provide for me, and guide me.” Then he prostrated.
items.ma-2896: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the conquest of Makkah: “Indeed this land is sacred; Allah made it sacred. Killing was not made lawful in it for anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me for an hour; so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection: its game is not to be startled, its thorns are not to be cut off, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who will announce it, and its grass is not to be cut.” Al-ʿAbbās said: O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir, for it is for their houses and for their smiths. He said: “Except the idhkhir. And there is no hijrah, but jihād and intention; and when you are called to go forth, go forth.”
items.ma-2897: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Ḥaywah narrated to us, Mālik ibn Khayr al-Zibādī informed me that Mālik ibn Saʿd al-Tujībī narrated to him that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Jibrīl came to me and said: O Muḥammad, indeed Allah ﷿ cursed khamr, and its presser, and the one who has it pressed, and its drinker, and its carrier, and the one to whom it is carried, and its seller, and its buyer, and the one who serves it, and the one who has it served.”
items.ma-2898: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah ibn ʿUqbah al-Ḥaḍramī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah al-Sabaʾī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās saying: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about Sabaʾ, what it is: a man, or a woman, or a land? He said: “Rather he is a man who begot ten; six of them settled in al-Yaman, and four of them in al-Shām. As for the Yamanīs: Madhḥij, Kindah, al-Azd, the Ashʿarīs, Anmār and Ḥimyar, all of them ʿarbāʾ; and as for the Shāmīs: Lakhm, Judhām, ʿĀmilah and Ghassān.”
items.ma-2899: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying, and two girls came until they stood in front of him, by his head, so he pushed them away, and gestured with his two hands to his right and to his left.
items.ma-2900: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a mawlā of the family of Ṭalḥah, narrated to us, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The name of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed her name and named her Juwayriyah.
items.ma-2901: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Dāwūd narrated to us, from ʿIlbāʾ, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew four lines on the ground, and said: “Do you know what this is?” They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of the women of the people of Paradise are Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, and Maryam bint ʿImrān, and Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim, the wife of Firʿawn.”
items.ma-2902: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth informed us, ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Shuʿbah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, or Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās passed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Rabīʿah while he was praying with his hair plaited, knotted behind him, so he stood by him and did not cease undoing the knots of his hair, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith acquiesced to him until he finished undoing it, then he sat. When Ibn al-Ḥārith finished the prayer, he came to him and said: Why did you do to my head what you did just now?! He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The likeness of the one who prays with his head knotted behind him is like the likeness of the one who prays tied up.”
items.ma-2903: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Bukayr, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “The likeness of the one who prays with his head knotted is like the likeness of the one who prays while tied up.”
items.ma-2904: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Jābir, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ had himself cupped three [times] at the two veins of the neck and between the two shoulders, and gave the cupper his wage; and had it been ḥarām, he would not have given it to him.
items.ma-2905: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr with three: with {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, and {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-2906: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer on the day of Friday: {Alif Lām Mīm. The sending down} – al-Sajdah – and {Has there come upon man}.
items.ma-2907: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ prostrating, having held [his arms] apart, until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.
items.ma-2908: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I observed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw him prostrating, holding [his arms] apart, and I saw the whiteness of his armpits.
items.ma-2909: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, raising it to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Every alliance that was in the Jāhiliyyah, Islam has added to it only strength, or sharpness.”
items.ma-2910: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Any slave-woman who bears from her master is one set free in the wake of him” – or he said: “after him” – and sometimes he said both of them together.
items.ma-2911: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he commanded ʿAlī, so he set out [water for] ghusl for him, then he gave him a garment, and said: “Screen me, and turn your back to me.”
items.ma-2912: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who raised it to the Prophet ﷺ; he said: “If you disagree about the road, make it seven cubits; and whoever his neighbour asks him to prop [a beam] upon his wall, let him do so.”
items.ma-2913: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah curse whoever changes the boundary-markers of the land; may Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever curses his parents; may Allah curse whoever takes as patron other than his own mawālī; may Allah curse whoever leads a blind man astray from the path; may Allah curse whoever has intercourse with an animal; may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ; may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ” – three times.
items.ma-2914: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, the mawlā of al-Muṭṭalib, narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Cursed is whoever reviles his father; cursed is whoever reviles his mother; cursed is whoever slaughters for other than Allah; cursed is whoever changes the boundary-markers of the land; cursed is whoever leads a blind man astray from the road; cursed is whoever has intercourse with an animal; cursed is whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said it repeatedly, three times, concerning al-lūṭiyyah.
items.ma-2915: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah curse whoever changes the boundary-markers of the land; may Allah curse whoever takes as patron other than his own mawālī; may Allah curse whoever leads a blind man astray from the road; may Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever has intercourse with an animal; may Allah curse whoever is undutiful to his parents; may Allah curse whoever does the deed of the people of Lūṭ.” He said it three times.
items.ma-2916: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded with the two rakʿahs of Ḍuḥā, and you were not commanded with them; and I was commanded with the Aḍḥā, and it was not prescribed.”
items.ma-2917: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The naḥr was prescribed for me, and it was not prescribed for you; and I was commanded with the two rakʿahs of Ḍuḥā, and you were not commanded with them.”
items.ma-2918: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, the mawlā of Ibn ʿUqayl al-Anṣārī, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I was taught a verse of the Qurʾān about which no man has ever asked me, and I do not know whether the people knew it and so did not ask about it, or did not grasp it so that they should ask about it! Then he began to narrate to us; and when he rose, we blamed one another for not having asked him about it. So I said: I am for it when he goes out tomorrow afternoon. Then when he went out the next afternoon, I said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, you mentioned yesterday that there is a verse of the Qurʾān about which no man has ever asked you, and you do not know whether the people knew it and so did not ask about it, or did not grasp it. And I said: Inform me about it, and about those [verses] that you recited before it. He said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Quraysh: “O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one who is worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.” And Quraysh knew that the Christians worship ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and what they say about Muḥammad. So they said: O Muḥammad, do you not claim that ʿĪsā was a prophet and a righteous servant from among the servants of Allah? Then if you are truthful, their gods are indeed as you say. He said: So Allah ﷿ sent down: {And when the son of Maryam was set forth as an example, behold, your people from it yaṣiddūn} [al-Zukhruf: 57]. He said: I said: What is yaṣiddūn? He said: They clamour. {And indeed he is a knowledge of the Hour} [al-Zukhruf: 61]. He said: It is the coming out of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﵇ before the Day of Resurrection.
items.ma-2919: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, he said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the courtyard of his house in Makkah, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn passed by him and smiled broadly at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Will you not sit?” He said: Yes indeed. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat facing him, and while he was talking with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his gaze to the sky, and looked at the sky for a while. Then he began to lower his gaze until he set it down on his right on the ground, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from his companion ʿUthmān towards where he had set his gaze, and began to nod his head as though he were seeking to understand what was being said to him, while Ibn Maẓʿūn watched. Then when he had finished his need and had grasped what was being said to him, the gaze of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to the sky as it had risen the first time, and he followed it with his gaze until it vanished into the sky. Then he turned to ʿUthmān in his first sitting position. He said: O Muḥammad, for what have I been sitting with you and coming to you? I have not seen you do the like of what you did this morning! He said: “And what did you see me do?” He said: I saw you raise your gaze to the sky, then set it where you set it, on your right, and you turned towards it and left me, and you began to nod your head as though you were seeking to understand something that was being said to you. He said: “And you noticed that?” ʿUthmān said: Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The messenger of Allah came to me just now, while you were sitting.” He said: The messenger of Allah?! He said: “Yes.” He said: And what did he say to you? He said: {Indeed Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression; He admonishes you that you may remember} [al-Naḥl: 90]. ʿUthmān said: That was when īmān settled in my heart, and I loved Muḥammad.
items.ma-2920: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For every prophet there is a ḥaram, and my ḥaram is al-Madīnah. O Allah, I declare it ḥarām with Your sanctities: that no muḥdith be sheltered in it, that its fresh grass not be cut, that its thorns not be cut down, and that its luqaṭah not be taken except by one who announces it.”
items.ma-2921: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Any man who claims descent from other than his father, or takes as his patron other than his mawālī who freed him, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and the people, until the Day of Resurrection; no ṣarf and no ʿadl will be accepted from him.”
items.ma-2922: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was forbidden [from] kinds of women, except those who were believing emigrant women. He said: {Women are not lawful for you after [this], nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses} [al-Aḥzāb: 52]. So Allah ﷿ made lawful your believing young women {and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet} [al-Aḥzāb: 50], and He made ḥarām every woman of a religion other than the religion of Islam. He said: {And whoever disbelieves in īmān, his work has become void, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers} [al-Māʾidah: 5]. And He said: {O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their dowries, and what your right hand possesses} up to His saying: {exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the believers} [al-Aḥzāb: 50]. And He made ḥarām other than that of the kinds of women.
items.ma-2923: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed marriage to a woman of his people called Sawdah, who was a woman with young children; she had five or six children from a husband of hers who had died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “What prevents you from me?” She said: By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, what prevents me from you is not that you are not the most beloved of creation to me; but I honour you too much for these children to cry out beside your head, morning and evening. He said: “Is there anything else that prevents you from me, other than that?” She said: No, by Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “May Allah have mercy on you. Indeed the best of women who have ridden the hindquarters of camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them to a child in its smallness, and the most protective of them over a husband with regard to what is in his hand.”
items.ma-2924:
And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in a sitting place of his, and Jibrīl came to him and sat before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, placing his palms on the knees of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me: what is Islam? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Islam is that you submit your face to Allah, and bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone, who has no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.” He said: If I do that, have I submitted? He said: “If you do that, you have submitted.”
He said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me: what is īmān? He said: “Īmān is that you believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and that you believe in death, and in life after death, and that you believe in Paradise and the Fire, the reckoning, and the Scale, and that you believe in al-qadar, all of it, its good and its evil.” He said: If I do that, have I believed? He said: “If you do that, you have believed.”
He said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me: what is iḥsān? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Iḥsān is that you work for Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He Yarāka.” He said: O Messenger of Allah, then tell me: when is the Hour? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Subḥān Allāh! It is among five of the unseen that none knows but Him: {Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed Allah is Knowing, Aware} [Luqmān: 34]. But if you wish, I will tell you of signs of it short of that.” He said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, so tell me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you see the slave-woman give birth to her mistress – or: her master – and you see the owners of sheep competing in the height of buildings, and you see the barefoot, hungry, needy become the heads of the people, then that is among the signs of the Hour and its portents.” He said: O Messenger of Allah, and who are the owners of sheep and the barefoot, hungry, needy? He said: “The Arabs.”
items.ma-2925: Hāshim narrated to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah – meaning Shaybān – narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take good omens and did not take bad omens, and every good name pleased him.
items.ma-2926: Hāshim narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying: {You were the best ummah brought out for the people} [Āl ʿImrān: 110], he said: Those who emigrated with Muḥammad ﷺ to al-Madīnah.
items.ma-2927: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Saʿīd ibn Khālid, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Dhuʾayb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came – or: came out to them – while they were sitting, and said: “Shall I not tell you of the best of people in station?” He said: We said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “A man holding the head of a horse in the way of Allah until he dies or is killed.” Then he said: “Shall I not inform you of the one who follows him?” We said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “A man withdrawn in a mountain pass, who establishes the ṣalāh, gives the zakāh, and keeps away from the evils of the people.” Then he said: “Shall I not inform you of the worst of people in station?” He said: We said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “The one who is asked by Allah and does not give by Him.”
items.ma-2928: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Dhuʾayb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: He came out to them while they were sitting, and said: “Shall I not tell you of the best of people in standing …” and he mentioned it.
items.ma-2929: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the woman and the slave from the spoils what the army received.
items.ma-2930: Ḥusayn narrated it to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to give the slave and the woman from the spoils.
items.ma-2931: Yazīd narrated it to us, he said: from one who heard Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: less than what the army received.
items.ma-2932: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Shuʿbah: that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās to visit him in an illness, and he was wearing a cloak of brocade. He said: O Abū ʿAbbās, what is this garment? He said: And what is it? He said: This is brocade! He said: By Allah, I did not know of it, and I do not think that the Prophet ﷺ forbade this when he forbade it except on account of haughtiness and arrogance, and we, praise be to Allah, are not like that. He said: Then what are these pictures on the brazier? He said: Do you not see that we have burned them with fire? Then when al-Miswar went out, he said: Remove this garment from me, and cut off the heads of these figures. They said: O Abū ʿAbbās, if you took them to the market, would they sell better with the head? He said: No. So he ordered their heads to be cut off.
items.ma-2933: Hāshim narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Shuʿbah, he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: Your mawlā, when he prostrates, places his forehead, his forearms and his chest on the ground. So Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: What makes you do what you do? He said: Humility. He said: This is the crouching of a dog. I saw the Prophet ﷺ, when he prostrated, the whiteness of his armpits was seen.
items.ma-2934: And Ḥusayn narrated it to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-2935: Hāshim narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to send him with his family to Minā on the Day of Sacrifice, so that they might cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah with the dawn.
items.ma-2936: Ḥusayn narrated it to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ sent him with his family to Minā on the Day of Sacrifice, and they cast [pebbles at] the Jamrah with the dawn.
items.ma-2937: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever has intercourse with his slave-woman and she bears him a child, she is freed after [him].”
items.ma-2938: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ḥusayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray in a single garment, draped with it, protecting himself with its excess from the heat of the ground and its cold.
items.ma-2939: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A girl would bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the shoulder [of meat] from the pot, and he would eat from it, then go out to the ṣalāh and pray, and he did not perform wuḍūʾ and did not touch water.
items.ma-2940: Ḥusayn narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on the small mat.
items.ma-2941: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz: that Najdah al-Ḥarūrī, when he went out from the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr, sent to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the share of the kindred: to whom do you see it belonging? He said: It is for us; for the kindred of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ apportioned it to them, and ʿUmar had offered us some of it which we saw to be less than our right, so we returned it to him and refused to accept it. And what he had offered them was: that he would help their one who marries, settle the debt of their debtor, and give to their poor; and he refused to give them more than that.
items.ma-2942: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ used to let his hair hang loose, while the polytheists used to part their hair, and the People of the Book used to let their hair hang loose; and the Prophet ﷺ loved to conform with the People of the Book in what had not been revealed to him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ parted his hair.
items.ma-2943: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no one among the people but that he has erred or intended a sin, not including Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā.”
items.ma-2944: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed me, one of them adding to the other: that a man called out to Ibn ʿAbbās while the people were around him, and said: Is it a sunnah that you seek with this nabīdh? Or is it easier for you than milk and honey?! So Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ came to ʿAbbās and said: “Give us a drink.” He said: Indeed this nabīdh is a drink that has been steeped and mashed; shall we not give you milk or honey to drink? He said: “Give us to drink from what you give the people to drink from.” So he came to the Prophet ﷺ, with his Companions of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār with him, with two waterskins in which was the nabīdh. Then when the Prophet ﷺ drank, he hurried before he was quenched, and raised his head and said: “You have done well; do likewise.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: The pleasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in that is dearer to me than that its mountain passes should flow with milk and honey.
items.ma-2945: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You hear, and it will be heard from you, and it will be heard from those who hear from you.”
items.ma-2946: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Zakariyyā ibn ʿUmar informed me that ʿAṭāʾ informed him: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās invited al-Faḍl on the Day of ʿArafah to a meal, and he said: I am fasting. So ʿAbd Allāh said: Do not fast, for a milk-pail was brought near to the Prophet ﷺ and he drank from it on this day; and the people take you as a model.
items.ma-2947: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never fasted a complete month other than Ramaḍān; and when he fasted, he would fast until the sayer would say: No, by Allah, he will not break his fast; and he would break his fast when he broke it, until the sayer would say: By Allah, he will not fast.
items.ma-2948:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: And in my father's book: from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, from his father, from al-Ḥasan – meaning Ibn Dhakwān –, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade walking in a single khuff or a single sandal.
And in the ḥadīth there is much other speech than this, and he did not narrate it to us; he struck it out in his book. I thought that he left his ḥadīth because he narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, who narrates from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and ʿAmr ibn Khālid is worth nothing.
items.ma-2949: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the mujaththamah, the milk of the jallālah, and drinking from the mouth of the waterskin.
items.ma-2950: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār – narrated to us, Abū Ḥāzim narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl came to me and commanded me to proclaim the talbiyah.”
items.ma-2951: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Khuṣayf informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ only forbade the garment of pure silk; as for a garment whose warp is silk and is not pure silk, we see no harm in it. And the Prophet ﷺ only forbade drinking from a vessel of silver.
items.ma-2952: Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Ḥuṣayn say: I was with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Seventy thousand of my ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning.” So I said: Who are they? He said: “They are those who do not seek ruqyah, do not take bad omens, and do not practise ʿiyāfah, and upon their Rabb they rely.”
items.ma-2953: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Ziyād informed me that Ṣāliḥ, the mawlā of al-Tawʾamah, informed him that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās narrating from the Prophet ﷺ: “Indeed the raḥim is a shujnah taking hold of the ḥujzah of al-Raḥmān; He joins whoever joins it, and cuts off whoever cuts it off.”
items.ma-2954: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning al-ʿAṭṭār – narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ performed four ʿumrahs: the ʿumrah of al-Ḥudaybiyah, the ʿumrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, the third from al-Jiʿirrānah, and the fourth, which was with his Ḥajj.
items.ma-2955: Abū al-Naḍr and Ḥusayn narrated to us, they both said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Ashʿath, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah lā yanẓuru ilā musbil.”
items.ma-2956: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Aʿraj, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Two men disputed, and the oath fell to one of them, so he swore by Allah, other than whom there is no deity, that he had no right against him. Then Jibrīl descended and said: Command him to give him his right, for the right is with him, and he is lying; and the kaffārah of his oath is his knowledge of Allah that there is no deity except Him, or: his testimony that there is no deity except Him.
items.ma-2957: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: ʿIlbāʾ ibn Aḥmar narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew four lines, then said: “Do you know why I drew these lines?” They said: No. He said: “The best of the women of Paradise are four: Maryam bint ʿImrān, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, Fāṭimah the daughter of Muḥammad, and Āsiyah the daughter of Muzāḥim.”
items.ma-2958: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Khālid, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them while they were sitting in a sitting place of theirs, and said: “Shall I not inform you of the best of people?” They said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “A man taking hold of the head of his horse in the way of Allah until he dies or is killed. Shall I inform you of the one who follows him?” He said: We said: Yes. He said: “A man withdrawn in a mountain pass, who establishes the ṣalāh, gives the zakāh, and keeps away from the evils of the people. Shall I inform you of the worst of people in station?” They said: Yes. He said: “The one who is asked by Allah and does not give by Him.”
items.ma-2959: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Iyās informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Umm Ḥufayd, the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās, presented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with ghee, dried curd, and lizards; and he ate from the ghee and from the dried curd, and left the lizards out of aversion. He said: And it was eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and had it been ḥarām, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-2960: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Mālik ibn Mighwal informed us, from Sulaymān al-Shaybānī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ made a ring and wore it, then said: “This has occupied me from you since today: a glance at it, and a glance at you.” Then he threw it away.
items.ma-2961: Maḥbūb ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Barakah Abū al-Walīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah curse the Jews: fats were made ḥarām for them, so they sold them and ate their prices; and indeed when Allah makes something ḥarām for a people, He makes its price ḥarām for them.”
items.ma-2962: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Its ʿiḍāh-trees are not to be cut down, its game is not to be startled, its luqaṭah is not lawful except for one who announces it, and its fresh grass is not to be cut.” So al-ʿAbbās said: O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir. He said: “Except the idhkhir.”
items.ma-2963: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Rukānah narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ did not fix a ḥadd for khamr. Ibn ʿAbbās said: A man drank and became intoxicated, and he was met swaying in a wide road, and he was taken to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Then when he came level with the house of ʿAbbās, he broke free and entered upon ʿAbbās and clung to him from behind. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he laughed and said: “He did it?!” Then he did not command them with anything concerning him.
items.ma-2964: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ when the qiblah was changed: What of those who died while praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis? So Allah ﵎ sent down: {And Allah would never let your īmān go to waste} [al-Baqarah: 143].
items.ma-2965: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Idrīs ibn Munabbih, from his father Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ asked Jibrīl to let him see him in his form, and he said: Call upon your Rabb. He said: So he called upon his Rabb. He said: Then a dark mass appeared before him from the direction of the east. He said: It kept rising and spreading. He said: Then when the Prophet ﷺ saw it, he fell unconscious. So he came to him and raised him up, and wiped the spittle from the side of his mouth.
items.ma-2966: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hishām ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Anas, that ʿAlī was brought some people of the Zuṭṭ who worshipped an idol, and he burned them. So Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.”
items.ma-2967:
Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Sayf ibn Sulaymān al-Makkī informed me, from Qays ibn Saʿd al-Makkī, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ judged with an oath and a witness.
Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb said: I asked Mālik ibn Anas about the oath and the witness: is it permissible in divorce and emancipation? He said: No, this is only in purchase and sale and the like.
items.ma-2968: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, from Sayf ibn Sulaymān, from Qays ibn Saʿd, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ judged with the oath together with the witness. ʿAmr said: That is only in property.
items.ma-2969: Al-Zubayrī Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Upon every Muslim is a Ḥajj; and had I said: every year, it would have been so.”
items.ma-2970: Al-Zubayrī and Aswad narrated to us, the wording being the same, they both said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ bought from a caravan that had arrived and made a profit of ūqiyyahs, and he divided it among the widows of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Then he said: “I will not buy a sale whose price I do not have with me.”
items.ma-2971: And Wakīʿ also narrated it to us, and he traced it back with a connected chain.
items.ma-2972: Al-Zubayrī and Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, they both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A woman became Muslim in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and married; then her first husband came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have become Muslim, and she knew my Islam. So the Prophet ﷺ removed her from her other husband and returned her to her first husband.
items.ma-2973: Abū Aḥmad Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, or from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, or from one of them from his companion, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever wants to perform Ḥajj, let him hasten, for the stray may be lost, the sick may fall ill, and a need may arise.”
items.ma-2974: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware of narrating from me except what you know; for whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire; and whoever lies about the Qurʾān without knowledge, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
