items.ma-2975: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did wipe over the two khuffs; so ask those who claim that the Prophet ﷺ wiped: was it before the revelation of al-Māʾidah or after al-Māʾidah? By Allah, he did not wipe after al-Māʾidah; and that I should wipe over the back of a passer-by in the open desert is dearer to me than that I should wipe over them.
items.ma-2976: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Ward, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr: O ʿUrayyah, ask your mother: did your father not come with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and so exit iḥrām?
items.ma-2977: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Shayāṭīn had seats in the sky, and they used to listen to the revelation; and the stars did not run, and the Shayāṭīn were not pelted. He said: Then when they heard the revelation, they would come down to the earth and add nine to the word. Then when the Prophet ﷺ was sent, whenever a Shayṭān sat in his seat, a flame would come to him and not miss him until it burned him. He said: So they complained of that to Iblīs, and he said: This is only from an occurrence that has occurred. He said: So he dispersed his troops, and behold, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing praying between the two mountains of Nakhlah. He said: So they returned to Iblīs and informed him. He said: And he said: He is the one who has occurred.
items.ma-2978: Rabʿī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Ibn Waʿlah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man went out when wine was lawful, and presented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a rāwiyah of wine. He came with it, leading it on a camel, until he found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting. He said: “What is this with you?” He said: A rāwiyah of wine that I have brought you as a gift. He said: “Did you know that Allah ﵎ has made it ḥarām?” He said: No. He said: “Indeed Allah has made it ḥarām.” Then the man turned to the one leading the camel and said something to him privately between the two of them. He said: “What did you say to him?” He said: I commanded him to sell it. He said: “Indeed the One who made its drinking ḥarām has made its sale ḥarām.” He said: So he commanded that the spouts of the large waterskin be opened, and they were opened, and it came out onto the soil. And I looked at it in al-baṭḥāʾ; there was nothing in it.
items.ma-2979: Hāshim narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped and gave the cupper his wage; and had it been ḥarām, he would not have given it to him. He used to be cupped on the two veins of the neck and between the shoulders, and a slave of Banū Bayāḍah used to cup him. A mudd and a half used to be taken from him every day, so the Prophet ﷺ interceded for him with his owners, and it was made a mudd.
items.ma-2980: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-2981: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
items.ma-2982: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-2983: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, he said: I heard Ṭāwūs narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: He ﷺ was commanded to prostrate upon seven. Shuʿbah said: And he narrated it to me another time, he said: “I was commanded to prostrate, and not to hold back hair or garment.”
items.ma-2984: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the women who visit the graves, and those who take mosques and lamps over them.
items.ma-2985: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Jamrah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray thirteen rakʿahs of the night.
items.ma-2986: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ passed by a man of Banū Sulaym who had sheep of his with him, and he greeted them with salām. They said: He only greeted you with salām to seek refuge from you. So they set upon him and killed him and took his sheep, and brought them to the Prophet ﷺ. Then Allah ﵎ sent down: {And do not say to one who offers you the salām: You are not a believer, seeking the goods of the worldly life} to the end of the verse [al-Nisāʾ: 94].
items.ma-2987: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying: {You were the best ummah brought out for the people} [Āl ʿImrān: 110], he said: The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ who emigrated with him to al-Madīnah.
items.ma-2988: Ḥusayn ibn Ḥasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, Abū Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting, and said: How do you speak, O Abū al-Qāsim, of the day when Allah ﵎ will place the heaven on this – and he pointed with the forefinger –, and the earth on this, and the water on this, and the mountains on this, and the rest of creation on this; all of that he was pointing with his finger. He said: Then Allah ﵎ sent down: {And they did not estimate Allah with His true estimation} the verse [al-Zumar: 67].
items.ma-2989: Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, Abū Kudaynah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning with no water in the camp. A man came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the camp. He said: “Do you have anything?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then bring it to me.” So he brought him a vessel with a little water in it. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his fingers over the mouth of the vessel and spread his fingers apart. He said: Then springs gushed forth from between his fingers, and he commanded Bilāl and said: “Call out among the people: the blessed wuḍūʾ water!”
items.ma-2990: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to me, my father narrated to us, he said: I heard Yūnus narrating from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When death came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: “Come, let me write for you a writing after which you will never go astray.” And in the house were men, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and ʿUmar said: Indeed pain has overcome the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you have the Qurʾān; the Book of Allah is sufficient for us. He said: So the people of the house differed and disputed; among them were those who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ will write for you – or he said: Bring [it] near, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may write for you – and among them were those who said what ʿUmar said. Then when they made much clamour and disagreement, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was distressed, he said: “Rise from me.” And Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: Indeed the calamity, all the calamity, was what came between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his writing that writing for them, from their disagreement and their clamour.
items.ma-2991: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray, while he was in Makkah, towards Bayt al-Maqdis, with the Kaʿbah before him, and after he emigrated to al-Madīnah, [for] sixteen months; then he was turned to the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-2992: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ḥasan narrated to us, from his father, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar came and said: Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah; peace be upon you; may ʿUmar enter?
items.ma-2993: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Wuhayb ibn Khālid narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Join the farāʾiḍ to their people; and what remains is for the nearest male man.”
items.ma-2994: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled in the year of the Conquest, in Ramaḍān, and fasted until he reached ʿUsfān; then he called for a vessel and drank in the daytime so that the people might see him, then broke his fast until he entered Makkah. And he conquered Makkah in Ramaḍān. Ibn ʿAbbās said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted while travelling and broke his fast; so whoever wishes may fast, and whoever wishes may break his fast.
items.ma-2995:
Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Khuṣayf, from Miqsam, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, he said: “Upon him is half a dīnār.”
He said: And Sharīk said: from Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-2996: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Ḥajj: every year? So he said: “Upon every Muslim is a Ḥajj; and had I said: every year, it would have been so.”
items.ma-2997: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Yūnus, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿAlī went out from the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his illness, and they said: How has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ risen this morning, O Abū Ḥasan? He said: He has risen, praise be to Allah, recovered. Then al-ʿAbbās said: Do you not see?! I see that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will be taken in death from this illness of his, and I recognise death in the faces of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. So go with us to the Messenger of Allah and let us speak to him; if the matter is with us, he will make it clear, and if it is with others than us, we will speak to him and he will give counsel concerning us. ʿAlī said: If he says: The matter is with others than us, the people will never give it to us; and by Allah, I will never speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this.
items.ma-2998: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Māʿiz when he said: I committed zinā: “Perhaps you pressed, or kissed, or looked at her?” He said: “As though he feared that he did not know what zinā is.
items.ma-2999: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to present the Qurʾān to Jibrīl once every year; then in the year in which he was taken, he presented it to him twice, and the recitation of ʿAbd Allāh was the last recitation.
items.ma-3000: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When {And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best} [al-Anʿām: 152 and al-Isrāʾ: 34] was revealed, they set apart the property of the orphans, until the food began to spoil and the meat to rot. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and so {And if you mix with them, they are your brothers; and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer} [al-Baqarah: 220] was revealed. He said: So they mixed with them.
items.ma-3001: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had finished with Badr: Take the caravan; there is nothing in front of it. He said: So al-ʿAbbās called out to him: It is not fitting for you; Allah promised you one of the two parties, and He has given you what He promised you.
items.ma-3002: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every fanged one of the beasts of prey.
items.ma-3003: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by us on the night of the Sacrifice, with the blackness of the night upon us, and he began to strike our thighs and say: “O my little sons, depart; and do not cast pebbles at the Jamrah until the sun rises.”
items.ma-3004: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr al-Nahshalī narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray eight rakʿahs at night, pray the witr with three, and pray the two rakʿahs of the Fajr.
items.ma-3005: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the mawlā of Abū Ṭalḥah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The name of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed her name and named her Juwayriyah.
items.ma-3006: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ahead the weak ones of his family from al-Muzdalifah by night, and he began to instruct them not to cast pebbles at the Jamrah of al-ʿAqabah until the sun rose.
items.ma-3007: Asbāṭ narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq – meaning al-Shaybānī – narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, he said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: So-and-so married, and he brought food near to us and we ate; then he brought near to us thirteen lizards, and some ate and some left them. Then one of those with Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not eat it, and I do not make it ḥarām, and I do not command it, and I do not forbid it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Evil is what you say. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was only sent as one who makes lawful and one who makes ḥarām. It was brought near to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he stretched out his hand to eat from it, and Maymūnah said: O Messenger of Allah, it is the meat of a lizard. So he withdrew his hand and said: “This is meat I have never eaten; so you eat.” So al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and a woman who was with them ate; and Maymūnah said: I will not eat of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not eat from.
items.ma-3008: Asbāṭ narrated to us, Muṭarrif narrated to us, from ʿAṭiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying: {Then when the nāqūr is sounded} [al-Muddaththir: 8], he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How can I be at ease, while the one with the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bent his forehead, listening for when he will be commanded so that he blows?” So the Companions of Muḥammad said: What shall we say? He said: “Say: Allah is sufficient for us, and excellent is al-Wakīl; upon Allah we have relied.”
items.ma-3009: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, he said: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about fasting in Rajab: what is your view on it? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast until we said: He will not break his fast; and he would break his fast until we said: He will not fast.
items.ma-3011: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd and Muʾammal narrated to us, the wording being the same, they both said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Muslims got hold of a man from among the great ones of the polytheists and killed him, and asked to buy his corpse; so the Prophet ﷺ forbade them. Muʾammal said: So the Prophet ﷺ forbade them to sell his corpse.
items.ma-3012: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ for the ṣalāh, and one of his wives said to him: Sit, for the pot is cooked. Then she handed him a shoulder [of meat], and he ate, then wiped his hand, and prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3013: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ibn Ṭāwūs narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits, then returns to it.”
items.ma-3014: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿUmar – meaning Ibn Farrūkh – narrated to us, Ḥabīb – meaning Ibn al-Zubayr – narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I saw a man enter the mosque, stand and pray; whenever he raised his head, he said the takbīr, and whenever he lowered his head, he said the takbīr, and when he rose from the two rakʿahs, he said the takbīr. I disapproved of that, so I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and informed him of it. He said: You have no mother! Is that not the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
items.ma-3015: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Nūḥ ibn Jaʿwanah al-Sulamī, from Khurāsān, narrated to us, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the mosque, saying with his hand like this – and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān gestured with his hand towards the ground –: “Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits for him, Allah will protect him from the blast of Jahannam. Indeed, the deed of Paradise is rugged ground upon a rise – three times. Indeed, the deed of the Fire is easy ground upon a plain. And the fortunate one is he who is protected from the fitan. And there is no swallow dearer to me than a swallow of rage that a servant suppresses; no servant suppresses it for Allah but Allah fills his inside with īmān.”
items.ma-3016: Ḥammād ibn Khālid narrated to us, from Mālik, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ passed by a dead ewe and said: “Whose was this ewe?” They said: Maymūnah's. He said: “Did you not benefit from its hide?”
items.ma-3017: Ḥammād ibn Khālid narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I and al-Faḍl passed by on a she-donkey while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer in an open stretch of land. So we dismounted and entered [the prayer] with him, and he said nothing to us about that.
items.ma-3018: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Zamʿah narrated to us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped and gave him his wage.
items.ma-3019: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Abū Ṭaybah in the evening and he cupped him, and he gave him his wage.
items.ma-3020: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, from Zamʿah, from Salamah ibn Wahrām, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at Jamʿ, and when everything had become bright, before the sun rose, he departed.
items.ma-3021: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Hāshim narrated to us, they both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard Abū al-Bakhtarī say: We sighted the crescent of Ramaḍān while we were at Dhāt ʿIrq. He said: So we sent a man to Ibn ʿAbbās to ask him – Hāshim said: and he asked him –, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has extended its sighting – Hāshim said: for its sighting – so if it is obscured from you, complete the count.”
items.ma-3022: Hāshim narrated to us, Warqāʾ narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ went to the place of relief, and I placed wuḍūʾ water for him. Then when he came out, he said: “Who placed this?” He said: Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: “O Allah, give him fiqh.”
items.ma-3023: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Abī Waḥshiyyah Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every fanged one of the beasts of prey, and every one with talons of the birds.
items.ma-3024: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Beware of narrating from me, except what you know.” He said: “And whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire; and whoever lies against the Qurʾān without knowledge, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-3025: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and began to speak in clear speech. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed some eloquence is magic, and indeed some poetry is judgment.”
items.ma-3026: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A sheep of Sawdah bint Zamʿah died, and she said: O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has died – meaning the sheep. He said: “Why did you not take its hide?” She said: Shall we take the hide of a sheep that has died?! So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “Allah ﷿ only said: {Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine} [al-Anʿām: 145]; and you are not eating it if you tan it and benefit from it.” So she sent for it, and skinned its hide, and tanned it, and took a waterskin from it, until it wore out with her.
items.ma-3027: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Sawdah bint Zamʿah, and he mentioned it.
items.ma-3028: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Māʿiz ibn Mālik: “Is what has reached me about you true, that you fell upon the slave-girl of Banū so-and-so?” He said: So he testified four testimonies. He said: So he stoned him.
items.ma-3029: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married my maternal aunt Maymūnah al-Hilāliyyah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3030: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that they went out with the Prophet ﷺ in iḥrām, and that a man among them was thrown by his camel, which broke his neck, and he died. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wash him with water and lote-leaves, and shroud him in two garments; do not let perfume touch him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with his hair matted.”
items.ma-3031: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There is no ṭiyarah, no contagion, no hāmah, and no ṣafar.” He said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, we take a mangy sheep and put it among the sheep, and they become mangy! He said: “Then who infected the first?!”
items.ma-3032: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of Maymūnah, and I placed wuḍūʾ water for him at night. He said: Then Maymūnah said: O Messenger of Allah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās placed this for you. So he said: “O Allah, give him fiqh in the religion, and teach him the interpretation.”
items.ma-3033: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, he said: So-and-so narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he walked, would walk gathered together, with no laziness in it.
items.ma-3034: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the children of the polytheists. He said: “Allah is more knowing of what they would have been doing when He created them.”
items.ma-3035: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wear the white of your garments, for they are among the best of your garments, and shroud your dead in them; and among the best of your kohl is antimony: it clears the sight and makes the hair grow.”
items.ma-3036: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved and have not slaughtered? He said: “There is no harm; and slaughter.” And another came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered before I cast pebbles? He said: “Then cast, and there is no harm.”
items.ma-3037: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he heard him say: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever claims descent from other than his father, or takes as his patron other than his mawālī, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people.”
items.ma-3038: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cast [pebbles at] the jimār after the sun had passed its zenith.
items.ma-3039: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Mukhawwal ibn Rāshid, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday: {The revelation} of al-Sajdah, and {Has there come upon man}.
items.ma-3040: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Umm Ḥufayd bint al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥazn, the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās, presented the Prophet ﷺ with ghee, dried curd, and lizards. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for them, and they were eaten at his table, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left them as one averse; so had they been ḥarām, they would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor would he have commanded that they be eaten.
items.ma-3041: ʿAffān narrated to us, Sukayn ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: So-and-so was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of ʿArafah. He said: The youth began to cast glances at the women and look at them. He said: And the Messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ began to turn his face away with his hand from behind, several times. He said: And the youth began to cast glances at them. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “O son of my brother, this is a day on which whoever controls his hearing, his sight, and his tongue is forgiven.”
items.ma-3042: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while he was in a tent on the day of Badr: “O Allah, I implore You for Your covenant and Your promise. O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped after today.” Then Abū Bakr took him by the hand and said: Enough, O Messenger of Allah, you have pressed upon your Rabb. And he was leaping in the coat of mail, and he went out saying: {The group will be routed, and they will turn their backs} [al-Qamar: 45].
items.ma-3043: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was approached [with a proposal] concerning the daughter of Ḥamzah, and he said: “She is the daughter of my brother by nursing, and she is not lawful for me; and what is made ḥarām by nursing is what is made ḥarām by the womb.”
items.ma-3044: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dāwūd narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Abū Jahl came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and forbade him, and the Prophet ﷺ threatened him. He said: Are you threatening me?! By Allah, I am the one with the greatest assembly of the people of the valley. So Allah sent down: {Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you seen if he is upon guidance, or commands taqwā? Have you seen if he denies and turns away} [al-ʿAlaq: 9–13]. Ibn ʿAbbās said: By the One in whose Yad is my soul, had he called his assembly, the Zabāniyah would have seized him.
items.ma-3045: ʿAffān narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, and he raised it, he said: “Whatever pact there was in the Jāhiliyyah, Islam did not increase it except in intensity and severity.”
items.ma-3046: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Black Stone is from Paradise, and it was whiter than snow, until the sins of the people of shirk blackened it.”
items.ma-3047: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a dead sheep that its owners had cast out, and said: “By the One in whose Yad is my soul, the world is more insignificant to Allah than this is to its owners.”
items.ma-3048: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah sought a fatwā from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a vow that was upon his mother, who died before fulfilling it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fulfil it on her behalf.”
items.ma-3049: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman of Khathʿam asked the Prophet ﷺ during the Farewell Ḥajj, while al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah in the Ḥajj upon His servants has come upon my father when he is a very old man, unable to stay firm on the mount; shall I perform Ḥajj on his behalf? He said: “Yes, perform Ḥajj on behalf of your father.”
items.ma-3050: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to me, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank milk, then called for water and rinsed his mouth, and said: “It has greasiness.”
items.ma-3051: Muḥammad ibn Muṣʿab narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a dead sheep and said: “Why did you not make use of its skin?” They said: O Messenger of Allah, it is carrion. He said: “Only the eating of it has been made ḥarām.”
items.ma-3052: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3053: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Karīm narrated to us, he said: One who heard Ibn ʿAbbās say narrated to me: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Ḍubāʿah to stipulate a condition in her iḥrām.
items.ma-3054: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, from some of his brothers, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Makkī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: A man has come to us who denies al-qadar. He said: Direct me to him. And he was blind at that time. They said: And what will you do with him, O Abū ʿAbbās? He said: By the One in whose Yad is my soul, if I get hold of him, I will bite his nose until I cut it off; and if his neck falls into my hands, I will crush it. For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “It is as though I see the women of Banū Fihr circling around al-Khazraj, their buttocks knocking together, as polytheists.” This is the first shirk of this ummah. And by the One in whose Yad is my soul, their evil opinion will bring them to the point that they remove Allah from having decreed good, just as they removed Him from having decreed evil.
items.ma-3055: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Makkī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with this ḥadīth. I said: Did Muḥammad meet Ibn ʿAbbās? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3056: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, he said: It reached me that ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās report: that a man was struck by a wound in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then a wet dream befell him, and he was commanded to perform ghusl, and he died. That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “They killed him; may Allah kill them! Was the cure for incapacity not asking?”
items.ma-3057: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made him ride behind him on his mount, and when he had settled upon it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr three times, praised Allah three times, glorified Allah three times, and said the tahlīl once; then he lay back on it and laughed. Then he turned to me and said: “There is no man who mounts his animal and does as I did, except that Aqbala Allāh ﵎ fa-ḍaḥika ilayhi, as I laughed to you.”
items.ma-3058: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī was asked: Is ghusl obligatory on Friday? He said: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever of you comes to the Jumuʿah, let him perform ghusl.” And Ṭāwūs said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: They mention that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Perform ghusl on the day of Jumuʿah, and wash your heads, even if you are not junub, and take some perfume.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: As for the ghusl, yes; as for the perfume, I do not know.
items.ma-3059: ʿAbd Allāh said: I found in my father's book, in his own handwriting, this ḥadīth: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the woman who joins [hair] and the woman for whom it is joined, the men who imitate women, and the women who imitate men.
items.ma-3060: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīrah Abū Yūnus narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, that Kurayb informed him that Ibn ʿAbbās said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the end of the night and prayed behind him. Then he took me by my hand and drew me and placed me beside him; and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to his prayer, I withdrew. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and when he finished, he said to me: “What is the matter with me? I place you beside me and you withdraw?” I said: O Messenger of Allah, is it fitting for anyone to pray beside you, when you are the Messenger of Allah whom Allah has given what He has given? He said: So I pleased him, and he supplicated to Allah for me that He increase me in knowledge and understanding. He said: Then I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sleep until I heard him breathing heavily; then Bilāl came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, the ṣalāh! So he rose and prayed, without repeating wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3061:
Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Balj narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn narrated to us, he said: I was sitting with Ibn ʿAbbās when nine men came to him and said: O Abū ʿAbbās, either you stand with us, or you leave us [alone], O you people. He said: So Ibn ʿAbbās said: Rather I will stand with you. He said: And he was healthy at that time, before he went blind. He said: So they began and talked, and we do not know what they said. He said: Then he came shaking out his garment and saying: Ugh and fie! They have spoken ill of a man who has ten; they have spoken ill of a man to whom the Prophet ﷺ said: “I will surely send a man whom Allah will never disgrace, who loves Allah and His Messenger.” He said: So those who were eager craned for it. He said: “Where is ʿAlī?” They said: He is at the mill, grinding. He said: “Was it for one of you to grind?!” He said: Then he came, suffering from sore eyes, barely able to see. He said: So he blew into his eyes, then shook the banner three times and gave it to him; and he came with Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy.
He said: Then he sent so-and-so with Sūrat al-Tawbah, and he sent ʿAlī after him, and he took it from him. He said: “None shall go with it except a man from me, and I am from him.”
He said: And he said to his cousins: “Which of you will ally with me in this world and the Hereafter?” He said: And ʿAlī was sitting with him, and they refused. So ʿAlī said: I will ally with you in this world and the Hereafter. He said: “You are my walī in this world and the Hereafter.” He said: So he left him, then turned to a man among them and said: “Which of you will ally with me in this world and the Hereafter?” But they refused. He said: So ʿAlī said: I will ally with you in this world and the Hereafter. So he said: “You are my walī in this world and the Hereafter.”
He said: And he was the first of the people to become Muslim after Khadījah. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took his garment and placed it over ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan, and Ḥusayn, and said: {Allah only intends to remove uncleanliness from you, O people of the house, and to purify you with purification} [al-Aḥzāb: 33].
He said: And ʿAlī sold himself; he put on the garment of the Prophet ﷺ, then slept in his place. He said: And the polytheists were pelting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Abū Bakr came, while ʿAlī was sleeping. He said: And Abū Bakr thought that he was the Prophet of Allah. He said: So he said: O Prophet of Allah. He said: So ʿAlī said to him: Indeed the Prophet of Allah ﷺ has gone off towards the well of Maymūn, so catch up with him. He said: So Abū Bakr went off, and entered the cave with him. He said: And ʿAlī was being pelted with stones as the Prophet of Allah used to be pelted, and he was writhing, having wrapped his head in the garment, not bringing it out until morning; then he uncovered his head. So they said: You are indeed ignoble! Your companion we used to pelt and he would not writhe, and you are writhing, and we found that strange.
He said: And he went out with the people on the expedition of Tabūk. He said: So ʿAlī said to him: Shall I go out with you? He said: So the Prophet of Allah said to him: “No.” So ʿAlī wept. So he said to him: “Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā, except that you are not a prophet? It is not fitting that I go except that you are my successor.” He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “You are my walī for every believer after me.”
And he said: And he closed the doors of the mosque except the door of ʿAlī. He said: So he would enter the mosque in a state of janābah, and it was his road; he had no road other than it.
He said: And he said: “Whoever I am his mawlā, then his mawlā is ʿAlī.”
He said: And Allah ﷿ informed us in the Qurʾān that He raḍiya ʿanhum, the Companions of the Tree, and He knew what was in their hearts; has He told us that He sakhiṭa ʿalayhim afterwards?!
He said: And the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to ʿUmar when he said: Permit me, that I may strike his neck. He said: “Would you have done so?! And what lets you know? Perhaps Allah qad iṭṭalaʿa ilā ahl Badr, and said: Do whatever you wish.”
items.ma-3062: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Mālik Kathīr ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Balj, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, similar to it.
items.ma-3063: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they both said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ḥasan ibn Muslim informed me, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I witnessed the prayer on the day of Fiṭr with the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, and each of them used to pray it before the khuṭbah, then deliver the khuṭbah afterwards. He said: Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came down – it is as though I am looking at him – when he made the men sit with his hand, then proceeded cleaving through them until he came to the women, with Bilāl with him, and he said: {O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah} [al-Mumtaḥanah: 12]. He recited this verse until he finished it, then said when he had finished it: “Are you upon that?” Then one woman – none other of them answered him – said: Yes, O Prophet of Allah – Ḥasan does not know who she was. He said: “Then give ṣadaqah.” He said: So Bilāl spread his garment, then said: Come, for you; my father and mother be your ransom. And they began to throw the large rings and the rings into the garment of Bilāl. Ibn Bakr said: al-khawātīm.
items.ma-3064: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I witnessed the Prophet ﷺ pray on the day of the ʿĪd, then deliver the khuṭbah; then he thought that he had not made the women hear, so he came to them and admonished them, and said: “Give ṣadaqah.” And the woman began to throw the ring, the earring, and the thing; then he commanded Bilāl, and he gathered it in a garment until he had passed it on.
items.ma-3065: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father; once he said: from Ibn ʿAbbās. So I said to Maʿmar: Did he not go beyond Ṭāwūs with it? He said: Rather, it is from Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: Then he heard him mention it afterwards, without mentioning Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The people of al-Madīnah enter iḥrām from Dhū al-Ḥulayfah; the people of al-Shām enter iḥrām from al-Juḥfah; the people of Yemen enter iḥrām from Yalamlam; and the people of Najd enter iḥrām from Qarn. And they are for them, and for whoever comes upon them from others than them who intends Ḥajj and ʿumrah; and whoever's house is within the mīqāt, he enters iḥrām from his house, until he comes to the people of Makkah.” Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: My father said: I entered iḥrām from Yalamlam when I came from ʿAbd al-Razzāq.
items.ma-3066: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of four of the animals: the ant, the bee, the hoopoe, and the shrike.
items.ma-3067: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Two roasted lizards were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while Khālid ibn al-Walīd was with him, and the Prophet ﷺ stretched out his hand to eat. It was said to him: It is a lizard. So he held back his hand, and Khālid said to him: Is it ḥarām, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “No, but it is not found in the land of my people, so I find myself averse to it.” So Khālid ate, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked on.
items.ma-3068: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and began to praise him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed some eloquence is magic, and indeed some poetry is judgment.”
items.ma-3069: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Qatādah, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the eating of every fanged one of the beasts of prey, and the eating of every one with talons of the birds.
items.ma-3070: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujāhid, he said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās and said: O Abū ʿAbbās, I was with Ibn ʿUmar, and he recited this verse and wept. He said: Which verse? I said: {Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it} [al-Baqarah: 284]. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Indeed when this verse was sent down, it distressed the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ severely and angered them severely, meaning, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, we are destroyed, if we are to be taken to account for what we speak and for what we do; as for our hearts, they are not in our hands. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: “Say: We hear and we obey.” They said: We hear and we obey. He said: Then this verse abrogated it: {The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Rabb, and the believers} to {Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; for it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned} [al-Baqarah: 185–286]. So they were excused for the speech of the self, and were taken to account for deeds.
items.ma-3071: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us; and al-Aswad said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The righteous dream is one part of seventy parts of prophethood.”
items.ma-3072: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Quraysh came to a woman soothsayer and said to her: Inform us who is closest among us in resemblance to the owner of this station. She said: If you drag a cloak over this soft ground, then walk upon it, I will tell you. So they dragged it, then the people walked upon it, and she saw the footprint of Muḥammad ﷺ, and said: This one is the closest of you in resemblance to him. Then they stayed after that twenty years, or close to twenty years, or what Allah willed; then he ﷺ was sent.
items.ma-3073: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn Qays informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ once, once.
items.ma-3074: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar and al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās and Muʿāwiyah, and Muʿāwiyah would not pass a corner without touching it. So Ibn ʿAbbās said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not touch except the Stone and the Yamānī. Muʿāwiyah said: Nothing of the House is to be abandoned.
items.ma-3075: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī informed us, from Ibn Khuthaym. And Abū Nuʿaym: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ married while in iḥrām, and was cupped while in iḥrām.
items.ma-3076: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man fell from his camel while in iḥrām, and it broke his neck – or killed him outright, Ayyūb was unsure –, so they asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Wash him with water and lote-leaves, and shroud him in his two garments; do not cover his head, and do not bring perfume near him, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as one in iḥrām.”
items.ma-3077: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar said: And ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man fell from a camel that had bolted, while in iḥrām, and his neck was broken, a breaking … then he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of Ayyūb.
items.ma-3078:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a vow that was upon his mother, and he commanded its fulfilment.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Jābir, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped on the two veins of the neck and between the shoulders; a slave of Banū Bayāḍah cupped him, and his wage was a mudd and a half, so he spoke to his owners until they remitted half a mudd from him. Ibn ʿAbbās said: And he gave him his wage; and had it been ḥarām, he would not have given it to him.
items.ma-3079: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Afṭas, he said: I heard Wahb narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Twelve thousand will come out of ʿAdan Abyan, supporting Allah and His Messenger; they are the best of those between me and them.” Maʿmar said to me: Go and ask him about this ḥadīth.
items.ma-3080:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, they both said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Yaʿlā informed me that he heard ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, say: Ibn ʿAbbās informed us: that Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah – Ibn Bakr said: the brother of Banū Sāʿidah – his mother died while he was absent from her, so he said: O Messenger of Allah, my mother died while I was absent from her; would it benefit her if I gave ṣadaqah of something on her behalf? He said: “Yes.” He said: Then I make you witness that the garden of al-Makhraf is ṣadaqah on her behalf.
And Ibn Bakr said: al-Mikhrāf.
items.ma-3081: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jibrīl led me in prayer at the House. He prayed the Ẓuhr with me when the sun had passed its zenith, and it was the measure of the sandal-strap. Then he prayed the ʿAṣr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to it. Then he prayed the Maghrib with me when the fasting person broke his fast. Then he prayed the ʿIshāʾ with me when the twilight disappeared. Then he prayed the Fajr with me when food and drink became ḥarām for the fasting person. Then the next day he prayed the Ẓuhr when the shadow of everything was equal to it. Then he prayed the ʿAṣr with me when the shadow of everything was twice it. Then he prayed the Maghrib with me when the fasting person broke his fast. Then he prayed the ʿIshāʾ with me up to the first third of the night. Then he prayed the Fajr with me, and it became bright. Then he turned to me and said: O Muḥammad, this is the time of the prophets before you; the time is between these two times.”
items.ma-3082:
Abū Nuʿaym narrated to me, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm ibn ʿAbbād ibn Ḥunayf, and he mentioned it with its isnād and its meaning.
Except that he said about the Fajr on the second day: I do not know what thing he said; and he said about the ʿIshāʾ: He prayed with me when the first third of the night had gone.
items.ma-3083: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Ṣanʿānī narrated to me, Wahb ibn Mānūs al-ʿAdanī informed me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he raised his head from the rukūʿ, would say: “Samiʿa Allāh li-man ḥamidah.” Then he would say: “O Allah, our Rabb, to You is the praise, filling the heaven, filling the earth, and filling whatever You will of anything afterwards.”
items.ma-3084: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar ibn Kaysān narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Wahb ibn Mānūs, other than this ḥadīth.
items.ma-3085: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped and gave the cupper his wage; and had it been suḥt, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not have given it to him.
items.ma-3086: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Jamrah al-Ḍubaʿī, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd, the naqīr, the pitch-coated vessel, and the ḥantam.
items.ma-3087: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The guardian has no say with the previously married woman; and the orphan girl is to be consulted, and her silence is her acknowledgement.”
items.ma-3088:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿUmar ibn Muʿattib, from the mawlā of Banū Nawfal – meaning Abū al-Ḥasan – he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about a slave who divorced his wife with two divorces, then both were freed: may he marry her? He said: Yes. It was said: From whom [is this]? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a ruling to that effect.
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: It was said to Maʿmar: O Abū ʿUrwah, who is this Abū Ḥasan? He has carried a great rock!!
items.ma-3089: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, he said: Al-Zuhrī said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ went out in Ramaḍān from al-Madīnah with ten thousand of the Muslims with him, and that was at the head of eight and a half years from his arrival in al-Madīnah. He travelled with those Muslims who were with him to Makkah, fasting, and they fasting, until when he reached al-Kadīd, which is between ʿUsfān and Qudayd, he broke his fast and the Muslims broke their fast with him, and he did not fast.
items.ma-3090: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to narrate: that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq entered the mosque while ʿUmar was speaking to the people, and went on until he came to the house in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had died, which was in the house of ʿĀʾishah. He uncovered from his face a ḥibarah cloak with which he had been covered, and looked at the face of the Prophet ﷺ, then bent over him kissing him, then said: By Allah, Allah will not bring two deaths together upon him; you have died the death after which you will not die.
items.ma-3092: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to recite in the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in what he was commanded to recite in, and was silent in what he was commanded to be silent in. There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example, {and your Rabb was never forgetful} [Maryam: 64].
items.ma-3093: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Makkah, he refused to enter the House while the gods were in it, so he commanded about them and they were brought out. Then they brought out the image of Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl ﵉, with divining arrows in their hands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah fight them! By Allah, they certainly knew that the two of them never divided by them.” He said: Then he entered the House and said the takbīr in the corners of the House, and went out, and did not pray in the House.
items.ma-3094: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ sent him with the baggage from Jamʿ by night.
items.ma-3095: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he disliked nabīdh of unripe dates alone, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade ʿAbd al-Qays the muzzāʾ, so I dislike that it be unripe dates alone.
items.ma-3096: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān narrated to us, they both said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿAzrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ṣubḥ prayer on Friday: {The revelation} al-Sajdah, and {Has there come upon man}. ʿAffān said: with {Alif Lām Mīm. The revelation}.
items.ma-3097: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Bukayr ibn Abī al-Samīṭ informed us, Qatādah said: from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited in the morning prayer on Friday: {The revelation} al-Sajdah, and {Has there come upon man}.
items.ma-3098: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Bāriq al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, Simāk Abū Zumayl al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever of my ummah has two forerunners will enter Paradise.” ʿĀʾishah said: My father [be your ransom]! And whoever has one forerunner? He said: “And whoever has one forerunner, O granted success.” She said: And whoever of your ummah has no forerunner? He said: “Then I am the forerunner of my ummah; they have not been stricken with the like of me.”
items.ma-3099: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, he said: Abū Sallām narrated, from al-Ḥakam ibn Mīnāʾ, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say upon the planks of his minbar: “Let people surely cease from their abandoning the Jumuʿahs, or Allah will surely seal their hearts, and then they will surely be written among the heedless.”
items.ma-3100: Hudbah ibn Khālid narrated to us, Abān ibn Yazīd al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Sallām, from al-Ḥakam ibn Mīnāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ, with the like of it.
items.ma-3101: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn Farrūkh narrated to us, Ḥabīb – meaning Ibn al-Zubayr – narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I saw a man praying in the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ, and he would say the takbīr when he prostrated, and when he rose, and when he lowered himself. I disapproved of that, and I mentioned it to Ibn ʿAbbās. He said: You have no mother! That is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3102: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of Maymūnah, and I placed wuḍūʾ water for him at night. Maymūnah said to him: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās placed this for you. So he said: “O Allah, give him fiqh in the religion, and teach him the interpretation.”
items.ma-3103: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, they both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd. My father said: ʿAffān narrated it to us, Ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn died, his wife said: May it be pleasant for you, O Ibn Maẓʿūn: Paradise. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her with a look of anger and said to her: “What lets you know?! By Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not know what will be done with me – ʿAffān said: nor with him –.” She said: O Messenger of Allah, your horseman and your companion! That was hard upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said that about ʿUthmān, who was among the best of them, until Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died, and he said: “Join our good predecessor, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn.” He said: And the women wept, and ʿUmar began to strike them with his whip. The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar: “Leave them to weep; and beware, you women, of the screeching of Shayṭān.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whatever is from the heart and the eye is from Allah and mercy; and whatever is from the hand and the tongue is from Shayṭān.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat at the edge of the grave, with Fāṭimah beside him weeping, and the Prophet ﷺ began to wipe the eye of Fāṭimah with his garment, out of mercy for her.
items.ma-3104: Bakr ibn ʿĪsā Abū Bishr al-Rāsibī narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Ḥamzah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I was a boy running with the boys, and I turned, and behold, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was behind me, coming on. I said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ has come only for me. He said: So I ran until I hid behind the door of a house. He said: And I did not realise until he took hold of me, seized me by the nape, and gave me a pat, and said: “Go and call Muʿāwiyah for me.” He said: And he was his scribe. So I ran and came to Muʿāwiyah and said: Answer the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, for he has a need.
items.ma-3105: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt – narrated to us. And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Dāwūd, said: Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs with the people on the day of Fiṭr without an adhān, then delivered the khuṭbah after the prayer, then took Bilāl by the hand and went to the women and addressed them; then he commanded Bilāl, after he had turned away from them, to come to them and command them to give ṣadaqah.
items.ma-3106: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed liʿān between al-ʿAjlānī and his wife. He said: And she was pregnant. He said: By Allah, I have not approached her since we did ʿafr – He said: And al-ʿafr is that the palm trees are watered after they have been left without watering, two months after the pollination –. He said: And her husband was thin in the calves and forearms, reddish-haired; and the one with whom she was accused was Ibn al-Saḥmāʾ. He said: Then she gave birth to a black boy, with receding hair, curly-haired, thick in the forearms. He said: Ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Is she the woman about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: “If I were to stone without proof, I would have stoned her”? He said: No, that was a woman who had made [it] public in Islam.
items.ma-3107:
Surayj narrated it to us, Ibn Abī al-Zinād narrated to us, and he mentioned its meaning.
And he said in it: thick in the forearms, plump in the calves; and al-Hāshimī said: khadl, and said: after the pollination.
items.ma-3108: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Fulayḥ narrated to us, al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from his father: that he saw the Prophet ﷺ eat a limb [of meat], then pray and not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3109: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Saʿīd informed us. And ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah and Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith while in iḥrām. He said: And in the ḥadīth of Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm: He consummated the marriage with her at a water called Sarif; then when he had completed his rites, he held the wedding night with her at that water.
items.ma-3110: Asbāṭ narrated to us, al-Shaybānī narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that unripe dates and dates be mixed together, and that raisins and dates be mixed together. He said: And he wrote to the people of Jurash: that they should not mix raisins and dates.
items.ma-3111:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When death came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the house were men, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Come, let me write for you a writing after which you will never go astray.” So ʿUmar said: Indeed pain has overcome the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you have the Qurʾān; the Book of Allah is sufficient for us. Then the people of the house differed and disputed; among them were those who said: Bring [it] near, that he may write for you a writing after which you will not go astray, and among them were those who said what ʿUmar said. Then when they made much idle talk and disagreement in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Rise.”
ʿUbayd Allāh said: And Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: Indeed the calamity, all the calamity, was what came between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his writing that writing for them, from their disagreement and their clamour.
items.ma-3112: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from a son of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to al-Madīnah and found the Jews fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. He said: “What is this?” They said: This is a great day, the day Allah delivered Mūsā and drowned the family of Firʿawn, so Mūsā fasted it in thanks. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Then I am closer to Mūsā and more deserving of fasting it.” So he fasted it and commanded its fasting.
items.ma-3113:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he performed wuḍūʾ and washed each limb of his once, then mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ did it.
Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ and another informed me, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no ṣarūrah in the Ḥajj.”
items.ma-3114:
Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say: “There is no ṣarūrah in Islam.”
Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī narrated to me: that a man called out to Ibn ʿAbbās while the people were around him, and said: Is it a sunnah that you seek with this nabīdh, or is it easier for you than honey and milk? Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ came to ʿAbbās and said: “Give us to drink.” He said: Indeed this nabīdh is a drink that has been steeped and dissolved; shall we not give you milk and honey to drink? He said: “Give me to drink from what you give the people to drink from.” He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ was brought, and with him his Companions from the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, large bowls containing the nabīdh; and when the Prophet ﷺ drank, he hurried before he was quenched, then raised his head and said: “You have done well; do likewise.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The pleasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in that is more pleasing to me than that its ravines should flow upon us with milk and honey.
items.ma-3115: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us. And Rawḥ, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed him, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was giving a khuṭbah, saying: “Whoever does not find an izār and finds trousers, let him wear them; and whoever does not find sandals and finds khuffs, let him wear them.”
items.ma-3116: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us. And Ḥajjāj, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3117: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abū al-Zubayr informed me, that he heard Ṭāwūs and ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informing from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am a heavy woman, and I want Ḥajj; so how do you command me, how should I make ihlāl? He said: “Make ihlāl, and stipulate that my place of release is where you detain me.” He said: So she attained [it].
items.ma-3118:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the women who visit graves, and those who take mosques and lamps over them.
Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah said: I think he meant the Jews.
items.ma-3119: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, from Mūsā ibn Salamah, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās: How should I pray when I am in Makkah, if I have not prayed with the imām? He said: Two rakʿahs, the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-3120: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ and Maymūnah were in a state of janābah, so Maymūnah bathed in a large bowl, and a remainder was left over; the Prophet ﷺ wished to bathe from it, and she said: O Messenger of Allah, I have already bathed from it. So he – meaning the Prophet ﷺ – said: “Indeed the water has no janābah upon it,” or he said: “Indeed the water does not become impure.”
items.ma-3121: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, he said: I think it was from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Prophet ﷺ performed tamattuʿ. ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar forbade the mutʿah. Ibn ʿAbbās said: What does ʿUrayyah say? He said: He says: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar forbade the mutʿah. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I think they will perish! I say: The Prophet ﷺ said, and he says: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar forbade.
items.ma-3122: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was commanded to use the siwāk, until I thought that a Qurʾān, or a revelation, would descend upon me with it.”
items.ma-3123: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, ʿUqayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank milk, then called for water and rinsed his mouth, then said: “Indeed it has fat.”
items.ma-3124: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Yaʿlā ibn Muslim informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: {O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you} [al-Nisāʾ: 59] was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Qays ibn ʿAdī al-Sahmī, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him in the expedition.
items.ma-3125: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I gathered the Muḥkam in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ was taken [in death] when I was ten years old. He said: So I said to him: And what is the Muḥkam? He said: The Mufaṣṣal.
items.ma-3126: Hushaym narrated to us, Manṣūr informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn: that a funeral procession passed by al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḥasan stood up but Ibn ʿAbbās did not stand up. Al-Ḥasan said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not stand up for it? He said: He stood up, and he sat.
items.ma-3127: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to give permission to the people of Badr, and he gave permission to me with them. Some of them said: He gives permission to this youth with us, while among our sons are those like him?! ʿUmar said: Indeed he is of those whom you have known. He said: So one day he gave them permission, and gave me permission with them, and asked them about this sūrah: {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come}. They said: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ, when conquest is opened to him, to seek His forgiveness and to turn to Him in repentance. He said to me: What do you say, O Ibn ʿAbbās? He said: I said: It is not so; rather He informed His Prophet عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ وَالسَّلامُ of the arrival of his appointed term, and said: {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} – the conquest of Makkah – {and you see the people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes} – so that is the sign of your death – {so glorify with the praise of your Rabb and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance}. He said to them: How can you blame me for what you see?
items.ma-3128: Hushaym narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj, and when he arrived he performed ṭawāf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and he did not shorten [his hair], and did not leave iḥrām because of the hady; and he commanded whoever had not driven the hady to perform ṭawāf, and to perform saʿy, and to shorten or shave, then leave iḥrām.
items.ma-3129: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah informed me, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked: Which drink is the best? He said: “The sweet, cold one.”
items.ma-3130: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, he said: Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū Jamrah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray thirteen rakʿahs at night.
items.ma-3131: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Jamrah, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was playing with the boys, so I hid from him behind a door, and he called me and patted me with a pat, then sent me to Muʿāwiyah; so I returned to him and said: He is eating.
items.ma-3132: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ḥabīb – Bahz said: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit narrated to us – he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: Al-Ṣaʿb – and Ibn Jaʿfar said: Ibn Jaththāmah – gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a piece of a donkey while he was in iḥrām, and he returned it. Bahz said: the rump of a donkey, or he said: a leg of a donkey.
items.ma-3134: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Sulaymān al-Shaybānī say, he said: I heard al-Shaʿbī say, he said: One who passed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by an isolated grave informed me; so he led them [in prayer], and they lined up behind him. I said: O Abū ʿAmr, who narrated to you? He said: Ibn ʿAbbās.
items.ma-3135: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Ṭāwūs, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “Whoever has land, that he grant it to his brother is better for him.”
items.ma-3136: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he was at the Stone, and he had a hooked staff with which he would strike the Stone, and he would kiss it; and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “{O you who believe, fear Allah with the fear due to Him, and do not die except as Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. If a single drop of the Zaqqūm were to be dropped upon the earth, it would embitter the livelihood of the people of the world; so how will it be for the one whose food it is, and he has no food other than it?!”
items.ma-3137: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, al-Qawārīrī narrated to us, Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us, from Sulaymān – meaning al-Aʿmash –, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: If a single drop of the Zaqqūm … and he mentioned it.
items.ma-3138: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Sulaymān narrating, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: A woman rode the sea, and vowed to fast a month, and she died before she fasted; so her sister came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he commanded her to fast on her behalf.
items.ma-3139: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “There is no deed more excellent than it in these days” – meaning the days of the ten – he said: It was said: Not even jihād in the way of Allah? He said: “Not even jihād in the way of Allah, except for one who goes out with himself and his wealth, and then does not return with any of that.”
items.ma-3140: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: I prayed the Ẓuhr prayer behind a foolish old man, and he pronounced the takbīr twenty-two times in it, pronouncing the takbīr when he prostrated and when he raised his head from prostration. Ibn ʿAbbās said: May you have no mother! That is the sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-3141: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Rawḥ narrated to us, both said: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade, on the day of Khaybar, every bird with a talon, and every beast of prey with a fang.
items.ma-3142: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, both said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the mujaththamah and the jallālah – Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: He forbade the milk of the jallālah – and drinking from the mouth of the waterskin.
items.ma-3143: Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the milk of the jallālah, and the mujaththamah, and drinking from the mouth of the waterskin.
items.ma-3144: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, both said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pressed regarding the daughter of Ḥamzah, that he marry her, and he said: “She is the daughter of my brother by suckling, and indeed what is forbidden by suckling is what is forbidden by lineage.”
items.ma-3145: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came upon his wife while she was menstruating, and asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he commanded him to give ṣadaqah of a dīnār, or half a dīnār.
items.ma-3146: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-3147: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah. And Yazīd ibn Hārūn, he said: Saʿīd informed us, from Qatādah, he said: Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he used to say at times of distress: “There is no deity except Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, al-Ḥalīm; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh; there is no deity except Allah, Rabb of the heavens and the earth, Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh.” Yazīd said: “Rabb of the seven heavens, and Rabb of the Noble ʿArsh.”
items.ma-3148: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ṭāwūs informed us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Dhū al-Ḥulayfah as the mīqāt for the people of Madinah, al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, Qarn for the people of Najd, and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. He said: “They are for them, and for whoever comes upon them from others than them, of those who intend Ḥajj and ʿumrah; then from where he began, until the people of Makkah reached that.”
items.ma-3149: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, and a camel was brought, and he marked the right side of its hump, then wiped the blood from it, and garlanded it with two sandals. Then he called for his mount and rode it, and when it stood up straight with him on al-Baydāʾ, he assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj.
items.ma-3150: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This and this are equal” – meaning the little finger and the thumb.
items.ma-3151: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us.
