And Ḥajjāj, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed – Ḥajjāj said: So he said: “May Allah curse the men who imitate women, and the women who imitate men.”
items.ma-3152:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq narrating, that he heard a man of Banū Tamīm say: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about a man's saying thus with his finger – meaning in the prayer – he said: That is sincerity.
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us regarding the siwāk, until we thought that something would be sent down upon him concerning it.
And I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.
items.ma-3153: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit – Bahz said: ʿAdī ibn Thābit informed me – he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of Aḍḥā – or the day of Fiṭr, he said: and my strongest thought is that he said: the day of Fiṭr – and prayed two rakʿahs, not praying before them or after them; then he came to the women, with Bilāl with him, and commanded them to give ṣadaqah, and the woman began to throw her earring and her necklace. And Bahz did not doubt; he said: the day of Fiṭr, and he said: ṣikhābahā.
items.ma-3154: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAdī ibn Thābit and ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said – one of them traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ: “Indeed Jibrīl used to thrust mud into the mouth of Pharaoh, fearing that he would say: There is no deity except Allah.”
items.ma-3155: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Do not take anything in which there is spirit as a target.”
items.ma-3156: Hāshim narrated to us the like of it. He said – meaning Shuʿbah –: You said: From the Prophet ﷺ? He said: From the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3157: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Abū al-Ḥakam, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about nabīdh of the jar, and about the gourd and the ḥantam. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Whoever is pleased to prohibit what Allah and His Messenger prohibited, let him prohibit nabīdh.
items.ma-3158: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Abū al-Ḥakam narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The month is complete – twenty-nine.”
items.ma-3159: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mushāsh, he said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, and he narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the children of Banū Hāshim and their weak ones to depart from Jamʿ by night.
items.ma-3160: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mukhawwal, he said: I heard Muslim al-Baṭīn narrating from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to recite in the Ṣubḥ prayer {Alif, Lām, Mīm. The revelation} – al-Sajdah – and {Has there come upon man}, and on Friday, the sūrah of al-Jumuʿah and al-Munāfiqūn.
items.ma-3161: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān and Manṣūr, from Dharr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that they said: O Messenger of Allah, we speak to ourselves of something, such that for one of us to be a cinder is dearer to him than that he should speak of it? He said: One of the two said: “Praise be to Allah, who has not been able [to get] from you [anything] except the whispering,” and the other said: “Praise be to Allah, who has returned his affair to the whispering.”
items.ma-3162: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from Madinah in Ramaḍān, when he conquered Makkah, and fasted until he reached ʿUsfān, then called for a large bowl of drink, or a vessel, and drank. So Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: Whoever wishes may fast, and whoever wishes may break the fast.
items.ma-3163: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: My maternal aunt Umm Ḥufayd presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ghee, dried curd and lizards. He ate of the ghee and the dried curd, and left the lizards out of distaste, and it was eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and had it been forbidden, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3164: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived at Madinah, and behold, the Jews had fasted on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, so he asked them about that, and they said: This is the day on which Mūsā prevailed over Pharaoh. The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions: “You are more deserving of Mūsā than they are; so fast it.”
items.ma-3165: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: “Allah, when He created them, knows best what they were doing.”
items.ma-3166: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā Abū ʿUmar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd, the pitch-coated vessel, and the naqīr.
items.ma-3167: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ṣuhayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And ʿAffān said – meaning in his ḥadīth –: Al-Ḥakam informed me of it, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ṣuhayb – I said: Who is Ṣuhayb? He said: A man of the people of al-Baṣrah – from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he was upon a donkey, he and a boy of Banū Hāshim, and he passed in front of the Prophet ﷺ while he was praying, and he did not turn away; and two girls of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib came and took hold of the knees of the Prophet ﷺ, and he parted between them – or he separated between them – and he did not turn away.
items.ma-3168: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Bahz narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr – Bahz said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr – from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah gave a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was at Qudayd, and he was in iḥrām, the rump of a donkey, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned it, dripping with blood.
items.ma-3169: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he spent the night at the house of his maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Prophet ﷺ came after the last ʿishāʾ, and prayed four [rakʿahs], then slept, then rose, and said: “Has the boy slept?” – or a word like it. He said: Then he stood to pray, and I stood on his left, and he took me and placed me on his right, then prayed five, then slept until I heard his snoring – or his khaṭīṭ –, then went out and prayed.
items.ma-3170: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night at my maternal aunt Maymūnah's, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿishāʾ, then came and prayed four [rakʿahs], then slept, then rose and prayed four, and said: “Has the little boy slept?” – or a word like it. He said: So I came and stood on his left, and he placed me on his right, then he prayed five rakʿahs, then two rakʿahs, then slept until I heard his snoring – or his khaṭīṭ –, then went out to the prayer.
items.ma-3171: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “I was given victory by the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind.”
items.ma-3172: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Rawḥ narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam – Rawḥ said: Al-Ḥakam narrated to us – from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “This is an ʿumrah by which we have enjoyed [the benefit]. So whoever does not have a hady with him, let him leave iḥrām completely. For the ʿumrah has entered into the Ḥajj until the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-3173: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī al-Ṭāʾī, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the sale of date-palms, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of date-palms until one eats from it, or it is eaten from, and until it is weighed. He said: So I said: What is weighed? A man who was with him said: Until it is estimated.
items.ma-3174: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was praying, and a kid began to want to pass in front of the Prophet ﷺ, so he began to step forward and step back – Ḥajjāj said: guarding against it and stepping back – until the kid leapt.
items.ma-3175: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam narrated to me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿishāʾ, then came and prayed four [rakʿahs], then said: “Has the little boy – or the boy – slept?” – Shuʿbah said: or something like this – He said: Then he slept. He said: Then he rose and performed wuḍūʾ? He said: I do not remember his wuḍūʾ. He said: Then he rose and prayed, and I stood on his left. He said: So he placed me on his right, then prayed five rakʿahs. He said: Then he prayed two rakʿahs. He said: Then he slept until I heard his snoring – or his khaṭīṭ –, then prayed two rakʿahs, then went out to the prayer.
items.ma-3176: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in Ramaḍān while he was going to raid Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted until he reached Qudayd, then called for a cup of milk and drank it. He said: Then his Companions broke their fast until they reached Makkah.
items.ma-3177: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, he said: I heard Qatādah narrating, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-3178: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to me, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrating, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-3179:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, he said: The cousin of your Prophet ﷺ narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ said: It is not fitting for a servant to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā” – and he attributed him to his father.
He said: And he mentioned that he was taken on a night journey, and that he saw Mūsā ﵇, tawny, tall, as though he were of the men of Shanūʾah; and he mentioned that he saw ʿĪsā of medium build, [inclining] to redness and whiteness, curly-haired; and he mentioned that he saw the Dajjāl, and Mālik, the keeper of the Fire.
items.ma-3180:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, he said: The cousin of your Prophet ﷺ narrated to us, he said: “It is not fitting for a servant to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā” – and he attributed him to his father.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned, when he was taken on a night journey, and said: “Mūsā: tawny, tall, as though he were of the men of Shanūʾah,” and said: “ʿĪsā: curly-haired, of medium build.” And he mentioned Mālik, the keeper of Jahannam, and he mentioned the Dajjāl.
items.ma-3181: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, he said: A man of Banū al-Hujaym said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What is this fatwā that has penetrated – or has branched out among – the people: that whoever performs ṭawāf of the House has left iḥrām? He said: The sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, even if you resent it.
items.ma-3182:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, that Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj said: A man of Banū al-Hujaym, who was called so-and-so ibn Bujayl, said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What is this fatwā that has penetrated the people: whoever performs ṭawāf of the House has left iḥrām? He said: The sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, even if you resent it.
Shuʿbah said: I say: shaghabat – and I do not know how it is.
items.ma-3183:
Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
And he said: It has spread among the people.
items.ma-3184: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying at Minā, and I was on a donkey, so I left it in front of the row, and entered the prayer; and I was close to puberty, and he did not find fault with that.
items.ma-3185: And I read this ḥadīth to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He said: I came riding upon a she-donkey, and I was at that time close to puberty, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer, so I passed in front of part of the row, and dismounted and let the she-donkey go, and entered the row, and no one objected to that against me.
items.ma-3186: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ drank from Zamzam while standing.
items.ma-3187: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, he said: Abū Zumayl narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, he said: When the Ḥarūriyyah came out, they withdrew, and I said to them: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, made peace with the polytheists, and said to ʿAlī: “Write, O ʿAlī: This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, has made peace upon.” They said: If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you! So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Erase, O ʿAlī. O Allah, You know that I am Your Messenger. Erase, O ʿAlī, and write: This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh has made peace upon.” By Allah, the Messenger of Allah is better than ʿAlī, and he erased himself; and his erasing of that was not such that he was erased from prophethood. Have I come out of this? They said: Yes.
items.ma-3188: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās wrote to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If the people were given according to their claims, [some] people would claim the blood of [other] people and their wealth; but the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.”
items.ma-3189: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Arqam ibn Shuraḥbīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and did not make a bequest.
items.ma-3190: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a bowl of tharīd was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Eat from around it, and do not eat from its middle, for the blessing comes down in its middle.” Ibn Jaʿfar said: from its sides, or from its two edges.
items.ma-3191: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwānah, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾishah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it} [al-Qiyāmah: 16], he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to endure intensity from the revelation, and he used to move his lips – he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: I move my lips as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to move them. And Saʿīd said to me: I move them as I saw Ibn ʿAbbās move his lips – so Allah ﷿ revealed: {Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation}. He said: Its collection in your chest, then you recite it: {So when We have recited it, follow its recitation}, so listen to it and be silent: {Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification}. After that, when Jibrīl departed, he would recite it as he had made him recite it.
items.ma-3192: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us ahead – the little boys of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib – upon our donkeys on the night of al-Muzdalifah, and he began to pat our thighs and say: “My little sons, do not stone the jamrah until the sun rises.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not think that anyone stones until the sun rises.
items.ma-3193: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah, from al-Ḥasan – meaning al-ʿUranī –, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a kid fell in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying, and he did not cut off his prayer.
items.ma-3194:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night at my maternal aunt Maymūnah's, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the night, and went to his need, then washed his face and his hands, then rose and went to the waterskin and released its tie, then performed wuḍūʾ, a wuḍūʾ between the two wuḍūʾs: he did not use much, yet he made it thorough. Then he rose and prayed; so I rose and stretched, disliking that he should see that I had been watching him, and I performed wuḍūʾ. He stood praying, and I stood on his left, and he took me by my ear and turned me round to his right, and the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was completed at thirteen rakʿahs. Then he lay down and slept until he breathed heavily, and when he slept he would breathe heavily. Bilāl came to him and informed him of the prayer, and he stood and prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ. And he used to say in his supplication: “O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my sight, and light in my hearing, and light on my right, and light on my left, and light above me, and light beneath me, and light before me, and light behind me, and make light great for me.”
Kurayb said: And seven are in the tābūt. He said: I met some of the children of al-ʿAbbās, and he narrated them to me, and he mentioned: my sinews, my flesh, my blood, my hair, and my skin. He said: And he mentioned two traits.
items.ma-3195: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb: that a woman lifted up a boy of hers and said: O Messenger of Allah, does this one have Ḥajj? He said: “Yes, and you have a reward.”
items.ma-3196: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.
items.ma-3197:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The whiteness of the armpits of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be seen when he prostrated.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I heard my father say: Shuʿbah used to look out for the people of ḥadīth, and one day he said: What has become of that handsome boy? Meaning Shabābah.
items.ma-3198: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Zayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Waʿlah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Any hide that is tanned has become pure.”
items.ma-3199: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronounced the talbiyah until he stoned the jamrah.
items.ma-3200: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, from Qays ibn Saʿd, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, he said: Najdah ibn ʿĀmir wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about things, and I was present with Ibn ʿAbbās when he read his letter and when he wrote his reply, and he wrote to him: You asked me … and he mentioned the ḥadīth. He said: And you asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kill any of the boys of the polytheists? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill any of them, and you, do not kill any of them, unless you know of them what al-Khaḍir knew of the boy when he killed him.
items.ma-3201: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come} was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ knew that his own self had been announced to him as dead; so it was said: {When the victory of Allah comes} – the whole sūrah.
items.ma-3202: Abū Aḥmad and Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman lifted up a boy of hers to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, does this one have Ḥajj? He said: “Yes, and you have a reward.”
items.ma-3203: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ sent ahead the weak of his family from Jamʿ, and said: “Do not stone the jamrah until the sun rises.”
items.ma-3204: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, both said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Ḥasan al-ʿUranī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When you stone the jamrah, everything has become lawful for you except women. He said: A man said: And perfume? – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: A man said to him: O Abū al-ʿAbbās – Ibn ʿAbbās said: As for me, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smearing his head with musk; is that perfume or not?
items.ma-3205: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed al-ʿAqīq as the mīqāt for the people of the east.
items.ma-3206: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, assumed iḥrām for Ḥajj, and marked his hady on the right side of the hump, and removed the blood from it, and garlanded it with two sandals.
items.ma-3207: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Two blessings in which many of the people are cheated: free time and health.”
items.ma-3208: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, he said: We tried to sight the new moon of Ramaḍān at Dhāt ʿIrq, and we sent a man to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he asked him, and he said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ extended it to its sighting.
items.ma-3209: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from Madinah fasting in the month of Ramaḍān, and when he reached Qudayd he broke his fast, and he remained not fasting until he entered Makkah.
items.ma-3210: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, the mawlā of al-Tawʾamah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that they disputed about the fasting of the Prophet ﷺ on the day of ʿArafah, so Umm al-Faḍl sent milk to the Prophet ﷺ, and he drank.
items.ma-3211: Wakīʿ and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ was cupped – Wakīʿ said: at al-Qāḥah – while he was fasting.
items.ma-3212: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ḥājib ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he heard it from al-Ḥakam ibn al-Aʿraj, he said: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās while he was using his cloak as a pillow at Zamzam, and I said: Tell me about ʿĀshūrāʾ, which day should I fast it? He said: When you see the new moon of Muḥarram, count, and enter the morning of the ninth fasting. He said: I said: Is it thus that Muḥammad ﵊ used to fast it? He said: Yes.
items.ma-3213: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr, a mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I remain until the next year, I will surely fast the ninth day.”
items.ma-3214: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not eat the food from its top, but eat from its sides, for the blessing comes down from its top.”
items.ma-3215: Wakīʿ and Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit; Ibn Jaʿfar said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take anything in which there is spirit as a target.”
items.ma-3216: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq, he said: Al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not take anything in which there is spirit as a target.” ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: He forbade that it be taken.
items.ma-3217: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Jābir, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ carried him and carried his brother, this one in front of him and this one behind him.
items.ma-3218: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that al-Ṣaʿb ibn Jaththāmah gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the rump of a donkey, dripping blood, while he was in iḥrām, and he returned it.
items.ma-3219: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Burqān narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, I heard it from him, he said: The lizard was mentioned in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and a man of those sitting with him said: It was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not declare it lawful and did not declare it forbidden. He said: Evil is what you say; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was only sent as one who declares lawful and one who declares forbidden. Umm Ḥufayd bint al-Ḥārith came visiting her sister Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, and with her was food containing lizard meat; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came after he had taken the evening drink, and it was brought near to him, and it was said to him: Indeed in it is lizard meat. So he withheld his hand, and those who were with him ate it; and had it been forbidden he would have forbidden them from it. And he said: “It is not in our land, and we find it repulsive.”
items.ma-3220: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This and this are equal” – he joined together his thumb and his little finger.
items.ma-3221: Wakīʿ and Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, both said: Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who takes back his gift is like the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-3222: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Mālik ibn Anas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ayyim has more right over herself than her walī, and the virgin is consulted about herself.” He said: “And her silence is her consent.”
items.ma-3223: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salamah, from ʿImrān Abū al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: Supplicate your Rabb for us, that al-Ṣafā become gold for us; and if it becomes gold, we will follow you, and we will know that what you said is as you said. So he asked his Rabb ﷿, and Jibrīl came to him and said: If you wish, this Ṣafā will become gold for them, and whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment with which I do not punish anyone of the worlds; and if you wish, we will open for them the doors of repentance. He said: “O my Rabb, no; rather open for them the doors of repentance.”
items.ma-3224: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: My sister vowed to perform Ḥajj, and she has died? He said: “Do you see: if she had owed a debt, would you pay it?” He said: Yes. He said: “Then Allah ﵎ is more deserving of fulfilment.”
items.ma-3225: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I attended the ʿĪd with the Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, and they began with the prayer before the khuṭbah.
items.ma-3226: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Prophet ﷺ went out on the day of an ʿĪd, and had it not been for my place with him, I would not have attended it, because of youth; and he came to the house of Kathīr ibn al-Ṣalt, and prayed two rakʿahs. He said: Then he gave a khuṭbah and commanded ṣadaqah. He said: And he did not mention an adhān, nor an iqāmah.
items.ma-3227: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed then gave a khuṭbah, and Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, on the ʿĪd, without adhān and without iqāmah.
items.ma-3228: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Sulaymān, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There are no days in which deeds are more excellent than these days.” It was said: Not even jihād in the way of Allah? He said: “Not even jihād in the way of Allah, except a man who goes out with himself and his wealth, and does not return with any of it.”
items.ma-3229: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, ʿAṭāʾ narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās – he said: And he did not hear it – he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent me in the last part of the night from Jamʿ with the baggage of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3230: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to me, that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr informed him, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him, he said: A man in iḥrām was coming with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he fell from above his mount, and his neck was broken, and he died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wash him with water and lote, and clothe him in his two garments, and do not cover his head, for he will come on the Day of Resurrection pronouncing the talbiyah.”
items.ma-3231: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to me, from Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “A woman is not to travel except with a dhū maḥram.” And a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I have enrolled in such-and-such a campaign, and my wife is going for Ḥajj. He said: “Then return, and perform Ḥajj with her.”
items.ma-3232: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār informed me, that he heard Abū Maʿbad, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informing from Ibn ʿAbbās; Rawḥ said: “Then perform Ḥajj with her.”
items.ma-3233: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, ʿIkrimah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām, and was cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3234: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: ʿAṭāʾ informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you eats, let him not wipe his hand with the napkin until he licks it or has it licked.”
items.ma-3235: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Qays, he said: Ṣāliḥ, the mawlā of al-Tawʾamah, narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the Ẓuhr and the ʿAṣr, and the Maghrib and the ʿIshāʾ, without rain and without travel. They said: O Abū ʿAbbās, what did he intend by that? He said: To give latitude to his ummah.
items.ma-3236: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit narrated to us, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he led them in prayer at an eclipse in eight rakʿahs: he recited, then bowed, then rose, then recited, then bowed, then rose, then recited, then bowed, then rose, then recited, then bowed, then rose, then prostrated. He said: And the other is like it.
items.ma-3237: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Qatādah narrated to us, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: Would that you married the daughter of Ḥamzah? He said: “Indeed she is the daughter of my brother by suckling.”
items.ma-3238: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Mālik informed us, he said: Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a woman of Khathʿam said: O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah in Ḥajj has overtaken her father, a very old man who cannot remain firm upon the saddle; may I perform Ḥajj on his behalf? He said: “Yes.”
items.ma-3239: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: He called his brother ʿUbayd Allāh on the day of ʿArafah to food; he said: I am fasting. He said: You are leaders who are followed; I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ call for a vessel of milk on this day, and he drank. And Yaḥyā once said: A household who are followed.
items.ma-3240: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿImrān Abū Bakr, he said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me: Shall I not show you a woman of the people of Paradise? He said: I said: Yes. He said: This black woman; she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I am struck down and become uncovered; so supplicate Allah for me. He said: “If you wish, be patient, and you will have Paradise; and if you wish, I will supplicate Allah for you that He grant you well-being.” She said: No, rather I will be patient; so supplicate Allah that I do not become uncovered – or: that it not be uncovered from me. He said: So he supplicated for her.
items.ma-3241: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Qatādah narrated to me, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās – Yaḥyā said: Shuʿbah used to raise it –: “The dog and the menstruating woman cut off the prayer.”
items.ma-3242:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: I was told, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of the bee, the ant, the shrike, and the hoopoe.
Yaḥyā said: And I saw in the book of Sufyān: from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abī Lubayd, from al-Zuhrī.
items.ma-3243: Yaḥyā narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the night, and released the waterskin, and performed wuḍūʾ, and stood to the prayer; so I rose and performed wuḍūʾ, and stood on his left, and he took me by my right [hand], and turned me and stood me on his right, and I prayed with him.
items.ma-3244: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Qatādah narrated to me. And Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū Ḥassān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then called for his camel, and marked the right side of its hump, and wiped the blood from it, and garlanded it with two sandals, then called for his mount; and when it stood up straight with him on al-Baydāʾ, he assumed ihlāl for Ḥajj.
items.ma-3245: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to relieve himself, then food was brought to him, and he ate it, and he did not touch water.
items.ma-3246: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Umm Ḥufayd, the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās, presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ghee, dried curd and lizards; and he ate the ghee and the dried curd, and left the lizards out of distaste, and it was eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and had it been forbidden, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3247: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ajlaḥ, he said: Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ, going back and forth with him in speech, and said: What Allah wills and you will. He said: “You have made me an equal to Allah! What Allah wills alone.”
items.ma-3248: Yaḥyā and Ismāʿīl narrated to us, in meaning, both said: ʿAwf narrated to us, Ziyād ibn Ḥuṣayn narrated to me, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from Ibn ʿAbbās – Yaḥyā said: ʿAwf did not know whether it was ʿAbd Allāh or al-Faḍl – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me on the morning of al-ʿAqabah, while he was standing upon his mount: “Bring, pick up for me.” So I picked up for him pebbles, which were pebbles of khadhf, and he placed them in his hand, and said: “With the like of these!” twice, and he said with his hand – Yaḥyā gestured that he raised it – and said: “Beware of extremism, for those before you were destroyed only by extremism in the religion.”
items.ma-3249: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ was turned toward the Kaʿbah, they said: O Messenger of Allah, what of those of our brothers who died before that, who died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis? So Allah ﷿ revealed: {And Allah would never let your īmān go to waste} [al-Baqarah: 143].
items.ma-3250:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb and Kathīr ibn Kathīr ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah – one of them adds to the other –, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās said: The first thing that women took was the girdle, from the side of the mother of Ismāʿīl; she took a girdle so as to efface her trace from Sārah … and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismāʿīl: had she left Zamzam – or he said: had she not scooped from the water – Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “So that found Umm Ismāʿīl, and she loved companionship; so they settled, and sent to their families, and they settled with them.” And he said in his ḥadīth: “Then she descended from al-Ṣafā, until when she reached the valley, she raised the edge of her garment, then ran as an exhausted person runs, until she had crossed the valley, then came to al-Marwah and stood upon it, and looked: does she see anyone? And she saw no one; and she did that seven times.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “So that is the running of the people between them.”
items.ma-3251: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: And ʿUthmān al-Jazarī informed me, that Miqsam, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying {And when those who disbelieve plot against you to confine you} [al-Anfāl: 30], he said: “Quraysh consulted one another one night in Makkah, and some of them said: When morning comes, confine him with fetters – they meant the Prophet ﷺ; and some of them said: Rather, kill him; and some of them said: Rather, expel him. So Allah ﷿ made His Prophet aware of that, and ʿAlī spent that night on the bed of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ went out until he reached the cave; and the polytheists spent the night guarding ʿAlī, thinking that he was the Prophet ﷺ. When morning came they rushed at him, and when they saw ʿAlī, Allah turned back their plot; and they said: Where is this companion of yours? He said: I do not know. So they followed his trail; and when they reached the mountain it became confused for them, and they climbed the mountain, and passed by the cave, and saw the spider's web upon its door, and said: Had he entered here, the spider's web would not be on its door. So he stayed in it three nights.”
items.ma-3252: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not fitting for anyone to say: I am better than Yūnus ibn Mattā” – he attributed him to his father – “he committed a sin, then his Rabb chose him.”
items.ma-3253: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of the Conquest: “Its fresh grass is not to be cut, its game is not to be startled, its thorny trees are not to be cut down, and its luqaṭah is not lawful except for one who announces it.” Al-ʿAbbās said: Except the idhkhir, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Except the idhkhir, for it is lawful.”
items.ma-3254: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās – he said: I know only that he raised the ḥadīth – he said: He used to command the killing of snakes, and say: “Whoever leaves them out of fear, or dread of retaliation, is not of us.” He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: The jānn is a transformation of the jinn, just as the apes of Banū Isrāʾīl were transformed.
items.ma-3255: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Mukhtār narrated to us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The snakes are a transformation of the jinn.”
items.ma-3256: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim informed me, from Ṭāwūs, he said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when Zayd ibn Thābit said to him: Are you giving the fatwā that a menstruating woman may depart before her last contact is with the House? He said: Yes. He said: Then do not give a fatwā on that. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: If not, then ask so-and-so the Anṣārī woman whether the Prophet ﷺ commanded her with that. So Zayd ibn Thābit went back to him laughing, and said: I think you have spoken the truth.
items.ma-3257: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥāḍir informed me, he said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked about the jar: may nabīdh be made in it? He said: Allah ﷿ and His Messenger forbade it. So the man went to Ibn ʿAbbās and mentioned to him what Ibn ʿUmar had said, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: He spoke truly. The man said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Which jar did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid? He said: Everything made of clay.
items.ma-3258: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ibn Shihāb informed me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he went out in the year of the Conquest in the month of Ramaḍān, and fasted, until he reached al-Kadīd and broke his fast.
items.ma-3259: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ informed me, he said: We attended with Ibn ʿAbbās the funeral of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, at Sarif, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: This is the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so when you lift her bier, do not jolt her with it and do not shake it, and be gentle, for he used to apportion [his time] to eight, and did not apportion to one. ʿAṭāʾ said: The one to whom he did not apportion was Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab.
items.ma-3260: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥuwayrith informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to relieve himself, and fulfilled his need in a secluded place, then came, and food was brought near to him, and he ate and did not touch water.
items.ma-3261:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: ʿAṭāʾ informed me: that Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās, died. He said: So I went with him to Sarif. He said: He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: The Mother of the Believers; do not jolt her, and do not shake [her]; be gentle, for the Prophet of Allah had nine women, and he used to apportion [his time] to eight, and did not apportion to the ninth. He meant Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy.
ʿAṭāʾ said: She was the last of them to die; she died in Madinah.
items.ma-3262:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, from Dhakwān, the mawlā of ʿĀʾishah: that he asked permission for Ibn ʿAbbās to enter upon ʿĀʾishah while she was dying, and with her was her brother's son ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and he said: This is Ibn ʿAbbās asking permission to come in to you, and he is among the best of your sons. She said: Leave me alone about Ibn ʿAbbās and his praise. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to her: He is a reciter of the Book of Allah, a jurist in the religion of Allah; so permit him, that he may greet you and bid you farewell. She said: Then give him permission if you wish.
He said: So he permitted him, and Ibn ʿAbbās entered, then greeted and sat, and said: Glad tidings, O Mother of the Believers! By Allah, there is nothing between you and the departure from you of all harm and weariness – or he said: sickness – and your meeting the loved ones, Muḥammad and his party – or he said: his Companions – except that your soul leave your body. She said: And also? Ibn ʿAbbās said: You were the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to him, and he loved only what is good; and Allah ﷿ sent down your exoneration from above seven heavens, so there is no mosque on the earth in which it is not recited, in the hours of the night and the hours of the day; and your necklace fell at al-Abwāʾ, and the Prophet ﷺ was detained at the halting place, and the people were with him in seeking it – or he said: in searching for it – until the people reached morning without water; so Allah ﷿ revealed: {then aim for clean earth} – the verse [al-Nisāʾ: 43, and al-Māʾidah: 6]; and in that was a concession for the people in general, because of you. By Allah, you are indeed blessed. She said: Leave me alone about this, O Ibn ʿAbbās; by Allah, I wish that I had been a thing discarded, forgotten.
items.ma-3263: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ṭāwūs, he said: The most knowledgeable of them informed me, he said: “But that he grant it to his brother is better for him than that he give him upon it a known kharj.”
items.ma-3264: Sufyān narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, he said: Najdah wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the killing of boys, and he wrote to him: You wrote asking me about the killing of boys, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not kill them, and you, do not kill them, unless you know of them the like of what the companion of Mūsā knew of the boy.
items.ma-3265: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ eight together and seven together. I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Why did he do that? He said: He wished not to cause hardship to his ummah.
items.ma-3266: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I came to him at ʿArafah and found him eating a pomegranate, and he said: Come near and eat; perhaps you are fasting? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fast it. And once he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fast this day.
items.ma-3267: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged the people of al-Ṭāʾif, he freed those of their slaves who came out to him.
items.ma-3268: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥumayd ibn ʿAlī al-ʿUqaylī informed us, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs when he travelled, and four when he stayed. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: So whoever prays four in travel is like one who prays two in residence. He said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: He did not shorten the prayer except once, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rakʿahs and the people prayed one rakʿah, one rakʿah.
items.ma-3269: Al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, that he heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab informing that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The likeness of one who gives ṣadaqah and then takes back his ṣadaqah is the likeness of the dog that vomits and then eats its vomit.”
items.ma-3270: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, then the qiblah was turned afterwards.
items.ma-3271: Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he rose in the night and used the siwāk, then prayed two rakʿahs, then slept, then rose, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, and prayed two rakʿahs, until he had prayed six, then prayed the Witr with three, and prayed two rakʿahs.
items.ma-3272: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, that he witnessed al-Naḍr ibn Anas narrating to Qatādah: that he witnessed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās giving fatwā to the people, and he did not mention the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his fatwā, until a man came and said: I am an Iraqi man, and I make these pictures? He said: Come near – twice or three times –: I heard Muḥammad ﷺ – or he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – say: “Whoever makes an image in the world will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with blowing the spirit into it, and he will not be able to blow.”
items.ma-3273: Zakariyyā ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he forbade the price of khamr, the mahr of a prostitute, and the price of a dog, and said: “When he comes to you seeking the price of a dog, fill his two palms with dust.”
items.ma-3274: Zakariyyā narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Qays ibn Ḥabtar, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah has made unlawful for you khamr, maysir, and kūbah,” and he said: “Every intoxicant is ḥarām.”
items.ma-3275: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ spoke to a man about something, and said: “Indeed, praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him and seek His help. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray, and whomever He leads astray, there is none to guide him. And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-3276:
Al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī narrated to us, Abū al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he spent the night with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ one night, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ rose in the night, and went out, and looked at the sky, then recited this verse which is in Āl ʿImrān: {Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth}, until he reached: {Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire} [Āl ʿImrān: 190 - 191]; then he returned to the house, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed, then lay down; then he returned again and looked at the sky, then recited this verse; then he returned, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed, then lay down; then he rose and went out and looked at the sky, then recited this verse; then he returned, used the siwāk and performed wuḍūʾ, then stood and prayed.
Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “In the rikāz is the khumus.”
items.ma-3277: Abū Aḥmad and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the shade of his room – Yaḥyā said: it had nearly shrunk away from him – and said to his Companions: “A man will come to you looking at you with the eye of a Shayṭān; so when you see him, do not speak to him.” Then a blue-eyed man came, and when the Prophet ﷺ saw him he called him and said: “For what do you revile me, you and your companions?” He said: Stay as you are until I bring them to you. He said: So he went and brought them, and they began to swear by Allah that they had not said it and had not done it; and Allah ﷿ revealed: {On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you} to the end of the verse [al-Mujādilah: 18].
items.ma-3278: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed me, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb informed me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited at the eclipse of the sun, and we did not hear a letter from him.
items.ma-3279: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted on the day of the conquest of Makkah until he reached Qudayd, then a cup of milk was brought, and he broke his fast and commanded the people to break their fast.
items.ma-3280: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʾammal informed me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a khuṭbah with his back to the Multazam.
items.ma-3281: Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Thawbān informed me, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Dīnār say: One who heard Ibn ʿAbbās informed me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The religion is sincere counsel.” They said: For whom? He said: “For Allah, and for His Messenger, and for the leaders of the believers.”
items.ma-3282: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3283: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married while he was in iḥrām.
items.ma-3284: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Khālid, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped and gave him his wage, and had it been forbidden, he would not have given it.
items.ma-3285: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Maṭar, from ʿAṭāʾ: that Ibn al-Zubayr prayed the Maghrib, and gave the salām at two rakʿahs, and rose to touch the Stone, and the people made tasbīḥ, and he said: What is the matter with you? He said: So he prayed what remained, and performed two prostrations. He said: It was mentioned to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: He did not turn aside from the sunnah of his Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-3286: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped, and gave the cupper his wage.
items.ma-3287: Yazīd – meaning Ibn Hārūn – narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr, and ate at her house a shoulder of meat, then went out to the prayer and did not renew wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3288: Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined the two prayers on a journey.
items.ma-3289: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he did not consider it right to alight at al-Abṭaḥ, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only stayed there on account of ʿĀʾishah.
items.ma-3290: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Dāwūd ibn Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned his daughter Zaynab to Abū al-ʿĀṣ, her husband, by her first marriage, after two years, and did not make a new dowry.
items.ma-3291: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Ḥumayd informed us, from al-Ḥasan, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās addressed the people at the end of Ramaḍān, and said: O people of al-Baṣrah, pay the zakāh of your fasting. He said: The people began to look at one another, and he said: Who is here of the people of Madinah? Stand up and teach your brothers, for they do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory the ṣadaqah of Ramaḍān: half a ṣāʿ of wheat, or a ṣāʿ of barley, or a ṣāʿ of dates, upon the slave and the free, the male and the female.
items.ma-3292: Yazīd narrated to us, Nāfiʿ informed us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās wrote to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made, and if the people were given according to their claims, people would claim much wealth and blood.”
items.ma-3293: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr informed us. And Muʿādh, he said: ʿImrān – meaning Ibn Ḥudayr – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, he said: A man stood up to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: The prayer! He was silent toward him; then he said: The prayer! He was silent toward him; then he said: The prayer! He said: Are you teaching us about the prayer?! We used to combine the two prayers with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – or in the time of the Messenger of Allah; Muʿādh said: in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-3294: Yazīd narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah informed us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I prayed behind an old man at al-Abṭaḥ, and he pronounced the takbīr twenty-two times; so I came to Ibn ʿAbbās and mentioned that to him, and he said: May you have no mother! That is the prayer of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
items.ma-3295: Yazīd narrated to us, Saʿīd informed us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, that ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās narrated to them, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a roasted shoulder, and ate from it, and ate his fill, then prayed, and did not perform wuḍūʾ because of that.
items.ma-3296: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Qāriẓ ibn Shaybah, from Abū Ghaṭafān, he said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās and found him performing wuḍūʾ; he rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose, then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Blow out the nose twice, thoroughly, or three times.”
items.ma-3297: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from one who heard Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give the woman and the slave from the spoils, less than what the army received.
items.ma-3298: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Minhāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no Muslim who visits his brother [in illness], entering upon him when his appointed term has not come, and says: I ask Allah, al-ʿAẓīm, Rabb of the Great ʿArsh, to cure so-and-so of his pain – seven times –, except that Allah ﷿ cures him of it.”
items.ma-3299: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad – meaning Ibn Isḥāq – informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and from al-Zuhrī, from Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, he said: Najdah al-Ḥarūrī wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about the killing of boys, and whether the women used to attend the war with the Prophet ﷺ, and whether he used to allot them a share. Yazīd ibn Hurmuz said: And I wrote the letter of Ibn ʿAbbās to Najdah; he wrote to him: You wrote asking me about the killing of boys, and you say: The knowledgeable one, the companion of Mūsā, killed the boy! So if you knew of the boys what that knowledgeable one used to know, you would kill; but you do not know, so avoid them, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing them. And you wrote asking me about the women, whether they used to attend the war with the Prophet ﷺ, and whether he used to allot them a share; they used to attend with the Prophet ﷺ, but as for allotting them a share, he did not do so, and he used to give them a small gift.
items.ma-3300: Yazīd narrated to us, Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān informed us, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās: that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he forbade the gourd, the ḥantam, the pitch-coated vessel, and the naqīr; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, refrain from it} [al-Ḥashr: 7].
items.ma-3301: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Sufyān – meaning Ibn Ḥusayn – informed us, from Abū Hāshim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night at my maternal aunt Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith's, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿishāʾ, then returned to her, and it was her night, and prayed two rakʿahs, then turned away, and said: “Has the boy slept?” and I was listening to him. He said: And I heard him say in his place of prayer: “O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and light in my tongue, and make light great for me.”
items.ma-3302: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān – meaning Ibn Ḥusayn – informed us, from Abū Bishr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that Ḍubāʿah bint al-Zubayr wanted Ḥajj, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “Stipulate at your iḥrām: My place of release is where you detain me; for that is yours.”
items.ma-3303: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Sinān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, is Ḥajj once, or every year? He said: “No, rather once; and whoever adds, it is voluntary.”
items.ma-3304: Yazīd narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb. And Rawḥ, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him with his family to Minā on the night of al-Naḥr, and we stoned the jamrah at dawn.
items.ma-3305: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās saw a man prostrating, having spread out his forearms, and Ibn ʿAbbās said: Thus a dog squats. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he prostrated, I saw the whiteness of his armpits.
items.ma-3306: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us. And Ḥammād, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, in meaning, from Shuʿbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I and al-Faḍl came upon a donkey, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer – al-Khayyāṭ, meaning Ḥammād, said: in an open space of the ground – and we passed in front of him, while we were on it, until we had passed most of the row, and he did not forbid us and did not turn us back.
items.ma-3307: Yazīd narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās visiting him in an illness he had, and saw on him a garment of brocade, and before him a brazier on which were figures. He said to him: O Abū ʿAbbās, what is this garment you are wearing? He said: And what is it? He said: Brocade. He said: By Allah, I did not know of it, and I do not think that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it except because of haughtiness and arrogance, and we, praise be to Allah, are not like that. He said: Then what is this brazier on which are the images? Ibn ʿAbbās said: Do you not see how we burned them with fire?!
items.ma-3308: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the mawlā of Banū Ṭalḥah, from Kurayb, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, that Ibn ʿAbbās said: The name of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith was Barrah, and the Prophet ﷺ changed her name and named her Juwayriyah. The Prophet ﷺ passed by her, and she was in her place of prayer, glorifying Allah and supplicating Him, and he went off for his need, then returned to her after the day had risen, and said: “O Juwayriyah, are you still in your place?!” She said: I am still in this place of mine. The Prophet ﷺ said: “I have spoken four words, I count them three times, which are more excellent than what you said: Glory be to Allah by the number of His creation; and Glory be to Allah, Riḍā Nafsihi; and Glory be to Allah, the weight of His ʿArsh; and Glory be to Allah, the ink of His Kalimāt; and praise be to Allah, the like of that.”
items.ma-3309: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ departed from ʿArafāt, the people hurried, so the Prophet ﷺ commanded a caller, who called: “O people, righteousness is not in the hurrying of the horses and the riding-camels.” And I did not see her raising her foreleg, running.
items.ma-3310: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad – meaning Ibn Isḥāq – said: One who heard ʿIkrimah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The one who captured al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was Abū al-Yasar ibn ʿAmr, who is Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr, one of Banū Salimah; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “How did you capture him, O Abū al-Yasar?” He said: A man helped me against him, whom I never saw before or after; his appearance was thus, his appearance was thus. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A noble angel helped you against him.” And he said to al-ʿAbbās: “O ʿAbbās, ransom yourself, and your brother's son ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, and Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith, and your ally ʿUtbah ibn Jaḥdam” – one of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Fihr –. He said: But he refused, and said: I was a Muslim before that, and they only compelled me. He said: “Allah knows best about your affair; if what you claim is true, Allah will reward you for that; but as for the outward of your affair, it was against us; so ransom yourself.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taken from him twenty ūqiyyahs of gold, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, count it for me against my ransom. He said: “No; that is something Allah gave us from you.” He said: But I have no wealth. He said: “Then where is the wealth that you put down in Makkah, when you went out, with Umm al-Faḍl, when there was no one with you two other than you two, and you said: If I am afflicted in this journey of mine, then for al-Faḍl so much, and for Quthama so much, and for ʿAbd Allāh so much?” He said: By Him who sent you with the truth, no one of the people knew this except me and her, and I know that you are the Messenger of Allah.
items.ma-3311: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad – meaning Ibn Isḥāq – said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to me, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Men shaved their heads on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, and others shortened [their hair]; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on those who shave.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten? He said: “May Allah have mercy on those who shave.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten? He said: “May Allah have mercy on those who shave.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, and those who shorten? He said: “And those who shorten.” They said: Then what is it with those who shave, O Messenger of Allah, that you have doubled mercy upon them? He said: “They did not doubt.” He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed.
items.ma-3312: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gnawed a shoulder, then stood and prayed and did not perform wuḍūʾ.
items.ma-3313: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ: that he saw no harm in a man assuming iḥrām in a garment dyed with saffron that had been washed, in which there was no shaking-off and no staining.
items.ma-3314: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-2370:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: The son of Ibn Shihāb's brother narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Muḥammad ibn Muslim, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd informed me, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to Qayṣar inviting him to Islam, and sent his letter with Diḥyah al-Kalbī, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to hand it to the chief of Buṣrā, so that he would hand it to Qayṣar; and the chief of Buṣrā handed it to Qayṣar. Now Qayṣar, when Allah ﷿ had removed from him the armies of Fāris, walked from Ḥimṣ to Īlīyāʾ on carpets that were spread for him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: When the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Qayṣar, he said, when he read it: Seek for me someone from his people whom I may ask about the Messenger of Allah. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb informed me that he was in al-Shām with men of Quraysh who had come as merchants, and that was during the truce that was between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the disbelievers of Quraysh. Abū Sufyān said: The messenger of Qayṣar came to me and took me and my companions until we reached Īlīyāʾ, and we were brought in to him, and behold, he was sitting in his royal assembly, with the crown upon him, and around him were the great men of the Romans. He said to his interpreter: Ask them which of them is nearest in lineage to this man who claims that he is a prophet. Abū Sufyān said: I am the nearest of them to him in lineage. He said: What is your kinship to him? He said: I said: He is the son of my paternal uncle. Abū Sufyān said: And there was no man of Banū ʿAbd Manāf in the company that day other than me. He said: Qayṣar said: Bring him near to me. Then he commanded concerning my companions, and they were placed behind my back, at my shoulder. Then he said to his interpreter: Say to his companions: I am asking this one about this man who claims that he is a prophet; if he lies, then call him a liar. Abū Sufyān said: By Allah, had it not been for shame on that day that my companions would relate lying from me, I would have lied about him when he asked me; but I was ashamed that they would relate lying from me, so I told the truth about him. Then he said to his interpreter: Say to him: How is the lineage of this man among you? He said: I said: He is among us a man of lineage. He said: Has anyone among you ever said this saying before him? He said: I said: No. He said: Did you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said? He said: I said: No. He said: Was there any king among his forefathers? He said: I said: No. He said: Do the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak ones? He said: I said: Rather their weak ones. He said: Are they increasing or decreasing? He said: I said: Rather they are increasing. He said: Does anyone turn back from his religion out of discontent with it after entering it? He said: I said: No. He said: Does he betray? He said: I said: No, and we are now in a truce with him, and we fear that. Abū Sufyān said: And no word was possible for me, into which I could put anything to belittle him, other than that one, [and] I did not fear that it would be related from me. He said: Did you fight him, or did he fight you? He said: I said: Yes. He said: How was your war and his war? He said: I said: It was turns in alternation: we are given the upper hand over him one time, and he is given the upper hand over us another. He said: What does he command you? He said: I said: He commands us to worship Allah alone and not to associate anything with Him, and forbids us what our fathers used to worship, and commands us with prayer, truthfulness, chastity, fulfilling the covenant, and returning the trust. He said: Then he said to his interpreter when I said that to him: Say to him: I asked you about his lineage among you, and you claimed that he is among you a man of lineage; and likewise the messengers are sent from the lineage of their people. And I asked you: Has anyone among you ever said this saying before him? and you claimed that none has; so I said: If anyone among you had said this saying before him, I would have said: A man following a saying that was said before him. And I asked you: Did you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said? and you claimed that you did not; so I know that he would not leave lying about people and then lie about Allah ﷿. And I asked you: Was there any king among his forefathers? and you claimed that there was not; so I said: If there had been a king among his forefathers, I would have said: A man seeking the kingdom of his forefathers. And I asked you: Do the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak ones? and you claimed that their weak ones have followed him, and they are the followers of the messengers. And I asked you: Are they increasing or decreasing? and you claimed that they are increasing, and likewise is īmān until it is complete. And I asked you: Does anyone turn back from his religion out of discontent with it after entering it? and you claimed that none does, and likewise is īmān when it mixes with the joy of the hearts: no one is discontent with it. And I asked you: Does he betray? and you claimed that he does not, and likewise the messengers. And I asked you: Did you fight him and did he fight you? and you claimed that he has done so, and that your war and his war is in turns: the upper hand is given over you one time, and you are given the upper hand over him another; and likewise the messengers are afflicted, and the final outcome is theirs.
And I asked you: What does he command you? and you claimed that he commands you to worship Allah ﷿ alone, associating nothing with Him, and forbids you what your forefathers used to worship, and commands you with truthfulness, prayer, chastity, fulfilling the covenant, and returning the trust; and this is the description of a prophet whom I knew was coming forth, but I did not think that he would be from among you. If what you have said about him is true, he will soon possess the place of these two feet of mine. By Allah, if I hoped to reach him, I would take on the hardship of meeting him, and if I were with him, I would wash his feet. Abū Sufyān said: Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and commanded concerning it, and it was read, and behold, in it: “In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. From Muḥammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Hiraql, the chief of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe; accept Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arīsiyyīn – meaning the farmers – and {O People of the Book, come to a word that is equal between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as masters besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 64].” Abū Sufyān said: When he finished his speech, the voices of those around him of the great men of the Romans rose, and their clamor increased, and I do not know what they said; and he commanded concerning us, and we were taken out. Abū Sufyān said: When I went out with my companions and was alone with them, I said to them: The affair of the son of Abū Kabshah has grown great; this is the king of Banū al-Aṣfar, he fears him. Abū Sufyān said: By Allah, I did not cease to be humbled, certain that his affair would prevail, until Allah put Islam into my heart while I disliked it.
